Dropped in here to check it out, and we're glad we did. They've been open 3 weeks now, and Peter G.'s extensive experience in the restaurant business shows. No startup glitches, they were running great without hiccups.

The first impression is the restaurant is inviting and comfortable. The second impression is a friendly greeting and Peter Ginapolis,  the owner,  is working the front, introduces himself to us, and takes us to our table. He came back a couple more times to make sure everything was to our liking, and even took me outside to meet his chefs who were working the smoker.

The quality of the ingredients is evident- everything was fresh and prepared technically well, seasoning and flavor profiles were just right. While we were eating, a table of six ladies came in and all ordered the salmon special. One of the chefs, Tony, came out and sat with them for a minute. Turns out one of the ladies was his mother! He asked if we were enjoying ourselves and was dessert in the picture? He said the bread pudding was particularly good. Bread pudding is my favorite!!! Tony called our server over, asked to put a bread pudding on his tab and he went back into the kitchen to make it his special way. Delicious!!!! On top of this, apparently his mom's group had ordered an extra special which he wrapped up and insisted that we take home!

We are definitely coming back again!!!!!

I had the brisket plate, and it was some of the better brisket I've had in the Midwest - beefy, tender, and great smoke flavor with a nice dark bark and pink smoke ring.  I typically judge a BBQ place on their brisket, and they do not disappoint in the least.

Another point in which I judge a good BBQ place on is their sides, or as they call them "flavors".  And it's another area in which they do not disappoint at all.  I tried the fried pickles and peppers, coleslaw and mashed potatoes with corn and BBQ gravy.  The fried pickles and peppers were great and surprisingly light.  The coleslaw was different than I've typically had, but very good.  The mashed potatoes and gravy steal the show however - mashed potatoes + sweet corn + gravy = winner!

Food: My wife and I split the brisket, beef rib and hot links sampler, and added the burnt ends on in addition. We also got the homemade applesauce and baked beans. To start, every meat was fall apart and very flavorful. The standouts were the ribs and the hot links. My wife does not like hot links at all, and even she said they were the best thing of the whole meal. Blown away! The ribs were second best, and while they pulled away clean, they were not mush. The sauces were some of the most creative I’ve seen at a BBQ joint. Razberry, Cola, Chipotle Honey, Habanero were just some of their options. All very different, but good in their own way. Portion size was good, and price was very reasonable. Cocktails were good also, but standard fair. On the down side, beans were just ok, and burn ends could have been better (however this could be on us, as we opted for no sauce and add our own. They probably would have been better glazed.)

Atmosphere: Huge space, that really opens up compared to the front view. A bit loud, but great place for a lot of people.

Service: Service was good, however my only critique would be to advise that the tables near the door are usable (we were waiting, and not told we could just sit at the front tables and order from the bar.) Otherwise, quick service and very kind.

Bob’s Bitchin BBQ  is a local gem, boasting boatloads of BBQ and a variety of homemade sauces.

Food: My wife and I split the brisket, beef rib and hot links sampler, and added the burnt ends on in addition. We also got the homemade applesauce and baked beans. To start, every meat was fall apart and very flavorful. The standouts were the ribs and the hot links. My wife does not like hot links at all, and even she said they were the best thing of the whole meal. Blown away! The ribs were second best, and while they pulled away clean, they were not mush. The sauces were some of the most creative I’ve seen at a BBQ joint. Razberry, Cola, Chipotle Honey, Habanero were just some of their options. All very different, but good in their own way. Portion size was good, and price was very reasonable. Cocktails were good also, but standard fair. On the down side, beans were just ok, and burn ends could have been better (however this could be on us, as we opted for no sauce and add our own. They probably would have been better glazed.)

Atmosphere: Huge space, that really opens up compared to the front view. A bit loud, but great place for a lot of people.

Service: Service was good, however my only critique would be to advise that the tables near the door are usable (we were waiting, and not told we could just sit at the front tables and order from the bar.) Otherwise, quick service and very kind.

My score: 9/10. We were pretty blown away by this place. We only go that way 2 times a year, but we will be back again for sure! Great price, some of the best ribs and hot links we’ve had, and love the large amount of sauces to try.

I’m an avid greens fan and I couldn’t even eat more then a couple bites of the greens, it’s not like they weren’t cooked down right or not scrubbed they had an overbearing amount of sodium in them. You could tell they had good flavoring in there but it all was masked by heavy duty sodium. The same for the bbq beans as well to much sodium, great flavor ruined by excessive amount of salt and some of the beans were not cooked throughly but I can get over that. I think they tried to step outside the box with the Mac and cheese but in my opinion penne noodles have no place in Mac and cheese. If they stepped out the box and tried shells I could see that but penne no no no. All in all great meats and very unique bbq sauce but my favorite sides were a let down. I plan to come back and try them again in high hopes that whoever was in the kitchen that day had a heavy hand with the salt.

Update! Decided to give them a whirl again and to my surprise it was amazing! Like I previously said before the meat is amazing, ordered the brisket and asked for ends and it was absolutely delicious! Cooked to perfection moist and flavorful. The sauce was very good, little on the sweeter side but still delectable. Now for the sides! Went with the green again and red beans and rice. The greens were cooked perfect great flavor and best of all didn’t taste like pure salt. The red beans and rice were spot on and hell of a lot less salt this time, still I little bit more then I personally like but do able. All in all I’m so happy I stopped back to give them a second shot. Mission bbq has been my go to because they are closer but I think im going to be driving the few extra miles for now on. Mission is good but does not compare to SHARKS brisket period.

After seeing Oak+Swine on the "Instagram-Worthy" episode of "Chicago's Best", we were VERY intrigued. Featured in their segment was the "Animal Frites" appetizer, and the owner said something along the lines of, "you begin enjoying your meal through its presentation". The presentation of this appetizer looked delectable, hence being on the "Instagram-Worthy" episode.

We called in a carryout order:
Animal Frites
Frito Pie
The Rodney
The Gobbler

Even being a carryout order, the dishes were meticulously assembled in a visually appealing display; their presentation was "as seen on TV". Definitely met our expectations.

As for the flavor of our food... Let's just say that I haven't been this impressed by a meal in a really long time! Every single bite was savory and packed with flavor. Again, this was a carryout order; I would imagine that the food tastes even better when dining at the restaurant! Our expectations definitely exceeded.

One final note about their service: When phoning my order in, despite having a full house (patrons were audible in the background, and there were many dining in when I picked up), the person taking my order was extremely friendly; our food was ready as promised after 30-35 minutes; and, at pick-up, multiple employees checked in with me to make sure I was taken care of.

Bravo, Oak+Swine! Bravo!

Today was my first experience at Chicago Culinary Kitchen and the reviews cannot justify how good the food actually is here.  Everything was cooked to perfection.  We tried as much as we could within reason.  Brisket(leaner cut), spare ribs, esquites, beans, pig candy(candied bacon), and the bread pudding.

The brisket was cooked perfectly and the cut was just what we asked for,  minimal fat. It was super tender and juicy,  no knife required.   The spare ribs were without a doubt the best ribs I've had to date.   Great bark on it,  extremely tender but still enough bite to remain on the bone.   The smoke really permeated the meat and creates a fantastic flavor profile.   Both the brisket and ribs are great with or without barbecue sauce.   If you're a purist the meat comes without sauce so don't worry.   The barbeque sauce itself is a perfect compliment to the flavor of the meat.   It is a little sweet yet tangy and any left over on your tray is easily soaked up with the white bread accompanying your meal.

The beans were done exquisitely,  a little sweet and smokey.  The beans were still a bit firm so it doesn't just turn into a mole like some places and there is meat cooked in making them nice and hearty.  The pig candy was comparable to Au cheval in the city albeit a thinner cut of bacon but just as delicious.  It was my first time trying esquites and I was far from disappointed.  They retained the corn flavor quite well while also complimenting it with the cream and spices, it kept me coming back for bite after bite.

To finish things off we had the bread pudding.   Sometimes I am weary to try bread pudding at places because it can be very hit or miss.   They hit it out of the park!  It was sweet but not over powering in that department.   The fireball caramel sauce on top was a perfect pair.   It was reminiscent of going to get a fresh baked cinnamon roll.   All in all every single thing was cooked perfectly and I would eat it all again and again.   Next time I plan to try other items on the menu because I'm certain they will be just as phenomenal.

The ambiance and staff were just as good as the food.   The communal dining is actually very inviting and the decor is all their own in styling.  The staff was all very nice and engaging.  They are obviously a very busy restaurant, but they all made sure anything a customer needed was taken care of.

5/5 would come again and recommend the restuarant to anyone including random strangers.

Also the house pickles were refreshing and tart, good for between meats to cleanse the palate. I got the two meat option with sliced brisket and pulled pork, combined with coleslaw and truffle Mac and cheese plus a slice of Texas toast. The brisket had a nicely developed smoke ring, wasn't dry and had good flavor, the pork was similar. The truffle Mac and cheese was thick and creamy with cheese and the crust on top was a good textural addition. They have four sauces available to add to the meat but it didn't really need it, however the tropical chipotle I believe it was, was my favorite. Overall I'd have to say BBQ supply was a refreshing take on BBQ in Chicago, I'd definitely come back.

Cork town (where the restaraunt located) is pretty easy to get to off of I-75 just south of the down town area of Detroit, but the parking seemed to all be street parking. No big deal to us. We had to walk about 4 minutes to get there.

We got there a little before the peak time on a Friday and didn't have to wait, and it didn't seem like anyone else had to wait for tables either while we ate.

Our waiter, Zach, was fantastic! He was very friendly and personable, even cracking a few jokes with us throughout our time there. He was eager to help, was on top of our waters, and knowledgeablely answered and directed us with all our questions.

The food was very good. We got vegetarian dishes (The Genius, Hoppin' Jack, Mac & Cheese, and Sweet Potato Mash) and were not disappointed. Their mac & cheese is exceptionally good, and my wife especially loved the sweet potato mash. All of the 5 sauces were good, though my ended up preferring the NC on the hoppin jack and apple on the genius, and I preferred the spicey on both, but did enjoy trying all the flavors.

The pricing of food was reasonable and you could get out of there for $10-18 a person easily if you wanted, or spend a little more if you want something like ribs.

At the end of our meal we asked about bringing people and their dogs from our dog training club to the patio for dinner and Zach explained that they have dog nights and that dogs are definitely welcome, just that it would be probably be a good idea to email the manager if we wanted to know more and coordinate a large group going. I would recommend contacting them first even if only trying to bring your own dog.

Finally, the to go packaging was entirely recyclable or compostable! We were pleased to see Slow's doing this to support the environment.

Would definitely recommend going here, just be ready to street park and walk a short way there.

When I travel, I love interacting with people. They can steer you to the best places in their states, towns or cities. While at the Chazen Museum of Art, I spoke to a security guard about a place that serves good barbeque. I told him that I was from Kansas and we know “Q”. Immediately he suggested Bob’s Bitchin’ Barbeque. With a name like that, I had to check it out.
Located in a small downtown area, the 1905 building had been home to a couple of hardware stores and used as a billiard hall.
Bob’s serves their meat hickory wood smoked in-house dry and seasoned. It can be served “wet” allowing the sauce to caramelize over heat or “dry” to allow you to sample the eight different sauces that you’ll find at your table.
Under the dinner section of the menu I ordered the Sampler platter; 1/3 rack of ribs, pulled pork and a pork chop that’s brined and hickory smoked that gives a ham taste. I had a choice of two made from scratch sides; coleslaw and baked beans. It also comes with a side of corn bread.
The taste was incredible as the meat fell off the bones with every bite. I’m serious. Those ribs were so good I would slap someone if they tried to take my food away! My favorite sauces were as follows:
Original, which has a hickory smoked flavor.
RBQ, “Sweet with a little fizz with Sprecher’s Root Beer.”
Mango Red Pepper, “Sweet with heat.”
I enjoyed the coleslaw with a kick of sweetness and the cornbread was moist and tasty.
Bob’s bragging rights are that in 2015, his Carolina sauce won 1st place in the Mustard division of the American Royal World Series of Barbecue Sauce contest in Kansas City. In 2016, it brought home the bronze. And to think I had to travel to Dodgeville, WI to find all this out.
Overall: If this place was any closer, I would be a regular. In the meantime, I will make the trip again in the near future for those melt in your mouth ribs and sides.

I also got the spaghetti which is not just noodles and sauce - REAL spaghetti with plenty of ground hamburger in it and seasoned to perfection. The meal came with a slice of cornbread and that was great as well. We went back inside to compliment the food and she said her green beans were her best side dish and gave a free sample (also generous portion) and they were in fact damn delicious! 😋 I highly recommend this place. If you're local to Kalamazoo and have never gone- you MUST go! I would classify this spot as a hidden gem and I must try for anyone looking for comforting, delicious soul food goodness! I will be making a trip in the near future.

So... Let me start with service... Top notch. These guys and gals(super cute too) waited on me hand a foot. Second, food... Um... Hell's Yessss! Did the three meat platter. Enjoyed the brisket, perfectly smoked, great flavor, tender, but took a little tug to pull it apart. Perfect. Next up - Burnt ends(my favorite smoked meat) and tgey didnt disappoint. They were fabulous! I dont say that about burnt ends often, but these were the real deal! Third meat was the pulled pork. Well smoked, beautiful, flavorful bark, although not enough of it. Expected good things here because of the rating, but DID NOT expect to be this impressed. As a smoker, and a father who is a master smoker, Bombers are getting it right. Oh yeah, sauces and craft beers. They have something for everyone. Sauces from Carolina's, to their Bombers sauce, to Kansas City sweet, to Atomic for the daring, to melt your face off Nuclear for the insane... A little bit of everything. Seemed they made a St. Louis sauce to mimic the STL icon, Maul's. Not my favorite, but good. Im like the heat of the Atomic, but Nuclear was great too. Nuclear has a building heat with nice flavor, a little goes a long way. Got extra Nuclear to go though...

Like it hot? Bombers Verbal warning when handing me the Nuclear - "Get this on your skin, it may burn you. Get this in your eye, you may go blind. Eat too much of this, you may bleed internally..." Consider yourself warned...

I happened to eat here a week ago on kind of a whim, while heading to another restaurant. In passing it by, my wife and I got curious and decided to try it out. This place is great. While we've only been here for lunch, both times have been worth it.

The location is laid out much like a more spacious version of an Outback Steakhouse or a Texas Roadhouse. It's pretty much all wood, with a beautifully designed bar serving as sort of the centerpiece for the restaurant. The place is clean and, while large, inviting.

The service has been good both times. Our server approached us within minutes of being seated (often by the same person), and orders came out promptly.

The food, I really cannot wait to explain.

The first time, we decided to split a full rack of ribs, and split an appetizer of three street tacos. You get three choices of taco: steak, brisket, and pulled pork. The steak tacos are nothing too special, the brisket tacos are very tasty and tender, and the pulled pork tacos... they redefine expectations of what a taco should taste like. I still cannot forget the flavor packed into this combination of pulled pork, cabbage, salsa, and guacamole, all wrapped in a flour tortilla which is crispy on the outside and soft and warm on the inside. If they don't provide it, ask for a few slices of lime to sprinkle on top, you should not be disappointed. The full rack of ribs were equally delicious. I'm familiar with restaurant ribs having a pressure cooked, thin rack of ribs that have little flavor on their own, whose flavor is balanced with an overly sweet sauce to mask the quality. Smokey Bones, however, has a true smoked flavor in the meat, and the sauce does not try to mask any of that flavor; instead it complements it perfectly. For those who are more into sauce than the meat, there are a variety of sauces on the table to adjust it to your taste.

The second time we visited, we both went for the tacos, and split an order of onion rings. The tacos, I hope I've explained how delicious they are (go for all 3 pulled pork, you can get it for $9.99). The onion rings were perfectly cooked, with some type of batter that stayed crispy even after it cooled down, maintained its seasoning, and protected the onion from turning to mush. Onion rings from some restaurants always pull completely out of the batter when you take a bite, leaving you with too much onion and not enough batter the first bite, and vice versa the rest of the time. This was NOT the case here. From the first to the last, the flavor and texture was consistent. Furthermore, it had a light and crispy flavor to it, so even after several of them, we didn't feel heavy.

Lastly, they provide a method to pay for your meal at the table in case the server is running a little slow (even though ours was not). We tried it out the second time, and the convenience of just paying and leaving without the need to wait for the back and forth was a plus for the lunchtime rush. I would only recommend that the restaurant face the screen towards the table so people understand that this is an option -- it had to be explained to us the first time.

Overall, we have been twice very impressed with Smoke Bones, and will definitely be returning, hopefully very soon.

Iron Grate is a tucked-away spot in Cudahy boasting a real southern BBQ experience.

Food:  We split the 3 meat/3 side meal with a side of Burnt ends. Starting with the sides, the Mac and Cheese and cornbread were fine, but the standout was the baked beans. Highly recommend, as they see less barbecue like, and more like a thick, flavorful bean soup. Maybe less traditional, but very tasty.

When it comes to the meats, the hotlinks were a bit dry, and didn’t have the spice you might expect. The ribs were huge, but not your traditional cut. That said, it was almost like a meatier, tougher pork belly. Very tasty, but different. The brisket was on point, very soft and melts. All said, the all-star for my wife and I were the burnt ends. Melty bits of fat that paired perfectly with their sweeter hot sauce. Highly recommend.
Atmosphere: Odd, to be honest. The ordering line has a cafeteria vibe, however you get to see them prepare the food to order. The sitting area doesn’t seem to mesh with a barbeque joint, but the outside seating area would be perfect for the summer.

Service: Cashier was very helpful in ordering, and waiter we prompt and kind.

My score: 8/10. If I had to say one thing about Iron Grate, is it is a space that really does its own thing. Great barbeque, but may not touch to a true southerners roots the way that a down-home joint may. All said, the food was very good and would definitely recommend.

With my wife, adult daughter and adult son leading the way, we had lunch at The Prized Pig.  We were excited to dine here as we were semiregular customers of their location (now closed) in Niles.

The portions were generous, prepared to a tasteful degree and worth every penny.  I lived in Columbus, Georgia years ago and the sights and smells at The Prized Pig reminded me of some great smoked barbe-que from that region.

The rib tips my wife had were amazing and my beef platter was just a good as I remember.  The corn bread has that great "tacky" quality on top with a center that is not dry but not under baked either.  Just perfect.  The mac-n-cheese was prepared with some ham for flavor and the taste was spot-on; the texture is improved with a final bake to create a slightly crusty finish on top. Lastly, the baked beans are not my favorite, having been raised on Boston baked beans thanks to my mom and Grandpa; both natives to Massachusetts.  That said, the beans are flavorful with a great southern spicy kick.

Cannot recommend The Prized Pig any higher.  Well worth going to their new location.  I am very glad this eatery is back with an attitude!  Bring your appetite!

I come to Kalamazoo from Grand Rapids to handle business on the regular. Last week we were in town and I had the taste for some soul food. I decided to add an additional side dish for $2.99. My grand total was $13.00 and my meal fed two people with rib tips leftover for later. Worth every penny. Large portions, homemade goodness - you can't go wrong at this spot. Comfort food galore! Every single side dish was PIPING hot. The rib tips were on point! I wanted to try her cabbage so bad - but she only makes cabbage on Saturdays 😣😢😭. I went with the greens instead and I will say - they were some of the best greens I ever had in my life! Cooked to absolute perfection with just the right amount of crisp in each stem to let you know they're FRESH greens, NOT canned. I also got the spaghetti which is not just noodles and sauce - REAL spaghetti with plenty of ground hamburger in it and seasoned to perfection. The meal came with a slice of cornbread and that was great as well. We went back inside to compliment the food and she said her green beans were her best side dish and gave a free sample (also generous portion) and they were in fact damn delicious! 😋 I highly recommend this place. If you're local to Kalamazoo and have never gone- you MUST go! I would classify this spot as a hidden gem and I must try for anyone looking for comforting, delicious soul food goodness! I will be making a trip in the near future.

Heaven’s Table BBQ is a new BBQ restaurant in the new food hall on the east side of Milwaukee.

Food: We got the 4 meat platter (Sausage, rib tips, brisket and beef shoulder.) Our sides were coleslaw and baked beans. Going down the row, the sausage was very good tasting, but like many sausages at BBQ joints, it was dry. The rib tips were really good, but almost had that idea of oxtail, in that you are chewing the bits off the bone/cartilage. Might have been better to just get the rips outright. The brisket was my wife’s fav, and was very well done and juicy. The beef shoulder was much like a pulled beef, and was very juicy and good.

The sauces were ok, as 1 was really good, and one was WAY too sweet and ketchup-like. The slaw was not my cup of tea, as it was vary vinegary and simple. The beans however were some of the best I’d had in a while. Cornbread was good as well.

Atmosphere: This is a difficult item to rate, as the business is in the food hall. The Hall itself is nice, and  good place to go if people have different tastes in food.

Service: Our attendant was very nice, and food came out very promptly. It is more cafeteria style, so no real service except going to order.

Overall: 8/10. I would put this on the same list as Iron Grate BBQ. I couldn’t tell you which was better or worse, but I’d say very comparable. If you like BBQ, I’d definitely give it a shot.

Our waiter, Zach, was fantastic! He was very friendly and personable, even cracking a few jokes with us throughout our time there. He was eager to help, was on top of our waters, and knowledgeablely answered and directed us with all our questions.

The food was very good. We got vegetarian dishes (The Genius, Hoppin' Jack, Mac & Cheese, and Sweet Potato Mash) and were not disappointed. Their mac & cheese is exceptionally good, and my wife especially loved the sweet potato mash. All of the 5 sauces were good, though my ended up preferring the NC on the hoppin jack and apple on the genius, and I preferred the spicey on both, but did enjoy trying all the flavors.

The pricing of food was reasonable and you could get out of there for $10-18 a person easily if you wanted, or spend a little more if you want something like ribs.

At the end of our meal we asked about bringing people and their dogs from our dog training club to the patio for dinner and Zach explained that they have dog nights and that dogs are definitely welcome, just that it would be probably be a good idea to email the manager if we wanted to know more and coordinate a large group going. I would recommend contacting them first even if only trying to bring your own dog.

Finally, the to go packaging was entirely recyclable or compostable! We were pleased to see Slow's doing this to support the environment.

Would definitely recommend going here, just be ready to street park and walk a short way there.

We arrived shortly after 12:30, and event though this was but Station One's third day in business, the queue was not an issue.  Once we entered the establishment, the smell of smoked meats was intoxicating. As we waited in line, we reviewed the menu posted above the counter. The menu is not complicated, by any means: You can choose to have your meats by the half-pound, or in sandwich form. The menu board was clear and easy to understand.

I decided upon the pork belly, and my wife opted for the pulled pork. The pork was sliced and weighed out in open view, dripping with juices as they are placed on the paper-lined metal tray. From there, we asked for some Mac-N-Cheese and Elotes, which were served in paper trays. The metal and paper service complement the overall decor, which is industrial. As we collected, and paid for our food, the staff was very friendly, freely answering questions and even going so far as to provide some small samples of their cornbread and the broccoli slaw. After snagging some slices of white bread and spicy pickles, we made out way to our table.

Our food was everything we would want in barbecue: The meat was tender, smokey, and full of melt-in-your mouth flavor. The macaroni and cheese was creamy, using large-gauge pasta designed for holding sauce. Our elotes were hot, and in a flavorful melange of chili powder, cheese, and creamy sauce.

We did not have a chance to try the bar, but it looked cozy, and well-appointed with good quality liquors (and Malort). Perhaps next time :) Thanks, Station One, for providing another wonderful dining option in Plainfield!

I had high hopes for Smoked on High, as any good optimistic exiled Texan. We know that Ohio is not in any way known for its barbeque, but then neither is South Florida, and the longer we were exiled there, the more good barbeque started to pop up (Smoke BBQ AND Bare Bones!! Mmm!!! I just had to unfollow Bare Bones on Instagram because they were posting too many luscious photos and seemings as they are way too far away now, I couldn't take it.)

We even have been to an excellent barbeque place in Phoenix, Little Miss BBQ. (Oh my!!!)

We got our hopes up partially because on our way into Columbus, moving truck in tow, we stumbled upon an excellent barbeque restaurant South of here, 7 Miles Smokehouse.

So back to Smoked on High. I have been wanting to come here before I even moved here. We are now missing our longlost famous KC Texan breakfast brisket tacos too long. So today was finally the day to try some Cbus brisket and if succesful, take some home.

We got some brisket of course. On the lovely lady's suggestion at the counter, we tried the spare ribs. We also tried the coleslaw and mac and cheese, and all three sauces.

So I went straight for the star of the show, the brisket. It was moist....big headstart plus! We did ask for the moist, but at some places, we are still handed tough meat. It had a nice flavor, a lovely smoke, especially in the fat. (Don't hate on me. I eat healthy most of the time. But sometimes it is time for fatty brisket, for what is great brisket without the fat?! Loyal Texan here...)  Hubby echoed many other reviewers in saying the meat didn't need a sauce. Score.

I usually am not a fan of spare ribs, but they had an excellent taste and were tender.

The mac and cheese was interesting, and boasted Thanksgiving flavors of something like rosemary and sage, very herby and not very cheesy. Hubby, connoisseur of mac and cheeses galour gave it the thumbs up.

I gave the coleslaw a thumbs up. It very much reminded me of the Texan coleslaws of my youth, which of course are the way coleslaws should taste. ;) It had a little extra kick of black pepper which was okay with me.

The sauces were all very interesting. There was a sweet, spicy, and mustard sauce. Surprisingly with the battle of Texan versus Carolina style raging strong, and the loyalists tasking sides, the Carolina mustard sauce is growing on me. Hubby, still skeptical, pronounced it one of the best mustard sauces he has had. We enjoyed all the sauces to some extent, although they weren't quite my favorite barbeque sauces. The mustard was my favorite of the three.

Hubby also tried a lemon acai soda which was very unique. It was nice and fun, but a little too sweet for my tastes, but then I don't drink sodas.

Lastly, service was EXCELLENT. The lady and gentleman were eager to please and pleasant.

So, yes, we left with a pound of brisket, and yes, we will be back.

Everyone we met or came in contact with that works there is so bubbly, friendly and happy! One man comes to mind (but not too take away from anyone else) who's name is Brenner! His smile never left his face! He is amazingly accommodating!
The world needs more Brenner's!
The food I can't even find perfect words to use for how good it is. Normally you'll get a good this or that but the side isn't, blah blah blah.. but here, every bite of every thing my wife and I tried was out of this world!!  Great sized portions. All six sauces that set on every table tastes great, the green beans with bacon was so good, I drank the juice from it!!! The fries are hand cut and perfectly seasoned. The potato salad reminded me of my mom's. The sausage with jalapeno is so darn good without being to hot.  The peach cobbler and brownies are simply to die for.  Smoke brisket, the best I've ever eaten.  I honestly hope it stays around for a very, very long time. Our area needed consistent, great BBQ and I truly believe it's been found in Missions BBQ.  Even the "latrine" has a urinal that takes you back to your basic training days!!
And for being one of the first 100 through the door we get a years free bbq... This just doesn't happen, like how percentages of proceeds go to various charities.
At noon they stop all operations to play the Star Spangled Banner. Mad respect for doing that! If you buy the big American Hero Cup soft drink you can bring it back for .99 refills! Who does that?!
Also, you can join their birthday club, hometown heroes club and veterans vip club! That's so awesome!
It's great to see a place thoughtful of veterans, first responders and those that care for others in a time when so many don't.

Today was my first experience at Chicago Culinary Kitchen and the reviews cannot justify how good the food actually is here.  Everything was cooked to perfection.  We tried as much as we could within reason.  Brisket(leaner cut), spare ribs, esquites, beans, pig candy(candied bacon), and the bread pudding.

The brisket was cooked perfectly and the cut was just what we asked for,  minimal fat. It was super tender and juicy,  no knife required.   The spare ribs were without a doubt the best ribs I've had to date.   Great bark on it,  extremely tender but still enough bite to remain on the bone.   The smoke really permeated the meat and creates a fantastic flavor profile.   Both the brisket and ribs are great with or without barbecue sauce.   If you're a purist the meat comes without sauce so don't worry.   The barbeque sauce itself is a perfect compliment to the flavor of the meat.   It is a little sweet yet tangy and any left over on your tray is easily soaked up with the white bread accompanying your meal.

The beans were done exquisitely,  a little sweet and smokey.  The beans were still a bit firm so it doesn't just turn into a mole like some places and there is meat cooked in making them nice and hearty.  The pig candy was comparable to Au cheval in the city albeit a thinner cut of bacon but just as delicious.  It was my first time trying esquites and I was far from disappointed.  They retained the corn flavor quite well while also complimenting it with the cream and spices, it kept me coming back for bite after bite.

To finish things off we had the bread pudding.   Sometimes I am weary to try bread pudding at places because it can be very hit or miss.   They hit it out of the park!  It was sweet but not over powering in that department.   The fireball caramel sauce on top was a perfect pair.   It was reminiscent of going to get a fresh baked cinnamon roll.   All in all every single thing was cooked perfectly and I would eat it all again and again.   Next time I plan to try other items on the menu because I'm certain they will be just as phenomenal.

The ambiance and staff were just as good as the food.   The communal dining is actually very inviting and the decor is all their own in styling.  The staff was all very nice and engaging.  They are obviously a very busy restaurant, but they all made sure anything a customer needed was taken care of.

5/5 would come again and recommend the restuarant to anyone including random strangers.

A remarkable establishment with an intriguing and insightful décor of treasures to match the culinary delights that Red's offers.  Of note is that Red's is the legacy of Pat's late father, his nick name.  This honor is reflected is the various tributes that one will find when they explore their surroundings while waiting for their meal.  With Pat commanding the stove in the kitchen your order is sure to be a delicious main course.  A course that is navigated via the grill top irons that match the cardinal direction points of a compass.  Everything from a rich chili to their signature prime rib is warmed up in this kitchen for your family's feast.
I visited Red's in November on the Afternoon that preceded the Super-moon of 2016 where a band was playing for an educational benefit. I stopped at K&K on a whim, driving by it around dinnertime. I'm glad I did.

Firstly, they have the friendliest young lady at the counter. Just makes you feel good to talk to her. My order took minimal time to come up to the window.  I actually missed the handle when she handed it to me, and half of the order spilled out. It was my fault, but she insisted that she was to blame, and immediately started another order, which came up lickety-split. I know a lot of places that wouldn't even think of doing that.

For $7.99, I got a huge box o' tips, fries, and the tastiest side of mixed greens in the city. I always get my tips dry, with sauce on the side. (mostly because I prefer Carolina style sauce, because there is something magical about the mustard). And, it's soooo much better when you gently dip them in the sauce, compared to drowning them in it. Besides, so much love goes into slow cooking ribs that when you find a place that does it right, it's the only way fully appreciate the magic.

Anyway, K&K tips are PERFECT for doing it that way. They use a rub of some kind, generously applied. And it's awesome. The sauce is the perfect balance of tangy and spicy, and the tips are so succulent that you only really need a dollop). Each piece was sizeable, meaty, succulent, perfectly seasoned. And...there was easilya full Pound, and I order the "basket" size, not the "dinner" size. Nothing was burnt, there was minimal fat, and NO gristle.

The fries were those beer-batteryish type. And awesome. But to me, the sign of a good soul food place is when they have mixed greens that are to die for. And their greens are absolutely outstanding. I'd would buy it by the pound.

SB/Mishawaka is lucky to have a couple of great rib places already, with Frankie's and Pitt's being mainstays of the community for ages. I think K&K is every bit as good, in every way, and will hopefully become equally as famous.

You get a couple of slices of bread with your meal. Place has only been open for a month and a half. While I was there they were definitely doing the business, pretty much non stop. They have inside and outside seating.

The thing to remember when you read a review from me place is I'm rating it on restaurants of like category. For example I might give a high end restaurant three stars but a local diner four. The high end restaurants food might have been better but I'm comparing it for the cost, service, etc that I'd expect from that type of restaurant. That being said, Homeboys is barely a eat in restaurant. They only have three or four tables inside (a couple of picnic tables outside too) and do a lot of takeout. You eat with plastic ware and its served in takeout containers. Having said all this if you love BBQ you must get there.

My suggestions are two things, though I've not had anything here to eat that I thought was bad. First, the pulled pork plate for about $8 comes with two big buns and enough pulled pork to make two huge sandwiches. I'm a big eater and can't finish it. You also get one side. Get the creamy coleslaw. It's some of the best ever, be aware though it has pineapple which adds a little sweetness.

Secondly there's a smoked 1/2 chicken dinner which comes with two sides. That also goes for around $8 and we'll fill you up. One last suggestion if your feeling a family they have a family meal option which will fill up the heartiest eaters.

If you are near Homeboys go here. If you need to drive an hour to eat her do it.

It's always a bonus to see a place feature their own sauces even if they don't all shine. In our case we loved the Sweet, the Michigan Apple and the Carolina. The kids ordered Eagle sandwiches and the adults split some pulled pork and sausages. Everything was perfect. This weekend, a friend texted me and asked if I wanted to try a new BBQ joint. I couldn't pass it up. So we drove to Lizton and parked in a small lot in front of a building that was even smaller. The smell of the wood-fired smoker was everywhere. They have indoor and outdoor seating, but it is still quite limited. We chose the brisket platter with tomatoes and cucumbers and a pork sandwich with potato salad. I watched them pull the pork by hand, which is a testament to the tenderness of the meat. Both meals were delicious. I enjoyed all of the table-side sauces -- especially the habanero bourbon sauce and the mustard sauce. There are no soft drink refills, but they sell beer and the iced tea is good. The only suggestion I'd have for them is to maybe move the trash container away from the entrance to avoid any unpleasant smells from lingering. Overall, this place deserves five stars and is in my top go-to BBQ joints alongside South Street Smokehouse in Lafayette, Big Hoffas in Westfield, or Hawg Heaven in Kokomo.

It had enough cheese for normal people, onion rings(I upgraded my side for .99c, I would give it a 2 out of 5 stars.) I just feel like I have had better. The sides for that were mashed potatoes and gravy again, and then the fire roasted corn(2.5 out of 5 stars). It tasted fine, but after a couple of nibbles I was finished. Desserts; we ordered the fried cocoa crisp oreos(3 out of 5 stars) I probably would never order them again, but they tasted better than I thought they were going to. The sauce that is served with it is somehow a bit sour and tangy and was absolutely phenomenal. My only complaint towards this establishment was the prices of the side dishes. For 5 dollars each, or 3 for 12, it still feels like you barely get anything for the price paid. While they are high quality ingredients it still was a bit pricey. The first thing I noticed when I walked in was a bourbon barrel from Buffalo Trace distillery, As a bourbon lover, this was a very good sign!  We were greeted quickly and seated.  After being seated we were quickly greeted by our server Alison, a very polite, attentive and professional server.  She answered questions about the drink menu and even went to check on one of their bourbons (they had a typo on their menu that was, well, strange, so she checked it out)  We ordered drinks, I got a 52 mule which is their version of a Kentucky mule--very tasty, my wife wasn't sure so sampled a beer or two and then got a tasty local craft brew.

We ordered some hush puppies with pulled pork on top (it is their featured appetizer with some cool name I can't remember) and it was delicious.  It was served with some zesty cole slaw and some type of ranchy/horshradishy kind of sauce.
When we got our meals (almost too quick, we hadn't quite finished our apps)  the plates were laden down with large amounts of food.  I got the beef brisket and there had to be 12 or more ounces of meat on my plate.  A very generous portion of hot crispy fries and some cole slaw.  My wife's slider plate was just about as full as mine.  The meat was close to perfect--if I had to nitpick, I would prefer my meat be seasoned just a bit more as it was kind of plain without the sauce, but very good.  The sauce was all very tasty with my favorite being the gold style with mustard.  The only thing I wasn't impressed with was my coleslaw--it was a bit dry for my taste, but a spoon of the left over horseradishy dressing from our appetizer made it perfect.

Alison continued her excellent service checking on us throughout our meal and even telling us about the activities going on in Chelsea.

I will be back for sure.  Their prices are on the high side (my beef brisket dinner was $19, my drink was about $10-the beer was a little cheaper )  but here the food and service quality are really top notch so it is worth the money.

I was looking for something good to eat and I stumbled across Pull Up Grill & BBQ while surfing the net. The reviews sounded good so I placed my order online for pick up. I've driven by this location many times and never knew it was there. I ordered turkey ribs, my first time eating them, mac & cheese, and green beans. Let me first say green beans are low on my list of green vegetables that I like I prefer brussel sprouts or lima beans more than green beans. The green beans had one of my favorite seasonings.... garlic! They weren't bad but that garlic had me ALMOST liking green beans...LOL. The mac & cheese was very creamy and good. Baby, the star of my dinner was those turkey ribs. I had no idea of what a turkey rib looked like or what to expect. All I can say is if I eat them somewhere else they have some big shoes to fill. The meat was oh so tender and fell off the bone. It was smoked to perfection you could taste the smokiness in every bite. The accompanied BBQ sauce was delicious as well but the meat didn't need any enhancement or sauce to take away the taste of the rib. I also got a piece of carrot cake that was nice and moist as well. This little hidden gem is now on my radar and I will definitely be back to try other menu items.

I think they tried to step outside the box with the Mac and cheese but in my opinion penne noodles have no place in Mac and cheese. If they stepped out the box and tried shells I could see that but penne no no no. All in all great meats and very unique bbq sauce but my favorite sides were a let down. I plan to come back and try them again in high hopes that whoever was in the kitchen that day had a heavy hand with the salt.

The sauce was very good, little on the sweeter side but still delectable. Now for the sides! Went with the green again and red beans and rice. The greens were cooked perfect great flavor and best of all didn’t taste like pure salt. The red beans and rice were spot on and hell of a lot less salt this time, still I little bit more then I personally like but do able. All in all I’m so happy I stopped back to give them a second shot. Mission bbq has been my go to because they are closer but I think im going to be driving the few extra miles for now on. Mission is good but does not compare to SHARKS brisket period.

Dropped in here to check it out, and we're glad we did. They've been open 3 weeks now, and Peter G.'s extensive experience in the restaurant business shows. No startup glitches, they were running great without hiccups.

The first impression is the restaurant is inviting and comfortable. The second impression is a friendly greeting and Peter Ginapolis,  the owner,  is working the front, introduces himself to us, and takes us to our table. He came back a couple more times to make sure everything was to our liking, and even took me outside to meet his chefs who were working the smoker.

The quality of the ingredients is evident- everything was fresh and prepared technically well, seasoning and flavor profiles were just right. The pulled pork was delicious,  just the right amount of smoke (they use both hickory and cherry in the smoker), excellent texture, and not one glob of fat or connective tissue on the plate. The pulled chicken was equally of high quality, not dried out, and well seasoned.  Sides were good, roasted corn, brisket bacon beans, mac 'n cheese. All great.

There is a good selection of draft and bottled beers, wine, and a full bar. Menu has a bigger selection of items than most BBQ restaurants,  with apps, seafood, salads, sandwiches, and full dinners.

Big points for:
-The sauces are original and there's a good variety (I couldnt get enough of the Baybecue, wow).
-The prices are comparable to any other bbq joint whether here or KC or St Louis, even though they may have been able to get away with charging more.
-Staff constantly wade through tables to clean and clear trays as you're finished, which is just a nice touch of extra commitment to the experience.

<Additional> after having been there a number of times now, I can say this is my preferred bbq, outside of my home.  They cook things properly and to my preference...with a nice bark.  Most importantly,  the meat, fat, connective tissue is broke down correctly.  This doesn't mean everything always turns out perfect.   This is bbq and items fluctuate in quality,  to a degree.

They are also improving and changing things up. The pulled pork, that I mentioned below in my first review,  is now consistently broken down quite well.  For me, it's become one of their top items.  Although I still find myself ordering the brisket most times I go in there.  Sausage has gone through a few changes, each variation is enjoyable.   All in all, nice place</Additional info end>

Because bbq can be so tough to hold, I normally like to try a new bbq place three to four times before writing a review.   Turnover and learning your daily customer base is key.  For this reason I will never complain when a bbq restaurant tells me they're out of an item or if they pull an item if it had been sitting to long.

Setting aside a truly impressive resume from the Chef,  the first thing I noticed was that this place knows how to properly break down protein.   Belly, brisket and ribs were all beautifully cooked.  Bbq is so much about starting with a good product and applying proper technique, St1 accomplishes this.  The simplicity of the rub is appreciated.  The ribs were probably the best that I've had from a bbq joint to date.  My portion of pulled pork was taken a bit too far, but certainly still okay.  Corn bread was nice and unique...it gave me the impression of a version of polenta cornbread,  really tasty!

I could go on about a proper bark, nicely rendered fat, etc, etc.  Oh, the in house sausages are well done as well.  Finer grind than I would have suspected,  but a welcome  interpretation.   The sausage was well made, well stuffed, and nicely cooked.

I loved everything about my experience at Landmark.   Our group walked in, none of us having been there before, and a nice man handed us all menus and gave us the run down of how things worked and recommended of his favorite menu items. They specialize in Montreal smoked meats, and oh boy, I'm so happy I ordered the Montreal smoked turkey Reuben. It was deliciously peppery, tender, and had a nice amount of woodsy smoke. The Russian dressing was zesty and light- but I chose cole slaw as a side... Sweet and vinegary. Not bogged down with thick mayo! Such a refreshing change from most slaws. They have a nice selection of draft beers and cocktails too! You always ordered at the counter, so food comes out nice & quick. The staff came to check on our table multiple times throughout the meal, which was nice if we wanted another beer or dessert.

I tried the Mac and cheese that my group ordered as well, which had beautiful toasted bread crumbs and parsley on top, and a surprising kick! I love all spice so that worked for me!

Also, the cookies. These are how cookies should always be. They were chunky like a scone, served warm with a crisp exterior and a soft gooey chocolatey interior.

For how much time and love goes into the smoked meats, the prices are completely fair! My group agreed the meats are on par with Mabel's, of not better.

This little hidden gem is now on my radar and I will definitely be back to try other menu items.

I am pretty new to Korean BBQ. So far, I have only had it at Star and once at Masijta. In both case we were a party of four that broadly bought the entire BBQ menu (or at least all the really fancy dishes on the menu). In case this makes a difference, we ate at Star late during a weekday evening (from about 8-10pm), and at Masijta during a Friday afternoon/early evening. Any reader should be aware, all I really care about is how good the food is-- price, atmosphere, service, etc. are all distant, secondary concerns for me, and right now, I'm focusing on finding the best Korean BBQ in around town (I like other Korean dishes as well, but I've found not nearly as much as the BBQ). The comparison between Star and Masijta BBQ isn't even a contest-- they aren't even playing in the same league. Star wins the battle of the BBQ hands down. The quality of the meat brought to the table was considerably better/better prepared at Star (Masijta's meats were all grisly and tough, Star's were all tender and succulent). Not only were the cuts of meat superior at Star, the presentation was far better. At Star, every bit of meat looked to have been carefully rolled/arranged on the platter in a artistic presentation, and each piece had obviously been given some TLC to ensure it was up to par. At Masijta, the meat came out in a massive gloppy pile (all the meats) with no care given to selection/preparation of the individual cuts or it's presentation. I only mention the presentation here because I think it speaks to how much/little care goes in to selecting the cuts of meat for the BBQ.

So, as far as Korean BBQ goes:
Star gets 5 of 5 stars! ;) Every bit of meat was delicious!
Masijta gets 2 of 5 stars. The quality of the meat wasn't even average-- it was below average. Of what was edible, it was tough and grisly. The pork cheek wasn't even edible.

This was our first visit to the Plantation Supper Club and it was a very enjoyable experience.  I have to be honest, we've been driving by for years and maybe it's a case of just being too familiar of a landmark at Hwy 51 and 70E and never really being motivated to stop...they really exceeded my expectations and that's why I'd urge you to give the Plantation a visit.  We love Wisconsin Supper Clubs and with that said, The Plantation certainly qualifies as a historic, iconic Northwoods Supper Club.  From the minute we walked in, we were enjoying ourselves - from the "throwback" blue and white bar to the friendly greeting when we arrived - we knew this was going to be a good visit.  Anna greeted us at the bar and fixed us a couple of Wisconsin classics - Brandy Old Fashioned.  We tried some of the sharp cheddar and horseradish cheese spreads as we learned more about the history of Plantation and the Woodruff area.  Candy served as our hostess and our server - she is a hoot.  She was professional, entertaining, and efficient - all great qualities that contributed to a wonderful first visit.  I tried the Prime rib and scallops and "she" tried the scallops with a baked potato - both entrees were served to perfection and were delicious.  Before dinner was served, Candy brought Hors d'oeuvres - deep fried chicken wings and toasted swiss cheese melts - seemed like an odd combination but they were excellent.  Next we tried the seafood bisque - not too heavy, not too rich - well seasoned - very good.  As I was paying our bill, Candy invited us to tour the kitchen and the entire facility, she mentioned that she had been in the food service industry many years and she has never worked at a restaurant that is so impeccably clean - although we didn't have time to accept her invitation, I really appreciated her genuine pride in the restaurant and it shows in her service - kudos.  Here's the interesting thing - the reason we finally visited the Plantation Supper Club was a friend, who is a local realtor, mentioned how much he enjoyed their Ahi Tuna steak and how impeccably clean the place is, "you could eat of the kitchen floor" he exclaimed...his recommendation brought us in and the Plantation's hometown hospitality and delicious food will bring us back - perfect combination - thank you for the enjoyable evening.

I ate the brisket, hot sausage links, fried pickles, and slaw.

The brisket was a perfect cut; right amount of smoke, flavorful, tender, and moist.  It wasn't dry or fatty; it was cooked just right.  It was cooked just like a brisket should be cooked - Texas style, the right layer of fat on top to keep the meat moist and tender, it melts in your mouth.  I don't use BBQ sauce on brisket, I just dip a corner here and there while eating to sample the sauces.

The hot link sausage was the same; right amount of spice and kick - tender and juicy, no need to use sauce to improve it, the sauces offered are a nice compliment, but I don't think it's needed.

The fried dill pickles are unbelievable, add the Alabama white BBQ sauce, wow!  They weren't soggy or mushy, the breading/batter is crisp, the pickles we're crunchy, not pasty, which can happen when frying pickles.

I search out out good BBQ all over Chicagoland, but it's difficult.  Chicago is NOT known for it's BBQ.  I've lived and traveled all over the US, and BBQ is an art, it truly is.  I always look for brisket and sausage, and use it as a gage.  I'm not a rib or pulled pork guy, so I don't comment on them. Firewater offers very very good brisket and sausage.

Both are worth a visit.  JMHO.

With 170 craft beers selection, a seeming 80+% of which looks to be local, and a rotating smoking rack you can see from the entire restaurant, filled with probably over a hundred pounds of various meats, I chose a pork sandwich with the ranch beans (as in style, filled with other veggies, not the dressing), mac and cheese, and the bourbon pecan pie, paired with a Southern Pecan nut brown ale. You can tell from their meat and sides selection, that they mean serious southern barbecue business here.

For being a barbecue joint, the beans would delight a vegetarian, who could probably make a decent meal from the nine vegetable/non-meat side options. The pork was solid, and the habenero bourbon sauce stood high above the other selections. The heat of the habenero was deceptive, as I hardly felt it going in, but a beer-fueled burp after I finished the sandwich brought it back in more potent force. Still, the heat is diluted enough to benefit from the flavor while not offending as many would normally be put off by the name.

The bourbon pecan pie was better than most pecan pies I've ever had, but it was the mac and cheese that stole the show. I was skeptical at first when I saw goldfish crackers in it, but after my first bite, I was utterly convinced. Forgetting the crackers, only added for crunch, their mac and cheese was the best and most satisfying homestyle mac and cheese I've had in decades. I'm not kidding. I want their recipe.

The soundtrack in this joint delightfully fits the food and rustic feel of the place, being half old-timey western tunes and covers of modern songs done in that style, and half 'O Brother Where are Thou?' soundtrack. The small rural town residents I'm currently dining with I could easily imagine as regulars, and somehow add to the charm.

The $19 my total before tip came to seemed a tad high, though they've received an Indy Star "Best Things Winner" award for Best Barbecue Restaurant, and I can see why. Sadly, living on the opposite side of Indy, I won't be making it this way very often, but if I ever find myself back here in Lizton, you can bet I'll be grabbing barbecue.

TL; DR Version: Great smoked meats, wonderful side dishes, friendly service and contemporary decor in the heart of Plainfield.

We arrived shortly after 12:30, and event though this was but Station One's third day in business, the queue was not an issue.  Once we entered the establishment, the smell of smoked meats was intoxicating. As we waited in line, we reviewed the menu posted above the counter. The menu is not complicated, by any means: You can choose to have your meats by the half-pound, or in sandwich form. The menu board was clear and easy to understand.

I decided upon the pork belly, and my wife opted for the pulled pork. The pork was sliced and weighed out in open view, dripping with juices as they are placed on the paper-lined metal tray. From there, we asked for some Mac-N-Cheese and Elotes, which were served in paper trays. The metal and paper service complement the overall decor, which is industrial. As we collected, and paid for our food, the staff was very friendly, freely answering questions and even going so far as to provide some small samples of their cornbread and the broccoli slaw. After snagging some slices of white bread and spicy pickles, we made out way to our table.

Our food was everything we would want in barbecue: The meat was tender, smokey, and full of melt-in-your mouth flavor. The macaroni and cheese was creamy, using large-gauge pasta designed for holding sauce. Our elotes were hot, and in a flavorful melange of chili powder, cheese, and creamy sauce.

We did not have a chance to try the bar, but it looked cozy, and well-appointed with good quality liquors (and Malort). Perhaps next time :) Thanks, Station One, for providing another wonderful dining option in Plainfield!

The three meat plate was enough for 2 at lunch time and came with some great sides. The beans weren't what I was expecting, but man were they good. The cornbread muffins were decent albeit a little dry. The coleslaw wasn't anything amazing but I enjoyed it and would order it again. The BBQ sauce is good depending on what you're used to. I used the it sparingly though as the meats spoke for themselves.

For meats we had the Milwaukee Ribs, Brisket, and Pulled Pork. The Ribs were interesting as the pork belly is left on making them about twice as tall as what you'd be expecting. This adds a ton of flavor, but naturally leaves the ribs very fatty. That isn't at all a bad thing but might not be for everyone. The pulled pork was smoked well and delivered great flavor.

Now I didn't like the brisket, I F'n loved it!!! I judge almost all BBQ places on their brisket and that's the main reason for the 5 stars. It is perfectly sliced, passes the pull test and packs an amazing amount of flavor into the bite. It is everything you could want out of a brisket and more. You can tell they know how to tend to the fire and get good clean smoke rolling.

TL:DR Go here as soon as humanly possible and let your eyes be bigger than your stomach because the food coma and meat sweats are well worth it. Your taste buds will thank you, your waistband won't.

Lillie's is a breath of fresh air in a market of boring, mediocre barbecue joints. The decor is spectacular - themed after an old fashioned slaughter house, I'd guess. Exposed light bulbs dangling from meat hooks, giant lamps from the ceilings that are reminiscent of a factory floor, and just about everything else is solid, warm wood.

The staff was very friendly and accommodating, and their uniforms fit the "old factory" feel.

Finally, the barbecue is outstanding. The pulled pork and tri-tips are amazing. The chicken was a let down - skip that. Perhaps most exciting was the barbecue sauces. They have the traditional (boring) tomato based sauces, then also vinegar and mustard base, which one does not often see in Chicago.

Beer selection is wonderful. The moon-shine based cocktails are also fantastic. Just be careful... nothing here is cheap!

I would probably pay a king's ransom for onion rings this good. Thankfully, I don't have to.

My philosophy of restaurant quality (also called the Onion Ring Standard) took some time to develop, but it first began here, at Saucy Dog's Barbecue in Jonesville, MI. I went there with a friend on a whim my freshman year of college, and decided to try the onion rings. I was blown away. Every time I have returned, I got the onion rings again and again. Simply put, these are the best onion rings I have ever had.

Presentation and Appearance - 4.5/5

When I think of an onion ring, there are usually at least two images that come to mind. The first is a thin, crispy, somewhat refined breaded strip of onion. The second type is like these onion rings: thick, a little rustic, and almost meaty in its appearance. The batter on the onion is smooth. The bubbles and crumbs that interrupt this smoothness lend to it an air of authenticity and charm, one that feels completely genuine. These onion rings feel like a perfect representation of the restaurant they come from, and that is to their strength.

I've docked half a point for presentation for two reasons. One, the size of the basket is just a bit too small. The mass of onion rings, while heaping and appetizing, has a tendency to spill out over the edges. Second, one onion ring was dropped off the basket and landed on the table just before they got to me. I ate it anyway, but it's not a great feeling.

Taste - 5/5

I don't even know where to begin. The batter was smooth, almost buttery and creamy, and delicious. There weren't a tremendous amount of seasonings in the batter, but the subtle flavor was a strength. The inner onion, meanwhile, was unique among onion rings. It was lightly sweated/sauteed prior to being dipped and fried. This gives it a light, not overpowering, flavor of onion throughout the ring. The batter and the onion meld in a delicious, slightly greasy, blend. They are a seamless, tasty whole.

A brief word on the accompanying dipping sauce. While often the sauce accompanying the onion ring is a poorly masked attempt to hide the poor flavor of an onion ring underneath a deluge of sauce, these sauce is the perfect complement to these onion rings. I would be hard pressed to find anything I'd rather dip these rings in. I have nothing bad to say about the taste of these rings.

Texture - 4.5/5

The texture on the batter is near perfection. Firm without being too hard, smooth without being too rich, it is a beautiful medium between all extremes. My only complaint comes with the irregular cooking of some of the breading (the bits and crumbs that disturb the overall smoothness), which were good, but not necessarily consistent with the rest of the onion ring.

The onion is interesting and unique, as noted in the taste section. The lightly sweated/sauteed onion could go disastrously wrong, with the onion becoming a mushy paste, and not firm enough to hold shape. This is not the case here. The sweating gives it just enough give to be soft and smooth, but it has sufficient firmness to hold the shape of the ring together. The best part of the texture is that there's just enough contrast between the batter and the onion to know there's a difference, but they complement each other perfectly.

Value - 5/5

A basket of these onion rings (as an appetizer) costs $5.49, and it is worth every penny. They aren't incredibly expensive (indeed, they're practically cheap by most restaurant standards), but you get what you pay for, and more. While the heaping basket has some presentation flaws, it lets the eater know they're getting a tremendous amount of delicious, thick, huge golden brown onion rings.

Total: 19/20

Not only was the food great but so we're the employees! Stopped here on a whim and glad I did. The brisket sandwich was great as we're the bbq beans. Next time I get around that area I'll be stopping by again.

With 170 craft beers selection, a seeming 80+% of which looks to be local, and a rotating smoking rack you can see from the entire restaurant, filled with probably over a hundred pounds of various meats, I chose a pork sandwich with the ranch beans (as in style, filled with other veggies, not the dressing), mac and cheese, and the bourbon pecan pie, paired with a Southern Pecan nut brown ale. You can tell from their meat and sides selection, that they mean serious southern barbecue business here.

For being a barbecue joint, the beans would delight a vegetarian, who could probably make a decent meal from the nine vegetable/non-meat side options. The pork was solid, and the habenero bourbon sauce stood high above the other selections. The heat of the habenero was deceptive, as I hardly felt it going in, but a beer-fueled burp after I finished the sandwich brought it back in more potent force. Still, the heat is diluted enough to benefit from the flavor while not offending as many would normally be put off by the name.

The bourbon pecan pie was better than most pecan pies I've ever had, but it was the mac and cheese that stole the show. I was skeptical at first when I saw goldfish crackers in it, but after my first bite, I was utterly convinced. I happened to eat here a week ago on kind of a whim, while heading to another restaurant. In passing it by, my wife and I got curious and decided to try it out. This place is great. While we've only been here for lunch, both times have been worth it.

The location is laid out much like a more spacious version of an Outback Steakhouse or a Texas Roadhouse. It's pretty much all wood, with a beautifully designed bar serving as sort of the centerpiece for the restaurant. The place is clean and, while large, inviting.

The service has been good both times. Our server approached us within minutes of being seated (often by the same person), and orders came out promptly.

The food, I really cannot wait to explain.

The first time, we decided to split a full rack of ribs, and split an appetizer of three street tacos. You get three choices of taco: steak, brisket, and pulled pork. The steak tacos are nothing too special, the brisket tacos are very tasty and tender, and the pulled pork tacos... they redefine expectations of what a taco should taste like. I still cannot forget the flavor packed into this combination of pulled pork, cabbage, salsa, and guacamole, all wrapped in a flour tortilla which is crispy on the outside and soft and warm on the inside. If they don't provide it, ask for a few slices of lime to sprinkle on top, you should not be disappointed. The full rack of ribs were equally delicious. I'm familiar with restaurant ribs having a pressure cooked, thin rack of ribs that have little flavor on their own, whose flavor is balanced with an overly sweet sauce to mask the quality. Smokey Bones, however, has a true smoked flavor in the meat, and the sauce does not try to mask any of that flavor; instead it complements it perfectly. For those who are more into sauce than the meat, there are a variety of sauces on the table to adjust it to your taste.

The second time we visited, we both went for the tacos, and split an order of onion rings. The tacos, I hope I've explained how delicious they are (go for all 3 pulled pork, you can get it for $9.99). The onion rings were perfectly cooked, with some type of batter that stayed crispy even after it cooled down, maintained its seasoning, and protected the onion from turning to mush. Onion rings from some restaurants always pull completely out of the batter when you take a bite, leaving you with too much onion and not enough batter the first bite, and vice versa the rest of the time. This was NOT the case here. From the first to the last, the flavor and texture was consistent. Furthermore, it had a light and crispy flavor to it, so even after several of them, we didn't feel heavy.

Lastly, they provide a method to pay for your meal at the table in case the server is running a little slow (even though ours was not). We tried it out the second time, and the convenience of just paying and leaving without the need to wait for the back and forth was a plus for the lunchtime rush. I would only recommend that the restaurant face the screen towards the table so people understand that this is an option -- it had to be explained to us the first time.

Overall, we have been twice very impressed with Smoke Bones, and will definitely be returning, hopefully very soon.

I'll start with saying that I really like the food so I'm going to cut them a lot of slack.  The fries are fresh cut and the sauces are good and warm with a thin consistency which I like.

That said, this is a strange place.   For starters, are there any other barbeque joints in malls?  You'd think the process of getting some pork would be straightforward, but no experience is ever quite the same here.  You may be one of the only people there but still have to wait 25 minutes for fries.  They once forgot my fries for like 30 minutes and to make it up to me gave me a huge order of them that nearly killed me (and which I appreciated).  For years every time I went in there I would receive a different price for the same exact order.  Going in for the BOGO deal?  There is a good chance the person taking your order isn't aware of such a deal or is aware but will struggle trying to enter it into their system.  The terms are not straightforward and not well understood or enforced either.  This was all a bigger problem in the days before "The Change".

I don't know what precipitated it, but one day they shut down and said they would reopen as a burger joint.  That was until they later changed their mind and reopened months later as the same place.  Things are a bit more consistent now with the pricing, and the terms of the BOGO are less favorable but at least seem known and understandable to the employees.

If you are going you may want to call ahead.  I've seen this place shut down for the following reasons.
-out of pork, gate shut but people inside and employees not acknowledging anything happened, a worker had a medical issue and paramedics were in the kitchen, employee appreciation event, change of business hours, went out of business for months.

Lillie's is a breath of fresh air in a market of boring, mediocre barbecue joints. The decor is spectacular - themed after an old fashioned slaughter house, I'd guess. Exposed light bulbs dangling from meat hooks, giant lamps from the ceilings that are reminiscent of a factory floor, and just about everything else is solid, warm wood.

The staff was very friendly and accommodating, and their uniforms fit the "old factory" feel.

Finally, the barbecue is outstanding. The pulled pork and tri-tips are amazing. The chicken was a let down - skip that. Perhaps most exciting was the barbecue sauces. They have the traditional (boring) tomato based sauces, then also vinegar and mustard base, which one does not often see in Chicago.

Beer selection is wonderful. The moon-shine based cocktails are also fantastic. Just be careful... nothing here is cheap!

I stopped at K&K on a whim, driving by it around dinnertime. I'm glad I did.

Firstly, they have the friendliest young lady at the counter. Just makes you feel good to talk to her. My order took minimal time to come up to the window.  I actually missed the handle when she handed it to me, and half of the order spilled out. It was my fault, but she insisted that she was to blame, and immediately started another order, which came up lickety-split. I know a lot of places that wouldn't even think of doing that.

For $7.99, I got a huge box o' tips, fries, and the tastiest side of mixed greens in the city. I always get my tips dry, with sauce on the side. (mostly because I prefer Carolina style sauce, because there is something magical about the mustard). And, it's soooo much better when you gently dip them in the sauce, compared to drowning them in it. Besides, so much love goes into slow cooking ribs that when you find a place that does it right, it's the only way fully appreciate the magic.

Anyway, K&K tips are PERFECT for doing it that way. They use a rub of some kind, generously applied. And it's awesome. The sauce is the perfect balance of tangy and spicy, and the tips are so succulent that you only really need a dollop). Each piece was sizeable, meaty, succulent, perfectly seasoned. And...there was easilya full Pound, and I order the "basket" size, not the "dinner" size. Nothing was burnt, there was minimal fat, and NO gristle.

The fries were those beer-batteryish type. And awesome. But to me, the sign of a good soul food place is when they have mixed greens that are to die for. And their greens are absolutely outstanding. I'd would buy it by the pound.

SB/Mishawaka is lucky to have a couple of great rib places already, with Frankie's and Pitt's being mainstays of the community for ages. I think K&K is every bit as good, in every way, and will hopefully become equally as famous.

So excited about this new restaurant opening next to the iconic Fitzgerald's. I came to order food to go as the patio was already full, not surprised due to the fact that Fitzgeralds was popping like always.  I was surprised they did have a dining room and decided to dine in.  With so many fabulous options it was hard to narrow down what to get.  We ended up getting the club club sandwich (turkey blt), the giant chicken wings, onion rings, pimento mac and cheese, & ice cream for dessert.  Starting with the sandwich this is no simple club sandwich.  With thick slices of turkey breast, pork belly, lettuce and tomato (ask for the bacon aioli for extra yumminess) my teenage son that eats everything could only get through half of this sandwich, it looks deceiving. Served with perfectly crispy shoestring seasoned fries this was a great treat.  The chicken wings (that have to be turkey wings bc they are huge & you can't change my mind) were perfectly juicy and had this fabulous crunch that was really how all wings should be. The onion rings were some of the best I've had in the city, possibly sprinkled with witchcraft and/or crack we devoured them all. The ice cream was exactly what I remember from an old school ice cream shop, not overly sweet, with a very creamy velvety texture.  Now the cons - the Mac and cheese just didn't do it for me, it felt very dry and grainy and didn't have a very cheesy taste for me.  I'll still try it again bc everything was so good I refuse to believe the mac couldn't be up there either.  While the staff were really friendly and great it definitely felt like they forgot about us in the dining room.  Nothing so bad that I would remove a star but more something that will be fixed once they get their bearings.  I'm looking forward to eating my way through the menu and I hope that everybody goes and shows this much needed addition to the area some love.

This location is all that remains of the old empire & while I may feel nostalgic about 3rd St, I am simply glad to have access to those ribs and that SAUCE & their house dressing!! The food has always been the best reason to go and remains the case. They use a vinegar recipe; if you are expecting sweet & sticky, you'll be surprised but not disappointed.

Their ribs are unparalleled. I don't live in Dayton anymore and have tried to find an equivalent; there is none, in neither a restaurant, food truck or grocery store. They have expanded the menu in the carry-out/cafe beyond steaks, chops & ribs, ribs the only of the former to remain. It now includes sandwiches, hamburgers, brisket, broasted wings, and a variety of sides. You can also buy their sauce, salad dressings & dry rubs by the jar! They even offer grill ready ribs for less cost, by the rack.

I go as often as I can. I recommend that you do the same!!
