So I heard about this place and I had a serious craving for ribs at lunch time. I walked about 2 miles to the place and every step and calorie burned was worth it. The ribs had a nice pink around the edges and was cooked to perfection. Unlike other places they cut the ribs correctly so each rib has a even amount of meat around the bone. The quality of meat itself is something to be desired at even your local meat shops. The consistency of texture is the same and you won't find any fat to be chewed through. I ordered macaroni and cheese and potato salad as my sides. They told me everything in house is made from scratch and i sure could taste it. The cheese on the macaroni had a good consistency and wasn't over powering the flavor of the ribs. The macaroni themselves weren't soggy as you would usually find. I didn't however too much care for the potato salad. I don't mind large chunks of potatoes but there was not a lot of dressing with it. At that point I might as well just had roasted potatoes and not a salad because of the lack of dressing. Any meat order comes with a serving of corn cake. The corn cake by far was my favorite right behind the ribs. Everything about the corn cake was perfect. The flavor, the texture and the feeling of fullness from it was perfect. I wish I ordered a second helping of it. The restaurant itself has a nice feeling to it. Good air conditioning in doors for the summer months and patios outdoors if you want to enjoy the weather. The customer service is very good. For the prices they are more than fair for location and quality of service.

I'll start with saying that I really like the food so I'm going to cut them a lot of slack.  The fries are fresh cut and the sauces are good and warm with a thin consistency which I like.

That said, this is a strange place.   For starters, are there any other barbeque joints in malls?  You'd think the process of getting some pork would be straightforward, but no experience is ever quite the same here.  You may be one of the only people there but still have to wait 25 minutes for fries.  They once forgot my fries for like 30 minutes and to make it up to me gave me a huge order of them that nearly killed me (and which I appreciated).  For years every time I went in there I would receive a different price for the same exact order.  Going in for the BOGO deal?  There is a good chance the person taking your order isn't aware of such a deal or is aware but will struggle trying to enter it into their system.  The terms are not straightforward and not well understood or enforced either.  This was all a bigger problem in the days before "The Change".

I don't know what precipitated it, but one day they shut down and said they would reopen as a burger joint.  That was until they later changed their mind and reopened months later as the same place.  Things are a bit more consistent now with the pricing, and the terms of the BOGO are less favorable but at least seem known and understandable to the employees.

If you are going you may want to call ahead.  I've seen this place shut down for the following reasons.
-out of pork, gate shut but people inside and employees not acknowledging anything happened, a worker had a medical issue and paramedics were in the kitchen, employee appreciation event, change of business hours, went out of business for months.

But yes, the food is good.

With my wife, adult daughter and adult son leading the way, we had lunch at The Prized Pig.  We were excited to dine here as we were semiregular customers of their location (now closed) in Niles.

The portions were generous, prepared to a tasteful degree and worth every penny.  I lived in Columbus, Georgia years ago and the sights and smells at The Prized Pig reminded me of some great smoked barbe-que from that region.

The rib tips my wife had were amazing and my beef platter was just a good as I remember.  The corn bread has that great "tacky" quality on top with a center that is not dry but not under baked either.  Just perfect.  The mac-n-cheese was prepared with some ham for flavor and the taste was spot-on; the texture is improved with a final bake to create a slightly crusty finish on top. Lastly, the baked beans are not my favorite, having been raised on Boston baked beans thanks to my mom and Grandpa; both natives to Massachusetts. There are very few places that offer such large, meaty, juicy ribs that fall off the bone like the New Riegel Cafe...and even fewer that offer them at such a reasonable price.  The sauce is completely unique, it's not store bought BBQ junk in a bottle, it's a garlic based blend of tangy deliciousness that is not found anywhere else.  The ribs are slow cooked, and they're both meaty and scrumptious...these aren't the small spare ribs that other joints have.  At about $11 for a regular order of ribs and fries, you can't go wrong.  In my opinion they're best with extra sauce, and put a little on your fries too.  The fries go well with the sauce.

The first thing I noticed when I walked in was a bourbon barrel from Buffalo Trace distillery, As a bourbon lover, this was a very good sign!  We were greeted quickly and seated.  After being seated we were quickly greeted by our server Alison, a very polite, attentive and professional server.  She answered questions about the drink menu and even went to check on one of their bourbons (they had a typo on their menu that was, well, strange, so she checked it out)  We ordered drinks, I got a 52 mule which is their version of a Kentucky mule--very tasty, my wife wasn't sure so sampled a beer or two and then got a tasty local craft brew.

We ordered some hush puppies with pulled pork on top (it is their featured appetizer with some cool name I can't remember) and it was delicious.  It was served with some zesty cole slaw and some type of ranchy/horshradishy kind of sauce.
When we got our meals (almost too quick, we hadn't quite finished our apps)  the plates were laden down with large amounts of food.  I got the beef brisket and there had to be 12 or more ounces of meat on my plate.  A very generous portion of hot crispy fries and some cole slaw.  My wife's slider plate was just about as full as mine.  The meat was close to perfect--if I had to nitpick, I would prefer my meat be seasoned just a bit more as it was kind of plain without the sauce, but very good.  The sauce was all very tasty with my favorite being the gold style with mustard.  The only thing I wasn't impressed with was my coleslaw--it was a bit dry for my taste, but a spoon of the left over horseradishy dressing from our appetizer made it perfect.

Alison continued her excellent service checking on us throughout our meal and even telling us about the activities going on in Chelsea.

I will be back for sure.  Their prices are on the high side (my beef brisket dinner was $19, my drink was about $10-the beer was a little cheaper )  but here the food and service quality are really top notch so it is worth the money.

Alright, for all those people that are reading this; curious to know if this BBQ Tavern is worth trying out.

I'll help you the best I can, with what I have to offer. I don't normally have a taste or preference for BBQ, as well as smoked meats. Just not my thing, but, I went with family so today we make an exception.

I'll get to the point. BBQ fan or not, get on over there and give it a chance. The staff seemed to have incorporated a pretty solid culture among themselves and between customers.

That said, this is not the stereotypical smoked meat you may be used to. Almost like it was meant to taste that way, as gravity pulls the meat right off the bone.

Not quite literally...but I did say quite ;)

I was surprised when I ordered a Caesar Salad and it was served with the dressing on the side. So I asked and was told by the server that they don't toss the Salads in dressing there. Not a huge deal, but I do have to say, was totally surprised by that. This isn't an Applebees.

For those of you wondering, I had 5 other plates around me, each with a different BBQ Masterpiece selected item. Remember, I'm not a fan of BBQ, but wow did this place really test my limits. Giant Brisket Sandwiches, giant slices of "Killer" Bacon (and I do mean "Killer" if you like Bacon), giant "fall-off-the-bone" Ribs...just, giant everything. In fact, I'd bet 10 bucks to anybody who can finish a sandwich in one sitting. Seriously...GIANT.

Here's the best part, they already know this! In fact, you even get a to-go bag after boxing up your food without even requesting it. For those like me who aren't captivated by cradling a styrofoam, rectangular container filled with our mana for survival, you'll understand. LOL

All in all, this place is a great experience and atmosphere to feed that "Wild Side" I know we all have. The owner himself made sure my family was taken care of tonight getting a table arranged. He even came by moments after to ensure that everyone was happy. Let me just tell you...that's what true food service is all about. That alone...is worth an A+.

So excited about this new restaurant opening next to the iconic Fitzgerald's. I came to order food to go as the patio was already full, not surprised due to the fact that Fitzgeralds was popping like always.  I was surprised they did have a dining room and decided to dine in.  With so many fabulous options it was hard to narrow down what to get.  We ended up getting the club club sandwich (turkey blt), the giant chicken wings, onion rings, pimento mac and cheese, & ice cream for dessert.  Starting with the sandwich this is no simple club sandwich.  With thick slices of turkey breast, pork belly, lettuce and tomato (ask for the bacon aioli for extra yumminess) my teenage son that eats everything could only get through half of this sandwich, it looks deceiving. Served with perfectly crispy shoestring seasoned fries this was a great treat.  The chicken wings (that have to be turkey wings bc they are huge & you can't change my mind) were perfectly juicy and had this fabulous crunch that was really how all wings should be. The onion rings were some of the best I've had in the city, possibly sprinkled with witchcraft and/or crack we devoured them all. The ice cream was exactly what I remember from an old school ice cream shop, not overly sweet, with a very creamy velvety texture.  Now the cons - the Mac and cheese just didn't do it for me, it felt very dry and grainy and didn't have a very cheesy taste for me.  I'll still try it again bc everything was so good I refuse to believe the mac couldn't be up there either.  While the staff were really friendly and great it definitely felt like they forgot about us in the dining room.  Nothing so bad that I would remove a star but more something that will be fixed once they get their bearings.  I'm looking forward to eating my way through the menu and I hope that everybody goes and shows this much needed addition to the area some love.

We stopped at Sparks BBQ for a late lunch/early dinner; I had the 2 meat dinner, my partner had the 1/2 rack of ribs. Both came with a side of baked beans and slaw (there were other choices like mac and cheese, etc) but we chose to upgrade to the broccoli-blue cheese slaw.

The portions were a good size for us--my meat choices were the 1/4 lb brisket with the original sauce and 1/4 lb. ribs.

The ribs, which had a dry rub, were flavorful, meaty and tender. I wouldn't hesitate to order them again. The brisket? Well, that was a near religious experience. To say the meat was tender would be to vastly understate it. The fats had melted perfectly into the meat, and the crust was exactly what I'd hoped it would be--smokey and crisp. The sauce didn't overwhelm the meat, but to my mind had a spicy sweetness that was well balanced by the tang of the just-right amount of vinegar. I will be judging any other brisket I eat in the future against Sparks, but I don't think I'll ever find better, I thought the smoke/meat/taste/texture was that good.

The beans--whoa. Dean Sparks was kind enough to share that the beans were his grandmothers recipe; they were excellent, and brought to mind my own experience of my grandmother cooking up baked beans in a bean pot with chunk of salt-pork melting on top. Brought me right back home 60 years ago.  Needless to say, I thought they were delicious.

It was the first time I've ever had broccoli slaw, and the first time I've ever had blue cheese in a slaw. It was, in my estimation, very good. I love blue cheese, so while I couldn't finish mine at the restaurant, I did take mine home (along with the beans I couldn't finish).

The restaurant has been at its present location for only about a week as of the time we visited (July 2, 2018); it looks as though it had been a bank in a previous life as what seems to be a safe vault was still there. The atmosphere was comfortable, the bathrooms clean and well appointed, the the service friendly.

We dropped by around 3ish and they were doing a brisk business. The pricing was competitive and we certainly feel as though we got our money's worth in both quality and quantity.

I do wish Dean and his staff the best of luck in their new location!

Had dinner here during a Christmas party and I have to say this is one is a newly minted gem. Being a party, we all kind of mixed and matched our selections, curiously slavering over our colleagues orders! No thing that I tried was less than amazing! For instance, the steak meal offering is much like the best that could be had in the highest end Peruvian and Argentinian steakhouses and reminded me very much of my erstwhile travels to such places. Food is cooked to a wide range of palettes, each rich and deep. Ingredients are of superlative quality.

Our party had the honor of speaking with chef Aaron who co-owns this place. He was discussing the nature of his establishment with our party. His philosophy is to encourage a collaborative environment and his sous chefs are encouraged to add their own personal touches. It is in this too that I think this place has a solid future. We stopped at Sparks BBQ for a late lunch/early dinner; I had the 2 meat dinner, my partner had the 1/2 rack of ribs. Both came with a side of baked beans and slaw (there were other choices like mac and cheese, etc) but we chose to upgrade to the broccoli-blue cheese slaw.

The portions were a good size for us--my meat choices were the 1/4 lb brisket with the original sauce and 1/4 lb. ribs.

The ribs, which had a dry rub, were flavorful, meaty and tender. I wouldn't hesitate to order them again. The brisket? Well, that was a near religious experience. To say the meat was tender would be to vastly understate it. The fats had melted perfectly into the meat, and the crust was exactly what I'd hoped it would be--smokey and crisp. The sauce didn't overwhelm the meat, but to my mind had a spicy sweetness that was well balanced by the tang of the just-right amount of vinegar. I will be judging any other brisket I eat in the future against Sparks, but I don't think I'll ever find better, I thought the smoke/meat/taste/texture was that good.

The beans--whoa. Dean Sparks was kind enough to share that the beans were his grandmothers recipe; they were excellent, and brought to mind my own experience of my grandmother cooking up baked beans in a bean pot with chunk of salt-pork melting on top. Brought me right back home 60 years ago.  Needless to say, I thought they were delicious.

It was the first time I've ever had broccoli slaw, and the first time I've ever had blue cheese in a slaw. It was, in my estimation, very good. I love blue cheese, so while I couldn't finish mine at the restaurant, I did take mine home (along with the beans I couldn't finish).

The atmosphere was comfortable, the bathrooms clean and well appointed, the the service friendly.

I had high hopes for Smoked on High, as any good optimistic exiled Texan. We know that Ohio is not in any way known for its barbeque, but then neither is South Florida, and the longer we were exiled there, the more good barbeque started to pop up (Smoke BBQ AND Bare Bones!! Mmm!!! I just had to unfollow Bare Bones on Instagram because they were posting too many luscious photos and seemings as they are way too far away now, I couldn't take it.)

We even have been to an excellent barbeque place in Phoenix, Little Miss BBQ. (Oh my!!!)

We got our hopes up partially because on our way into Columbus, moving truck in tow, we stumbled upon an excellent barbeque restaurant South of here, 7 Miles Smokehouse.

So back to Smoked on High. I have been wanting to come here before I even moved here. We are now missing our longlost famous KC Texan breakfast brisket tacos too long. So today was finally the day to try some Cbus brisket and if succesful, take some home.

We got some brisket of course. On the lovely lady's suggestion at the counter, we tried the spare ribs. We also tried the coleslaw and mac and cheese, and all three sauces.

So I went straight for the star of the show, the brisket. It was moist....big headstart plus! We did ask for the moist, but at some places, we are still handed tough meat. It had a nice flavor, a lovely smoke, especially in the fat. (Don't hate on me. I eat healthy most of the time. But sometimes it is time for fatty brisket, for what is great brisket without the fat?! Loyal Texan here...)  Hubby echoed many other reviewers in saying the meat didn't need a sauce. Score.

I usually am not a fan of spare ribs, but they had an excellent taste and were tender.

The mac and cheese was interesting, and boasted Thanksgiving flavors of something like rosemary and sage, very herby and not very cheesy. Hubby, connoisseur of mac and cheeses galour gave it the thumbs up.

I gave the coleslaw a thumbs up. It very much reminded me of the Texan coleslaws of my youth, which of course are the way coleslaws should taste. ;) It had a little extra kick of black pepper which was okay with me.

The sauces were all very interesting. There was a sweet, spicy, and mustard sauce. Surprisingly with the battle of Texan versus Carolina style raging strong, and the loyalists tasking sides, the Carolina mustard sauce is growing on me. Hubby, still skeptical, pronounced it one of the best mustard sauces he has had. We enjoyed all the sauces to some extent, although they weren't quite my favorite barbeque sauces. The mustard was my favorite of the three.

Hubby also tried a lemon acai soda which was very unique. It was nice and fun, but a little too sweet for my tastes, but then I don't drink sodas.

Lastly, service was EXCELLENT. The lady and gentleman were eager to please and pleasant.

So, yes, we left with a pound of brisket, and yes, we will be back.

I would probably pay a king's ransom for onion rings this good. Thankfully, I don't have to.

My philosophy of restaurant quality (also called the Onion Ring Standard) took some time to develop, but it first began here, at Saucy Dog's Barbecue in Jonesville, MI. I went there with a friend on a whim my freshman year of college, and decided to try the onion rings. I was blown away. Every time I have returned, I got the onion rings again and again. Simply put, these are the best onion rings I have ever had.

Presentation and Appearance - 4.5/5

When I think of an onion ring, there are usually at least two images that come to mind. The first is a thin, crispy, somewhat refined breaded strip of onion. The second type is like these onion rings: thick, a little rustic, and almost meaty in its appearance. The batter on the onion is smooth. The bubbles and crumbs that interrupt this smoothness lend to it an air of authenticity and charm, one that feels completely genuine. These onion rings feel like a perfect representation of the restaurant they come from, and that is to their strength.

I've docked half a point for presentation for two reasons. One, the size of the basket is just a bit too small. The mass of onion rings, while heaping and appetizing, has a tendency to spill out over the edges. Second, one onion ring was dropped off the basket and landed on the table just before they got to me. I ate it anyway, but it's not a great feeling.

Taste - 5/5

I don't even know where to begin. The batter was smooth, almost buttery and creamy, and delicious. There weren't a tremendous amount of seasonings in the batter, but the subtle flavor was a strength. The inner onion, meanwhile, was unique among onion rings. It was lightly sweated/sauteed prior to being dipped and fried. This gives it a light, not overpowering, flavor of onion throughout the ring. The batter and the onion meld in a delicious, slightly greasy, blend. They are a seamless, tasty whole.

A brief word on the accompanying dipping sauce. While often the sauce accompanying the onion ring is a poorly masked attempt to hide the poor flavor of an onion ring underneath a deluge of sauce, these sauce is the perfect complement to these onion rings. I would be hard pressed to find anything I'd rather dip these rings in. I have nothing bad to say about the taste of these rings.

Texture - 4.5/5

The texture on the batter is near perfection. Firm without being too hard, smooth without being too rich, it is a beautiful medium between all extremes. My only complaint comes with the irregular cooking of some of the breading (the bits and crumbs that disturb the overall smoothness), which were good, but not necessarily consistent with the rest of the onion ring.

The onion is interesting and unique, as noted in the taste section. The lightly sweated/sauteed onion could go disastrously wrong, with the onion becoming a mushy paste, and not firm enough to hold shape. This is not the case here. The sweating gives it just enough give to be soft and smooth, but it has sufficient firmness to hold the shape of the ring together. The best part of the texture is that there's just enough contrast between the batter and the onion to know there's a difference, but they complement each other perfectly.

Value - 5/5

A basket of these onion rings (as an appetizer) costs $5.49, and it is worth every penny. They aren't incredibly expensive (indeed, they're practically cheap by most restaurant standards), but you get what you pay for, and more. While the heaping basket has some presentation flaws, it lets the eater know they're getting a tremendous amount of delicious, thick, huge golden brown onion rings.

Total: 19/20

My wife had a "kinda" pulled pork dinner.  She's still drooling over the sauce.  I can't remember what she had for a side.  I was concentrating on my own meal.

I had a "really" catfish dinner.  My sides were slaw and collards.  Oh. And cornbread and coffee to drink.  The fish was perfect.  Two big, tender, and sweet filets with a crispy cornmeal coating.  Slaw was excellent, with a sort of vinegar dressing.  The greens were also quite fine, with plenty of meat seasoning.  The cornbread was pretty good -- sweeter than best, but YMMV.  The coffee takes us back to perfection.  I usually take moderate cream and sweetener, but it was *so good* that to put anything in it would downgrade it.

Plenty of parking within a block -- sometimes right in front.  Prices are moderate, portions are generous, the help is good.  The owner is often out in the dining area interacting pleasantly with guests.

Johnny V's is hands down the best BBQ I've ever eaten. The smoking, meat quality, and sauces were spot-on. (I've eaten a lot of BBQ in many places. I've lived in the Midwest, deep south and in Texas.)

I also need to comment on the Mac & Cheese and cornbread. Frankly, I expected them to invest in the quality of the meat, but both of these side items can also stand on their own. The cornbread is more like spoon bread muffins, rather than the heavy cornbread I've had before. (In fairness, I know everyone has different preferences, and some prefer less sweet. This is an excellent sweet cornbread.)

I'm not sure about the pasta itself, but the Mac & Cheese is made/baked in-house. Creamy cheese sauce with a baked cheese crust on top. It's excellent. (One possible "lighter" meal combo I'd recommend is the burnt ends and Mac & Cheese.)

Also, the manager and the owner made it a point to check on our meal and interact. This could be more difficult when the place gets busy; I appreciate they do this when they're able.

Appetizers started our meal. Pulled pork poutine on pork cracklings. Not to be confused with authentic Canadian poutine it is quite interesting and tasty. The Louisiana gumbo is a delicious cornucopia of seafood treats in a comfortably spicy gumbo.

For our entrees, the catfish was lightly breaded and deliciously flakey. The collard greens and cheesy mac delightful complimented. The jambalaya was full of shrimp, nicely spiced. Too much for us to finish and we weren't shy about asking for take home boxes!

While we were eating, a table of six ladies came in and all ordered the salmon special. One of the chefs, Tony, came out and sat with them for a minute. Turns out one of the ladies was his mother! He asked if we were enjoying ourselves and was dessert in the picture? He said the bread pudding was particularly good. Bread pudding is my favorite!!! Tony called our server over, asked to put a bread pudding on his tab and he went back into the kitchen to make it his special way. Delicious!!!! On top of this, apparently his mom's group had ordered an extra special which he wrapped up and insisted that we take home!

We are definitely coming back again!!!!!

The waffle fries were great. Not your typical style. These were hot, seasoned perfectly and they had a great crunch! Charred Brussel sprouts: ummm delicious! Great crisp with just enough maple. My daughter got the pulled pork sandwich and son got the pulled chicken bbq tacos.  The pulled pork had burnt ends, as it should. Never had them before and learned the vendor who makes them also makes them for local Mexican restaurants! Where have these been all my life?!

The thing to remember when you read a review from me place is I'm rating it on restaurants of like category. For example I might give a high end restaurant three stars but a local diner four. The high end restaurants food might have been better but I'm comparing it for the cost, service, etc that I'd expect from that type of restaurant. That being said, Homeboys is barely a eat in restaurant. They only have three or four tables inside (a couple of picnic tables outside too) and do a lot of takeout. You eat with plastic ware and its served in takeout containers. Having said all this if you love BBQ you must get there.

My suggestions are two things, though I've not had anything here to eat that I thought was bad. First, the pulled pork plate for about $8 comes with two big buns and enough pulled pork to make two huge sandwiches. I'm a big eater and can't finish it. You also get one side. Get the creamy coleslaw. It's some of the best ever, be aware though it has pineapple which adds a little sweetness.

Secondly there's a smoked 1/2 chicken dinner which comes with two sides. That also goes for around $8 and we'll fill you up. One last suggestion if your feeling a family they have a family meal option which will fill up the heartiest eaters.

If you are near Homeboys go here. If you need to drive an hour to eat her do it.

Blackwood BBQ serves some of the BEST bbq beef brisket in Chicago - and amazingly enough, during lunch hours in the loop (three locations. Michigan Ave & South Water, Lake and Wells, and Clinton and Madison)

You can order your brisket one of three ways: Fatty, Regular, or Lean. Brisket is a cut of beef that has a significant amount of fat to it, which can be a turn off for some. Fatty is basically the brisket sliced and served to you - nothing reduced. Lean is just that - no fat. and I believe (because I have order it this way) regular is a mix of fatty and lean; essentially, less fat.

On to the sauces...
Honestly, if you're getting brisket - don't add any sauce. The brisket is so good it can stand on its own.

But if you must know, Blackwood has a series of BBQ sauces you can choose to apply to your meats. I used to get the Chicago (sweet and spicy). You can also opt for Memphis (sweeter), Kansas City (spicier), North carolina (vinegar based), South Carolina (mustard based), or Alabama ("White sauce in the  celebrated Southern style"). But honestly - if you're getting brisket - don't add any sauce. The brisket is so good it can stand on its own.

<Additional> after having been there a number of times now, I can say this is my preferred bbq, outside of my home.  They cook things properly and to my preference...with a nice bark.  Most importantly,  the meat, fat, connective tissue is broke down correctly.  This doesn't mean everything always turns out perfect.   This is bbq and items fluctuate in quality,  to a degree.

They are also improving and changing things up. The pulled pork, that I mentioned below in my first review,  is now consistently broken down quite well.  For me, it's become one of their top items.  Although I still find myself ordering the brisket most times I go in there.  Sausage has gone through a few changes, each variation is enjoyable.   All in all, nice place</Additional info end>

Because bbq can be so tough to hold, I normally like to try a new bbq place three to four times before writing a review.   Turnover and learning your daily customer base is key.  For this reason I will never complain when a bbq restaurant tells me they're out of an item or if they pull an item if it had been sitting to long.

Setting aside a truly impressive resume from the Chef,  the first thing I noticed was that this place knows how to properly break down protein.   Belly, brisket and ribs were all beautifully cooked.  Bbq is so much about starting with a good product and applying proper technique, St1 accomplishes this.  The simplicity of the rub is appreciated.  The ribs were probably the best that I've had from a bbq joint to date.  My portion of pulled pork was taken a bit too far, but certainly still okay.  Corn bread was nice and unique...it gave me the impression of a version of polenta cornbread,  really tasty!

I could go on about a proper bark, nicely rendered fat, etc, etc.  Oh, the in house sausages are well done as well.  Finer grind than I would have suspected,  but a welcome  interpretation.   The sausage was well made, well stuffed, and nicely cooked.

For instance, the steak meal offering is much like the best that could be had in the highest end Peruvian and Argentinian steakhouses and reminded me very much of my erstwhile travels to such places. Food is cooked to a wide range of palettes, each rich and deep. Ingredients are of superlative quality.

Our party had the honor of speaking with chef Aaron who co-owns this place. He was discussing the nature of his establishment with our party. His philosophy is to encourage a collaborative environment and his sous chefs are encouraged to add their own personal touches. It is in this too that I think this place has a solid future. Novelty and quality should be hallmarks of this tavern!

The area of town it is in also telling. It is an area of town near the OSU campus that has a bit of a rough edge, but with a new additions such as Rooks, that area may be an anchor for much desired vitalization.

TL:DR Rooks is a campus area ingenue that will stand the test of time. Delicious, succulent and varied! It is a must try.

PS: Even though vegans and vegetarians can by rather enjoyably, Rooks is a carnivore's ball!

I went for dinner. We grabbed some mac and cheese, pulled pork, and ribs to go. I wanted brisket, but they were out.

The mac was good. It wasn't amazing, but it was good and I'll definitely order it again. The ribs were okay. It wasn't tough, but it wasn't melt in your mouth. It didn't even really pull away from the bone that well. The flavor was good, and with the mac it was enough food for me (and I'm a 200lb guy who hadn't eaten all day). The pulled pork was awesome. Plenty of bark, great smoke flavor, good texture. It didn't really need sauce.

Speaking of sauce, we had Kansas City sauce and South Carolina (?) sauce. The Kansas City sauce had a good, subtle spice to it and the slightest bit of sweetness. It had a little more tomato present than I would have preferred, but it was all around a solid sauce. The Carolina Sauce (it could have been the NC, I dunno) was a great balance of mustard and vinegar flavors with a little BBQ spice mixed in. It had a nice tang to it that played really well with the BBQ spices. No sweetness to be found, no tomato flavor present, though it looked like it could have still been an ingredient (the other Carolina sauce seemed more like a straight vinegar, this was a little red and a little thicker). I enjoyed both sauces, but lean more towards the Carolina one.

As I said above, serving sizes were good. The mac was probably a 6-8oz serving, which was plenty. The ribs were four ribs with a good amount of meat, weighed out at a little more than half a pound. The pulled pork was about spot on for half a pound (they weigh it in front of you). My wife eight about 3/4 of both her mac and the pulled pork along with the slice of included white bread. I ate the ribs and all of the mac and bread, and felt satisfied. I finished off the remaining pork, and feel stuffed. The portions might be tricky if you don't overindulge, they will likely be too much for one serving, but not enough to split or save for a second meal. If you are willing to push yourself a little, and it didn't take much convincing, then you should have no problem finishing it all and being perfectly content.

Inside it is pretty barebones. There is corrugated metal on the walls, a giant chalk board with the menu, and a large counter place your order and watch them carve it up and weigh it out. They were processing payments off of an iPhone with Square, but I'd imagine that will change after they get a bit more situated. There are long picnic style tables for eating in, a small soda fountain, and pumps with the various sauces.

I can't compare it to Prized Pig, I unfortunately never got to go. I can say that the food is good and I will definitely be going back somewhat regularly. It's worth making a special trip to check out, and I think once you give it a try you won't have any problem with swinging by whenever you are in the neighborhood.

This was our first visit to the Plantation Supper Club and it was a very enjoyable experience.  I have to be honest, we've been driving by for years and maybe it's a case of just being too familiar of a landmark at Hwy 51 and 70E and never really being motivated to stop...they really exceeded my expectations and that's why I'd urge you to give the Plantation a visit.  We love Wisconsin Supper Clubs and with that said, The Plantation certainly qualifies as a historic, iconic Northwoods Supper Club.  From the minute we walked in, we were enjoying ourselves - from the "throwback" blue and white bar to the friendly greeting when we arrived - we knew this was going to be a good visit.  Anna greeted us at the bar and fixed us a couple of Wisconsin classics - Brandy Old Fashioned.  We tried some of the sharp cheddar and horseradish cheese spreads as we learned more about the history of Plantation and the Woodruff area.  Candy served as our hostess and our server - she is a hoot.  She was professional, entertaining, and efficient - all great qualities that contributed to a wonderful first visit.  I tried the Prime rib and scallops and "she" tried the scallops with a baked potato - both entrees were served to perfection and were delicious.  Before dinner was served, Candy brought Hors d'oeuvres - deep fried chicken wings and toasted swiss cheese melts - seemed like an odd combination but they were excellent.  Next we tried the seafood bisque - not too heavy, not too rich - well seasoned - very good.  As I was paying our bill, Candy invited us to tour the kitchen and the entire facility, she mentioned that she had been in the food service industry many years and she has never worked at a restaurant that is so impeccably clean - although we didn't have time to accept her invitation, I really appreciated her genuine pride in the restaurant and it shows in her service - kudos.  Here's the interesting thing - the reason we finally visited the Plantation Supper Club was a friend, who is a local realtor, mentioned how much he enjoyed their Ahi Tuna steak and how impeccably clean the place is, "you could eat of the kitchen floor" he exclaimed...his recommendation brought us in and the Plantation's hometown hospitality and delicious food will bring us back - perfect combination - thank you for the enjoyable evening.

The prices are reasonable, the portions are plentiful and the service was very friendly. The menu has a nice selection of appetizers and sandwiches which are all made with skill and attention.

We ordered the fried pickles as an appetizer, and they were cut thin like french fries. This was great since you got more of the seasoning in each bite. Very good. When we've had these at other locations, they typically come with a dipping sauce, and I'm not sure if they forgot to bring it or they don't offer it with the fried pickles. We didn't miss it though because they were breaded and seasoned so well.

Next, we had sandwiches including cod and the corned beef Reuben. They were all good. The corned beef Reuben was stacked high with chunky and sliced corned beef and not the typical deli sandwich meat you get at some places.  It was very tender and flavorful. Will definitely get that again. For our first visit under new ownership, they did well, and we plan to visit again.

Finally checked out Sublime Smoke after first reading a newspaper review over a year ago. Specializing in barbecue and smoked meats, my wife and I were excited to sample several different things from the menu.

When you enter Sublime Smoke, you order at the front counter and then take a seat, where your food will be delivered to you. After ordering our food, we made a trip to the bar to check out their great selection of craft beers on tap. They had 16 varieties on tap (and many others in cans or bottles, including domestic beers), so we each decided to get four small flights for $5 so we could sample several different kinds.

From there, we found a seat outside, where there were approximately eight wooden picnic tables set up under a covered patio with overhead fans. Less than 15 minutes after ordering, our food was ready.  Because there were so many tasty-sounding options, we decided to try several things and split them.

The pork loin back ribs were very meaty, with just enough fat to add flavor. They came with a dry rub and the house BBQ sauce. The crispy smoked chicken wings were equally good. Crisp on the outside and tender on the outside, these wings were full of smoked flavor, without being overpowering. I love shrimp, but I’d never had grits before. After sampling the shrimp and grits here, this won’t be the last time I have grits! They were cheesy and moist, and not lumpy at all. The shrimp were plentiful and flavorful.

For our sides, we got small orders of the baked mac and cheese, collard greens, and loaded baked beans. My wife ate all of the collard greens and loaded baked beans before I could try them, and said they were outstanding! You could tell the baked mac and cheese was homemade and was appropriately cheesy, without being too much.

Overall, our meal was excellent, and everything was fairly priced. I can’t wait to visit this spot again in the near future!

Warm weather and BBQ go hand in hand. I have been wanting to branch out and try the various BBQ restaurants in Cleveland, so last night I met up with some friends at Woodstock for dinner.

Inside is a very eclectic collection of decorations, and is heavy on wood paneling/pieces of art. Lots of Ohio themed items, which is really cool. With such nice weather, we sat out on the patio. The bartender and servers were very pleasant, and even brought out cushions for our chairs (the wind had been blowing them away earlier, so they were kept inside).

To start off I went with the Stuffed Smoked Jalapenos. They were a nice take on Jalapeno Poppers, had some spice, and overall a good smokey flavor. Capping it off I ordered the 2 meat/1 side dish. I opted for Brisket, Ribs, Mac n' Cheese, and added an order of Cole Slaw.

The Brisket was tender, albeit a little dry. I didn't get much flavor from the rub, but the fatty parts were really good. Mac N' Cheese was decent, but the sauce was a little gritty. Cole Slaw was solid. Creamier than I usually like, but lots of celery seed which I fancy. Corn Bread was fluffy and sweet. My favorite part was the Ribs, which were really tender and had a good amount of rub on them. The rub was thick with a good sweetness to it. I could pull the bone clean out, which was really nice.

It feels like they are trying to blend multiple BBQ styles, which can work, but may take some time. I think if they narrow down their craft some, they are on the cusp of being an elite BBQ restaurant in Cleveland. All in all, they are a good place with really friendly people. Stop by and get yourselves some BBQ!

You're also hit with the smell of trapped exhaust gas.  Not sure if that was natural gas, propane or what.  The bar was beautiful, as well as the staff.  Warm, friendly, and enthusiastic.  Beware of the wine list.  When you're looking at pricing say for a Malbec, there are two prices listed.  One is per glass, and the other per HALF bottle.  I've never seen this before.  Usually the two prices were per glass/bottle.  So for a glass you're paying $9, $21 per half bottle, and $42 for a full bottle.  I was shocked.  We were seated in the main dinning room, and immediately decided that the open area was too loud.  Also, we were seated at a table with dirty dishes still on it, and the lady who seated us left some dirty glasses on our table.  The lounge was way more relaxing.  We ordered the ribeye at $45 per plate.  It was great, but it wasn't outstanding.  The flavor was a little bland.  It came with four spears of asparagus, and potato.  We loved our waiter, and everyone there.  It was a nice experience.  In the future we will stick with Hayden's Crossing in Wilmington for the best ribeye ever.

It was smoky, trim, slightly dry but nothing that a dip in the au ju or homemade bbq sauce couldn't fix. It was definitely worth the trip. Darlene greeted me as I came through the door. As it wasn't very busy I had my choice of seating. I get a table near the front corner for a great view of the layout to this College town sports bar. And let's be honest. That's what this is. With no less then 6 TVs visible to my seat. Video poker/slots/gambling screen in the corner at the end of the bar hardwood chairs and table tops with a high gloss resin finish this very easily could have been any gastropub in any town that has a community college or higher campus nearby. The atmosphere is what it is. Now I picked this place because my coworkers rave about it. I let Darlene know it was my first time there and she gave me plenty of room and time to take pictures and mull over the menu even though I did that online days in advance  to ha e an idea of what I was going into. I was on a time crunch so today I ordered only the mini nachos with brisket and the cheese curds. At $7 the curds could have been a larger portion size. After talking with Darlene I found that they only do mozzarella and not cheddar or a good mix of the two. They were not overly battered or overly thick on the cheese. Darlene came to my table and spent a few minutes explaining the difference sauces I had available to me and how they were made. She also pointed out the two that would be preloaded on my nachos. The nachos with the pieces of chopped brisket where a fair size for the price. These inhouse made chips are covered in toppings. Not one chip was bare. The mixture of the cheeses two sauces and other accoutrements causes more wetting of the palate and is well worth the time and money. I made a point to visit the restrooms to give them a look over and I am happy to report neat, clean, and organized. No mess. Nothing on the floors. My next venture will delve into burgers and wraps.

I’m going to start off this review by saying I am a little biased towards Hickory River Smokehouse. I have been there four times and I really like it. I know there are the naysayers out there that say “Oh this place is better” or “This place is the best” and blah blah blah. I have had BBQ in KC and Memphis and Georgia and Texas. I am not trying to say this place is the best in the world but it is solid. They have a variety of really good BBQ and sides.

The Pulled Pork is great. It has won multiple State Fair titles. I also like the Beef Brisket and the Baby Back Ribs. You can’t go wrong with either the Hot or Mild Sauces. The undisputed Hickory River Smokehouse Champion is The Cue Shoe. This dish will knock you out into a food coma. I am a big guy and I struggle with this mountain of culinary love. The foundation is Texas Toast then a heap of Pulled Pork soaked in your choice of sauce. Next they top it with French Fries and smother it in a delicious white cheese sauce.

The sides are also good. I have had the Mashed Potatoes, Sweet Corn Bread and the Mac & Cheese. If I could give them one knock it would be the Baked Beans. I just don’t like them and think it is probably a matter of preference, but you may love them.

The only location I have been to is the Peoria spot. I think the interior is appropriate and have had nothing but good service there. From my experiences the staff has been great.

According to the Big Food Jerk.

If you want delicious BBQ at reasonable prices and good service then I highly recommend The Hickory River Smokehouse and Oh Yeah you gotta try the Cue Shoe!

I ended up at That BBQ Joint (TBJ) by happenstance after my efforts to visit a different restaurant were foiled by my inability to find a parking space.  But my luck was not all bad that day as both the food and service at TBJ exceeded my expectations.

There is a definite black and white theme to the restaurant interior.  The interior walls have a fresh coat of institutional white paint, with black trim around the doors and windows.  The menus are written on whiteboards with black ink and the food comes on a black & white checkerboard patterned paper liner.  The large front windows allow for waves of natural light to stream into the interior and allow diners keep tabs on the action taking place on Willy Street.  While the building has seen better days, the new occupants have cleaned it up nicely.

Since TBJ does not have waiter service, I had limited interaction with the staff.  Nonetheless, all the staff members I interacted with were courteous, polite and helpful.  As a first time visitor, my order taker offered helpful suggestions when I mentioned I was visiting for the first time.  He also checked in to see what I thought of my sandwich which doesn't always happen at counter service restaurants.  Throughout my time at TBJ, this employee was constantly tidying out the dining area and checking the condiment supply levels when there was a break in the somewhat steady flow of lunch time customers.

I elected to go with the Thursday special, the TBJ Cubano sandwich (pulled pork, ham, mustard, pickles and a pressed, well-buttered French roll). Mad props to the kitchen for their fantastic griddle work on the French roll as every bite yielded a satisfying crunch.  The pulled pork component provided plenty of porky deliciousness.  The Achilles heel of the sandwich was the ocean of generic yellow mustard slathered onto the sandwich.  With a little better balance, this could be a top echelon sandwich in town with an amazing stable of sandwich offerings.

Bonus content: TBJ sells bottles of their sauce for $8.

After this positive first impression, a return visit to TBJ is certainly in my future.  The wonderful aroma of smoked meats wafting through the restaurant during my first visit has me eager to try there more traditional BBQ offerings of smoked brisket, ribs, pulled pork and smoked chicken.

The brisket sandwich is SMALL, I'm used to going to a bbq place and if I'm paying $9 bucks for a sandwich, I expect it to be good for one and big for $9.... The brisket itself is decently smoky but it is very dry, and the portion I don't even think is /was a 1/4lb. All the sauces are meh as I tried all three. The mustard is deccent if you like mustard sauce, the spicy to me tastes best of all three, the house sauce just tastes strange as it has ALOT of terragon in it. Maybe thats what is throwing me off as I am not used to terragon in BBQ anywhere Ive had BBQ, and Ive been to alot of joints. The ciabatta roll is a nice touch, but if you think about the size of a standard roll you can picture the amount of meat I'm talking about when I say it definitely did not overtake the little ciabatta roll.

The garlic fries we're definitely the pinnacle of my experience, flavorful, perfectly salted and fried to a crunchy awesomeness. The fried green tomatoes on the other hand....  I have absolutely no idea what the other person was talking about, although decent they are nothing to write home about. First of all, so you know...  You only get THREE slices of tomato (with a side of goat cheese for dipping ) for SIX dollars. I don't know about you, but to me, I feel hoodwinked, led astray and run amuck for paying $2 per slice of tomato. Although the service and atmosphere are nice, food is key so I simply cannot recommend this place seeing all of the other great BBQ joints in the city. Maybe a good addition to the area but just not for me.

If I could, I would actually give Sharks BBQ 3.5 stars. Great customer service, it only takes 1-5 mins to receive your order, and it is reasonably priced.

Sharks BBQ is (what I define) a "fast casual BBQ restaurant." This means, it is NOT a formal "sit down" restaurant. At Sharks BBQ you wait in line, they take your order, you receive your order (it takes 1-5 mins for you to receive your order), and you can eat it there or take it to-go. There have been plenty of fast causal BBQ restaurants popping up all over the area.

What I love about Sharks BBQ is their amazing customer service, the employees are super friendly, they are great people to talk to. Another thing I love is how quick it takes for you to receive your order, which is another advantage of the emerging "fast casual" BBQ restaurants. Lastly, my favorite thing about Sharks BBQ is their pricing. Their items are all very reasonably priced. I personally got their brisket and the ribs. I would recommend those two items.

What I didn't like about Sharks BBQ was the lack of variety of BBQ sauces, and the food is pretty good, but obviously not as good as a traditional "sit down" BBQ restaurant. This is expected because you get your order in such a timely manner (Again, it takes 1-5 mins to receive your order).

I would recommend Sharks BBQ if you are looking for a BBQ fix and you are limited with time. Otherwise, if you have the time, I would highly recommend a sit down BBQ restaurant.

I took off the peppers because I was not sure if they were spicy/hot pepper's,  and did not want to chance it. (Just wasn't a day to eat something spicy.) However, the Hotdog was FIRE, LIT, Delicious, So So good... and would highly recommend trying it if you are not a fan of Chicago style, because this makes some of the traditional Chicago style hotdogs that you find in Chicago, or even Portillo's look down right sad... it so worth the try and I was Surprised by just how yummy it was. The french fries, were a traditional crinkle cut/deep fried, and just the right of cooking, not under done and mushy or overcooked and dried up or super crunchy. Just the perfect salt to fried ratio that eating them plain was on point with my hotdog. I am not a huge ranch dressing dipper for chicken tenders or french fries (cuz my daughter always eats like that) but the ranch was banging too. It was not thick or drippy and just the right amount of flavor, that I actually even tried it on my fries, and hotdog. My daughter said she loves the chicken tenders,  they were great size and portion, not the really narrow tenderloin strips but a good 4 oz. portion about for each tender. Crispy, and moist chicken cooked right with No undercooked Or overcooked rubbery look like some places restaurant or fast food places in the surrounding area of town. My daughter ordered because someone at her work had bought food their and she said they looked good, and she had to try them. I asked her if she would order again, she said Absolutely.  The sundae was vanilla icecream with strawberry drizzle and whip cream, my daughter has order that before and she said she never disappointed,  it yummy. It a soft serve icecream I believe. I tried it and I am not a strawberry icecream kind of person, but I agree... was very good. I ordered the chocolate malt and I loved it... good chocolate taste and thickness for a malt style. I did not get to try the Chocolate cake slices, but my children loved it so much that they said it is similar to the Portillo's chocolate cake, (it looked very moist on the cake part, and the chocolate frosting looked creamy and thick sliced, double layer, richness that I am not even needing to drive all the way to Oswego for it... Smokey's is the spot!!! I wish I had been here years ago. I only came in once years (6) before to ask about fund raising donations for a gift basket when my daughter was in cheerleading and they even donated gift certificates back then. Honestly,  I am looking forward to going back and trying other option's on the menu. I think what through me off was the name, but now Smokey's it is for a Delicious, Fast, Friendly,  Convenient meal of goodness. Thank you Smokey's for the Great Food and Service. I didn't give it 5 stars because I did not order anything to complicated,  and it just my first time really eating their food, so I will update this post once I try more! 😁 Next time I will take pictures.

Mabel's BBQ is located along East 4th Street in downtown Cleveland. Mabel's contains a 2 level dining area. There are steps going to both levels as well as a ramp for the lower level where the kitchen and restrooms are located. There are several tables which can accommodate a group of approximately 14 people.

FOOD: 4/5
Mabel's BBQ slogan is "Eat More Meat." Expect large meat portions.

Mabel's BBQ offers a limited menu of food items. The food is tasty and well worth the visit. However, the food items are rather pricey by the time you order a sandwich, side and beverage. A cheap visit for those 3 things would be approximately $20. With an alcoholic beverage, expect to pay more.

SERVICE: 5/5
The waiter was very attentive to our group of 14 and made sure everyone received their food in a timely manner and checked on beverages frequently. He was aware when someone else came in to join our group.

RESTROOMS: 3/5
There were two independent restrooms located on the bottom level. There is often a line of people waiting to use the restrooms. They were older and not near as nice as the dining area.

PARKING:
Mabel's BBQ is located on East 4th Street; which is a walking street only. Park in a city lot, garage or along the street.

BOTTOM LINE:
Mabel's food was tasty and enjoyable. If you are giving up meat for Lent, this is not the place to come for food.

Read an article about PrimeBBQ opening up in Monroe. I am a Texas transplant and like most Texans, I consider myself a BBQ afficonado...I've been to most of the local eateries and thought I'd check this one out. I took my wife and walked in to bustling restaurant...smell of smoke and the sounds of plates and silverware filled the air...the place was packed, so we decided to take the food home and eat...ordered the Sampler Platter to try as much of the menu as possible. We got home and popped the aluminum lid off to find that everything was covered in BBQ sauce. Strike 1. The food was decent and may have been good but the sweet flavor of the sauce covered up any flavor of the smoke. Rule #1 to BBQ is don't hide the flavor of the meat...let the customer decide how much sauce (if any) they want on their meat. Brisket was very fatty and not a charred fatty. Riblets were good, ribs were good and the chicken was good...the pulled pork was very good...all of these may have been great but so hard to tell...I'm giving a 4 star because I could tell that underneath all the sauce was a pretty darn good smoke meat...SUGGESTIONS: 1. Don't slather your meat in sauce, allow the customer to decide. 2. Allow your brisket to char a little bit...bark is good...fat is good...gristle is not. Overall, good job PrimeBBQ for being brand new, great freshman effort..can't wait to get back and see how they've matured! OH! Banana Pudding was Great!

Great Burnt Ends and Rib Tips as well.  Also, I must mention the Mac & Cheese…you gotta have some good sides at a BBQ joint. My only complaint was that they brought out the drinks in tiny, child size glass jars. Filled up to the top with ice, these jars held less than 10 oz of liquid, maybe 8. I felt like I was back in Germany, where a tiny Coke cost almost 5 marks and giant beer cost three. Maybe things have changed since then but I digress.

When I asked for a regular glass they said that they only served alcoholic drinks in those. I said a pint-size glass would be appropriate, but she wasn't allowed to give me a Dr. Pepper in a pint glass. So she brought me my drink refill in two of the tiny little jelly jars. I felt like a kid at a party when all of the regular glasses had run out.

I'm absolutely certain I'm not the only person who has asked for this. It's definitely a Butch masculine restaurant and I'm not the only person who came in at lunch time and wasn't drinking alcohol. I wouldn't have given my 11 year old boy a glass that small.

It's a stupid problem, but I think this is an example of where the customer isn't right, it's corporate that's right. Well hear me now Smokey Bones corporate, it's a stupid idea to serve soft drinks in tiny glasses next to plates of food so big that you can't finish them. Listen to your customer base and move your customers from the Kiddy table.

I get that you're going for the Southern Vibe with mason jars and handles on them, but I want to enjoy my drink without having to constantly ask for a refill. And if you're picturing an idyllic time with neighbors at a barbecue or sipping lemonade out of mason jars on a southern porch in the hot summer somewhere in Georgia, those were full size mason jars not the tiny jelly jars you guys have.

So save those tiny little glass jars for the kids cups and contact your restaurant supplier now. I might be the only one who is saying it but most of your customers are thinking it or feeling it unconsciously... It's different and not in a good way. You could spend 300 bucks and have all the glasses you would ever need. It's one thing to be unique and yummy and special, and another thing to be out of Step.

Stopped here on Memorial Day and was not disappointed. Not a large menu, about a dozen choices. We ordered the half rack of ribs, and the dinner entrée portion of the Pulled Pork. The pulled pork was good, but there isn't anything that comes with them, so don't be surprised when you get a bare pile of pulled pork. Maybe I'm ignorant to the way you are supposed to get it, but that seemed weird to me, and is half the reason why I took one star off. The ribs are the real star. Smoky, juicy, tender, dry rubbed, and a generous portion to boot. We split the ribs, and took most of pulled pork home for sandwiches the next day. There was a house barbecue sauce on the table that was sweet, with a prominent raisin flavor, and is the other factor for a four star instead of a five. They offer a full bar, with domestic beer on tap and in bottles, as well as draft choices from our beautiful beer state. Definitely looking forward to stopping back in and checking out more of their offerings soon!

Warm weather and BBQ go hand in hand. I have been wanting to branch out and try the various BBQ restaurants in Cleveland, so last night I met up with some friends at Woodstock for dinner.

Inside is a very eclectic collection of decorations, and is heavy on wood paneling/pieces of art. Lots of Ohio themed items, which is really cool. With such nice weather, we sat out on the patio. The bartender and servers were very pleasant, and even brought out cushions for our chairs (the wind had been blowing them away earlier, so they were kept inside).

To start off I went with the Stuffed Smoked Jalapenos. They were a nice take on Jalapeno Poppers, had some spice, and overall a good smokey flavor. Capping it off I ordered the 2 meat/1 side dish. I opted for Brisket, Ribs, Mac n' Cheese, and added an order of Cole Slaw.

The Brisket was tender, albeit a little dry. I didn't get much flavor from the rub, but the fatty parts were really good. Mac N' Cheese was decent, but the sauce was a little gritty. Cole Slaw was solid. Creamier than I usually like, but lots of celery seed which I fancy. Corn Bread was fluffy and sweet. My favorite part was the Ribs, which were really tender and had a good amount of rub on them. The rub was thick with a good sweetness to it. I could pull the bone clean out, which was really nice.

It feels like they are trying to blend multiple BBQ styles, which can work, but may take some time. I think if they narrow down their craft some, they are on the cusp of being an elite BBQ restaurant in Cleveland. All in all, they are a good place with really friendly people. Stop by and get yourselves some BBQ!

Bar looked to have a nice selection of beers as well.

Seeing as such I hate to say anything negative about the place however I feel the previous reviews are a bit misleading. The brisket sandwich is SMALL, I'm used to going to a bbq place and if I'm paying $9 bucks for a sandwich, I expect it to be good for one and big for $9.... The brisket itself is decently smoky but it is very dry, and the portion I don't even think is /was a 1/4lb. All the sauces are meh as I tried all three. The mustard is deccent if you like mustard sauce, the spicy to me tastes best of all three, the house sauce just tastes strange as it has ALOT of terragon in it. Maybe thats what is throwing me off as I am not used to terragon in BBQ anywhere Ive had BBQ, and Ive been to alot of joints. The ciabatta roll is a nice touch, but if you think about the size of a standard roll you can picture the amount of meat I'm talking about when I say it definitely did not overtake the little ciabatta roll.

The garlic fries we're definitely the pinnacle of my experience, flavorful, perfectly salted and fried to a crunchy awesomeness. The fried green tomatoes on the other hand....  I have absolutely no idea what the other person was talking about, although decent they are nothing to write home about. First of all, so you know...  You only get THREE slices of tomato (with a side of goat cheese for dipping ) for SIX dollars. I don't know about you, but to me, I feel hoodwinked, led astray and run amuck for paying $2 per slice of tomato. Although the service and atmosphere are nice, food is key so I simply cannot recommend this place seeing all of the other great BBQ joints in the city. Maybe a good addition to the area but just not for me.

These tender, smokey pieces of meaty pig ribs have me questioning if heaven is beyond life or an extension of the good things of this life. Seriously, they are THAT good. So good, I drove 20 minutes ahead of thunderstorms and tornadoes to get Sunday dinner.

I called in advance to confirm price and availability. Sunday special: $13.80 for a FULL slab!  This is nearly half the price of a local competitor. ODM was well worth the additional 15 minute drive, in one direction.

As I parked in my driveway, I was weak and delirious from hunger, inspired by the smokey scent of the meat. When inside, I quickly opened the Styrofoam lid to reveal beautifully cut slabs of meat pulling away from tips of bone. I could not resist tasting a small end piece, even before it was sauced.

I felt my eyes roll back; my lungs over-inflating with a gasp. A husky flavor say at the back of my mouth. Warm, moist particles coated my tongue, and I became light-headed. I noticed a smooth, silky texture form at the roof of my mouth, it's volume increasing rapidly. I gained my senses to discover I was eating without chewing. These tender ribs were literally melting in my mouth!

I suffered through the fifteen minutes it took to make side dishes and warm the ribs to dinner-time temperature. Once done, with sauce added to increase my delight, the feast was on!  So undisciplined was I that I consumed too much too quickly. Belly-busting fullness overtook me at four bones. How many had I eaten without the sauce? Who cares!  I was done; waddling to my bed became mission one.

Next time, I'll buy my sides there!

When you walk in here, it's different.  Straight ahead of you is the kitchen, to the left bathrooms, and a counter/gift shop looking area, and to your right the lounge.  No signage.  There was a wait for a table, but instead of pagers, they ask for your cell phone number.  As soon as you walk into the lounge, it's dimly lit like a rustic lodge, quiet, and upscale.  You're also hit with the smell of trapped exhaust gas.  Not sure if that was natural gas, propane or what.  The bar was beautiful, as well as the staff.  Warm, friendly, and enthusiastic.  Beware of the wine list.  When you're looking at pricing say for a Malbec, there are two prices listed.  One is per glass, and the other per HALF bottle.  I've never seen this before.  Usually the two prices were per glass/bottle.  So for a glass you're paying $9, $21 per half bottle, and $42 for a full bottle.  I was shocked.  We were seated in the main dinning room, and immediately decided that the open area was too loud.  Also, we were seated at a table with dirty dishes still on it, and the lady who seated us left some dirty glasses on our table.  The lounge was way more relaxing.  We ordered the ribeye at $45 per plate.  It was great, but it wasn't outstanding.  The flavor was a little bland.  It came with four spears of asparagus, and potato.  We loved our waiter, and everyone there.  It was a nice experience.  In the future we will stick with Hayden's Crossing in Wilmington for the best ribeye ever.

Maybe add some beans to help keep food costs down and add variety to the bowl. The cheesy cauliflower wasn't special, but excellent. Beware of the wine list.  When you're looking at pricing say for a Malbec, there are two prices listed.  One is per glass, and the other per HALF bottle.  I've never seen this before.  Usually the two prices were per glass/bottle.  So for a glass you're paying $9, $21 per half bottle, and $42 for a full bottle.  I was shocked.  We were seated in the main dinning room, and immediately decided that the open area was too loud.  Also, we were seated at a table with dirty dishes still on it, and the lady who seated us left some dirty glasses on our table.  The lounge was way more relaxing.  We ordered the ribeye at $45 per plate.  It was great, but it wasn't outstanding.  The flavor was a little bland.  It came with four spears of asparagus, and potato.  We loved our waiter, and everyone there.  It was a nice experience.  In the future we will stick with Hayden's Crossing in Wilmington for the best ribeye ever.

My only complaint was that they brought out the drinks in tiny, child size glass jars. Filled up to the top with ice, these jars held less than 10 oz of liquid, maybe 8. I felt like I was back in Germany, where a tiny Coke cost almost 5 marks and giant beer cost three. Maybe things have changed since then but I digress.

When I asked for a regular glass they said that they only served alcoholic drinks in those. I said a pint-size glass would be appropriate, but she wasn't allowed to give me a Dr. Pepper in a pint glass. So she brought me my drink refill in two of the tiny little jelly jars. I felt like a kid at a party when all of the regular glasses had run out.

I'm absolutely certain I'm not the only person who has asked for this. It's definitely a Butch masculine restaurant and I'm not the only person who came in at lunch time and wasn't drinking alcohol. I wouldn't have given my 11 year old boy a glass that small.

It's a stupid problem, but I think this is an example of where the customer isn't right, it's corporate that's right. Well hear me now Smokey Bones corporate, it's a stupid idea to serve soft drinks in tiny glasses next to plates of food so big that you can't finish them. Listen to your customer base and move your customers from the Kiddy table.

I get that you're going for the Southern Vibe with mason jars and handles on them, but I want to enjoy my drink without having to constantly ask for a refill. And if you're picturing an idyllic time with neighbors at a barbecue or sipping lemonade out of mason jars on a southern porch in the hot summer somewhere in Georgia, those were full size mason jars not the tiny jelly jars you guys have.

So save those tiny little glass jars for the kids cups and contact your restaurant supplier now. I might be the only one who is saying it but most of your customers are thinking it or feeling it unconsciously... It's different and not in a good way. You could spend 300 bucks and have all the glasses you would ever need. It's one thing to be unique and yummy and special, and another thing to be out of Step.

I thought I had written this review already, but  it seems that I didn't. I took my girlfriend here for our third date back in September, 2020. Every time I try a new smokehouse/BBQ I always get their brisket because that is the standard I judge a smokehouse/BBQ house by how they make their brisket.

The Cheese curds were fantastic... again.... Cheese Curds. The brisket was good. it was nice and tender, pulled apart.  The flavor was okay, it didn't have that rich smoky flavor one would prefer from smoked meat. For sides I had the home-made bacon bleu potato salad. and the home-made Macaroni salad.  Both were really good. That home-made bacon bleu potato salad alone would keep me coming back... as long as you like bleu cheese and potato salad.

I felt like I was back in Germany, where a tiny Coke cost almost 5 marks and giant beer cost three. Maybe things have changed since then but I digress.

When I asked for a regular glass they said that they only served alcoholic drinks in those. I said a pint-size glass would be appropriate, but she wasn't allowed to give me a Dr. Pepper in a pint glass. So she brought me my drink refill in two of the tiny little jelly jars. I felt like a kid at a party when all of the regular glasses had run out.

I'm absolutely certain I'm not the only person who has asked for this. It's definitely a Butch masculine restaurant and I'm not the only person who came in at lunch time and wasn't drinking alcohol. I wouldn't have given my 11 year old boy a glass that small.

It's a stupid problem, but I think this is an example of where the customer isn't right, it's corporate that's right. Well hear me now Smokey Bones corporate, it's a stupid idea to serve soft drinks in tiny glasses next to plates of food so big that you can't finish them. Listen to your customer base and move your customers from the Kiddy table.

I get that you're going for the Southern Vibe with mason jars and handles on them, but I want to enjoy my drink without having to constantly ask for a refill. And if you're picturing an idyllic time with neighbors at a barbecue or sipping lemonade out of mason jars on a southern porch in the hot summer somewhere in Georgia, those were full size mason jars not the tiny jelly jars you guys have.

So save those tiny little glass jars for the kids cups and contact your restaurant supplier now. I might be the only one who is saying it but most of your customers are thinking it or feeling it unconsciously... It's different and not in a good way. You could spend 300 bucks and have all the glasses you would ever need. It's one thing to be unique and yummy and special, and another thing to be out of Step.

To start off I went with the Stuffed Smoked Jalapenos. They were a nice take on Jalapeno Poppers, had some spice, and overall a good smokey flavor. Capping it off I ordered the 2 meat/1 side dish. I opted for Brisket, Ribs, Mac n' Cheese, and added an order of Cole Slaw.

The Brisket was tender, albeit a little dry. I didn't get much flavor from the rub, but the fatty parts were really good. Mac N' Cheese was decent, but the sauce was a little gritty. Cole Slaw was solid. Creamier than I usually like, but lots of celery seed which I fancy. Corn Bread was fluffy and sweet. My favorite part was the Ribs, which were really tender and had a good amount of rub on them. The rub was thick with a good sweetness to it. I could pull the bone clean out, which was really nice.

It feels like they are trying to blend multiple BBQ styles, which can work, but may take some time. I think if they narrow down their craft some, they are on the cusp of being an elite BBQ restaurant in Cleveland. All in all, they are a good place with really friendly people. Stop by and get yourselves some BBQ!

212 SW Water St

The Blue Duck BBQ Tavern is in the old Chicago & Rock Island Railroad Depot and Freight House just steps away from the Illinois River. The moment you enter the lobby the sweet dreamy smell of smoking oak draws you in. The place is clean, trendy, tasteful and albeit quaint. When I say quaint I mean it. We left at 5:30 on a Saturday evening and there was already a crowd of hungry diners waiting to be seated.  They could easily double or triple their seating and still fill the seats. Why you might ask? Because the place is especially good!

The place has a great concept: Beer – Whiskey – BBQ now that’s a winning formula right there. In addition to standard BBQ fare they have some unique offerings such as a Poutine and a Banh Mi. Of course I went straight up traditional Brisket, Mac & Cheese, Baked Beans with a side order of Rib Tips and a biscuit. For my appetizer I had their fried pickles which are homemade and delicious. They are not overly dilly and the garlic aioli (mayo) is wonderful as well. The Brisket is moist, tender and very smoky. If you do not like a heavy smoke taste then this may not be your bag however for me I like it smoky! The Rib Tips are average, the bark was a little dry and you need to mix it with the gelatinous fatty interior to really enjoy it. Their BBQ sauce reminds me of a Carolina sauce with a touch of Southwest splashed in for good measure. The Mac & Cheese is bland. The Baked Beans were above average zangy, tasty good! The biscuit was useless and I’m sorry I didn’t get a piece of key lime pie. The service is really good and other than a few food preferences this place really is especially good!

Very interesting concept. You give the host your credit or debit card and they swipe it. It is returned to you along with a store card. You use this card during your visit to order food and pour your own drinks from the wall of tappers. There are about three dozen beers to choose from, three wines, two cocktails, and six hard ciders. Insert your card above the drink of your choice. Choose a glass or a flight. A screen above the tapper keeps track of how many ounces you've poured and the total of what you've spent.

To order food, place the card in a special spot on the table. A tablet is activated which displays the menu items. Make your choices and a runner brings your food after a short time. There is no tipping. The business advertises that it pays its employees a fair wage and tipping isn't required.

Read an article about PrimeBBQ opening up in Monroe. I am a Texas transplant and like most Texans, I consider myself a BBQ afficonado...I've been to most of the local eateries and thought I'd check this one out. I took my wife and walked in to bustling restaurant...smell of smoke and the sounds of plates and silverware filled the air...the place was packed, so we decided to take the food home and eat...ordered the Sampler Platter to try as much of the menu as possible. We got home and popped the aluminum lid off to find that everything was covered in BBQ sauce. Strike 1. The food was decent and may have been good but the sweet flavor of the sauce covered up any flavor of the smoke. Rule #1 to BBQ is don't hide the flavor of the meat...let the customer decide how much sauce (if any) they want on their meat. Brisket was very fatty and not a charred fatty. Riblets were good, ribs were good and the chicken was good...the pulled pork was very good...all of these may have been great but so hard to tell...I'm giving a 4 star because I could tell that underneath all the sauce was a pretty darn good smoke meat...SUGGESTIONS: 1. Don't slather your meat in sauce, allow the customer to decide. 2. Allow your brisket to char a little bit...bark is good...fat is good...gristle is not. Overall, good job PrimeBBQ for being brand new, great freshman effort..can't wait to get back and see how they've matured! OH! Banana Pudding was Great!

Pulled pork and brisket both seemed a bit dry (possibly from being cooked ahead) and lacked the full flavor like the ribs did. Not sure if they use the same rub, but they should. The baked beans were good, and they should honestly make a BBQ sauce to match that flavor to really fill their sauce line up. When I moved to Wisconsin after 34 years in Texas I was worried that I wouldn't be able to have real Texas BBQ unless I made it myself.  That all changed when I visited Joe's.  They have great BBQ.  It is a very limited menu and written on a chalkboard next to the register when you come in.  The place itself is very small with a few tables but they do offer BBQ to go and it appears thats mainly how people get the food.

We tried the brisket, chicken, and ribs.  All were delicious.  They have sides of spicy BBQ sauce or mild BBQ sauce to go along with the meal if you want.  They also had mac and cheese, beans, and cole slaw available as sides in which we got all of them.

The only negative thing I would say would be they don't have any high chairs at all or a kids menu.  They have plenty of space for them and its not exactly a quiet place that you wouldn't mind having kids.  We made it work but it would have been nice to have a chair to but a kid in.

Bottom line is if you want some fantastic Texas BBQ.  Joe's is the place for that.
