I have heard of this place from recommendations and I didn’t plan on going here but we were in East Peoria and were looking for a place to eat when I spotted Whitey’s. Whitey’s BBQ is located on the corner of Washington and Anna streets in downtown East Peoria. It is at quite possibly the smallest and most dangerous sidewalk in the state of Illinois. However you must chance the dangers of the sidewalk because once inside you will be safe and secure with some outstandingly frickin awesome BBQ. I’m not gonna talk much about looks and motif because quite frankly who cares. Whitey could serve his BBQ in an alley and I would go there.

The Brisket is some of the best I can remember having in a long time. It is perfectly cooked, tender as can be, flavorful, juicey, and it’s just perfect. The most difficult cut of meat to do right and Whitey’s nails it. I also really liked the pulled pork.  Once again you can get some dried out pulled pork but no no not from here. Great Burnt Ends and Rib Tips as well.  Also, I must mention the Mac & Cheese…you gotta have some good sides at a BBQ joint.  I didn’t try many because I was in a meat frenzy, but that is some dynamite Mac & Cheese. I tried both BBQ sauces and I loved the mild. It had an aromatic flavor to it that you must try.

I ended up at That BBQ Joint (TBJ) by happenstance after my efforts to visit a different restaurant were foiled by my inability to find a parking space.  But my luck was not all bad that day as both the food and service at TBJ exceeded my expectations.

There is a definite black and white theme to the restaurant interior.  The interior walls have a fresh coat of institutional white paint, with black trim around the doors and windows.  The menus are written on whiteboards with black ink and the food comes on a black & white checkerboard patterned paper liner.  The large front windows allow for waves of natural light to stream into the interior and allow diners keep tabs on the action taking place on Willy Street.  While the building has seen better days, the new occupants have cleaned it up nicely.

Since TBJ does not have waiter service, I had limited interaction with the staff.  Nonetheless, all the staff members I interacted with were courteous, polite and helpful.  As a first time visitor, my order taker offered helpful suggestions when I mentioned I was visiting for the first time.  He also checked in to see what I thought of my sandwich which doesn't always happen at counter service restaurants.  Throughout my time at TBJ, this employee was constantly tidying out the dining area and checking the condiment supply levels when there was a break in the somewhat steady flow of lunch time customers.

I elected to go with the Thursday special, the TBJ Cubano sandwich (pulled pork, ham, mustard, pickles and a pressed, well-buttered French roll). Mad props to the kitchen for their fantastic griddle work on the French roll as every bite yielded a satisfying crunch.  The pulled pork component provided plenty of porky deliciousness.  The Achilles heel of the sandwich was the ocean of generic yellow mustard slathered onto the sandwich.  With a little better balance, this could be a top echelon sandwich in town with an amazing stable of sandwich offerings.

Bonus content: TBJ sells bottles of their sauce for $8.

After this positive first impression, a return visit to TBJ is certainly in my future.  The wonderful aroma of smoked meats wafting through the restaurant during my first visit has me eager to try there more traditional BBQ offerings of smoked brisket, ribs, pulled pork and smoked chicken.

Alright, so, in order to be useful to anyone interest in this place, lets start with important things, and work our way down.

Food:
The food was excellent. We got three different appetizers, which each were very good portion sizes, perfect temperature, and very good flavors.

The one who had the salad, was impressed with the size of it overall, and said it too was very good.

The ribs (which we all got), were good when sauced, but the ones dry (and sauce added) were VERY good. The side choices were very good, and I had a hard time deciding just two.

Also the cornbread with the bourbon butter was a great finish to a meal.

Service:
The service was very very good. For the person we had having been new, aside from one very small issue, she did an excellent job.

She stopped by our table every few minutes to make certain didn't need anything, and kept our drinks filled.

Any questions we had, she was quick to get an answer for us, and was knowledgeable otherwise.

Anything we wanted, she was able to get for us quickly, and without any issues.

Overall, no real issues and was well done.

Atmosphere:
The place overall had a good feel to it, was nice and open (I'm used to tables being way to close together), and the seats were comfortable.

The music was just a little louder that I would have liked, but speaking at a normal volume, we were still able to hear each other.

There is also a nice outdoor area (which we didn't sit at though), but it overall had a very nice look to it.

Overall:
The food was good, but there was a little bit of things that could have been better. The service was excellent, and there were no real issues there. The atmosphere had a little to be desired, but otherwise wasn't a problem. This could certainly be a 4/5 or 4.5/5 to even many of the pickiest eaters.

If I could, I would actually give Sharks BBQ 3.5 stars. Great customer service, it only takes 1-5 mins to receive your order, and it is reasonably priced.

Sharks BBQ is (what I define) a "fast casual BBQ restaurant." This means, it is NOT a formal "sit down" restaurant. At Sharks BBQ you wait in line, they take your order, you receive your order (it takes 1-5 mins for you to receive your order), and you can eat it there or take it to-go. There have been plenty of fast causal BBQ restaurants popping up all over the area.

What I love about Sharks BBQ is their amazing customer service, the employees are super friendly, they are great people to talk to. Another thing I love is how quick it takes for you to receive your order, which is another advantage of the emerging "fast casual" BBQ restaurants. Lastly, my favorite thing about Sharks BBQ is their pricing. Their items are all very reasonably priced. I personally got their brisket and the ribs. I would recommend those two items.

What I didn't like about Sharks BBQ was the lack of variety of BBQ sauces, and the food is pretty good, but obviously not as good as a traditional "sit down" BBQ restaurant. This is expected because you get your order in such a timely manner (Again, it takes 1-5 mins to receive your order).

I would recommend Sharks BBQ if you are looking for a BBQ fix and you are limited with time. Otherwise, if you have the time, I would highly recommend a sit down BBQ restaurant.

We enjoyed eating here for the first time yesterday. We'd gotten hungry for barbecue and were reading the reviews and had been a little worried about what they said.
The wait staff here is very attentive! I know someone had said the portions here were small- I'd gotten the ribs and chicken combo and while the half slab on the plate *was* smaller than some I have seen, the platter was priced accordingly, as it was the same for ribs plus chicken here than I would just get a half slab and no chicken elsewhere. And after eating the meal, I felt comfortably full. I did see one could add another half slab to any meal for 6.99 which would be the price of a rib/chicken combo elsewhere, so surely with the extra half slab the portions are not small at all. My husband got the half chicken plate and it was more than he could eat, so the chicken is plenty, and also inexpensive as well.
The sides are good- the braised cabbage is done in an authentic southern style, seasoned up with meat. I also got the sweet potato which is served with cinnamon spread and you can get brown sugar and more cinnamon if you like. My husband got the baked beans which he remarked were excellent and also the collards, which although mild in taste, were punched right up with a splash of hot sauce.
I think the most important thing here is the genuine flavor of smoke--which being an avid barbecuer myself I can assure you that it tastes right. There is another place in town that I suspect pours liquid smoke in their brine and that flavor just overwhelms their meat, especially the chicken. Here the smoke tastes like it comes from the smoker and nowhere else.
We know we will be back, as this place does meet our standards. Our waitress told us that on Sundays the chicken is all-you-can-eat. I am looking forward to that and if I manage to have some room after dinner I will sample some of the pie. My husband tried a chiffon type pumpkin pie and it was marvelous!

The cabbage rolls were steaming hot, but the other items were lukewarm, borderline cold, when they came out.  They were busy; it appeared that the other food must have sat while waiting for the rolls.  I noticed this on other dishes while at the counter paying my bill; visible steam pouring from cabbage rolls but not from other plates being carried.  5. Vinegar!  I had the vinegar bacon slaw.  Good, not great because you could not inhale anywhere near the bite you were taking without your brain trying to jump from your skull.  I know, "dude you ordered vinegar slaw," but this was overboard.  You could also taste the heavy handed vinegar in the bbq chicken sauce and the extra cabbage with the rolls.  6. Wait staff was nice and attentive, though food was a little slow coming following the salad course.  Again, they were busy and were banging away, but the differences in food temps indicates that something was happening in the kitchen to slow service.
We almost never let one visit define an establishment, but in this case, the prices will likely keep us away.

I rarely do reviews, and most always those few I do, are positive. This one however, let's call educational. This evening we made an infrequent appearance at Cowboy. We live closer to town where there are many places for a dinner after work . But for fun and diversity we chose Cowboy tonight for the first time in about a year. I wanted to see the Belmont Stakes and we knew they had TV's. Our wait person was young, energetic, friendly and pleasant, call him "G." EVERYTHING was great, but for one thing.
The Saturday special is prime rib. I discussed with  G that I liked rare prime rib, and since it was early in the evening, there should be rare prime rib available. G explained that since the meat was smoked, the doneness is controlled by the amount of time the meat is heated in the au jus before coming to the table. I ordered the prime rib Saturday special and repeated that I would like it RARE.
The main course was served and after a few bites of meat I could tell that it was not rare, but in fact was very well done. I flipped the cut of meat over and discovered my piece was the end cut! How could an end cut, of standing rib roast, ever be rare? When G came over I explained this to him. G offered to have someone from the kitchen come out to discuss this. G came back and said the explanation was given to him, for him to pass it on to me. He said that since the meat was smoked, all the cuts were the same doneness.
So, if you want your prime rib rare or even medium rare, DO NOT order prime rib from Cowboy.

After years of hearing the praise and adulation of Slow's I was obliged to visit their new Pontiac location. I was blown away by the mediocrity of the food. It was not bad food, it was not good food. It tasted precisely like nothing. I'm not sure a single rock of salt made its way into any of the dishes in the kitchen.

My date and I ordered 4 of the sides, and while the smoked baked beans with pulled pork is a great concept, they tasted like nothing. Ditto the Mac and cheese. Mom's Green beans were pleasantly spicy with a mustard kick, though they were not terribly flavorful beyond that spice. The coleslaw, again, very bland and inoffensive.

I ordered the jambalaya entree, and was rather disappointed that it lacked spice and flavor entirely. My dining companion ordered the pulled pork, which had a wonderful texture and a great bark from the smoker (I could tell that their rub was pretty decent, in fact). Alas the interior portion of the meat was, again, devoid of flavor. The sauce selection was underwhelming as well, though the North Carolina sauce was authentic and probably the highlight of the meal.

The waitress was excellent and attentive, I made a reservation and got right in on a fairly busy night. The restaurant interior was pleasant, and I have nothing but compliments to offer on those fronts. I also appreciate that Slow's made an investment in downtown Pontiac.

However, there are countless other places in the Metro Detroit area that do what Slow's does, only with a whole lot more flavor in the food. I'm going to return in a few months and give them another try, because I cannot in good conscience write an establishment off based on one meal. It is my sincere hope that the kitchen opens a box of salt in the meantime and dares to use it for seasoning the food.

Having been a huge fan of the Nick's in Romeoville, and having been very sad when they closed without warning, I was thrilled to find this Nick's fairly close to home. So on our way to Big R, we stopped in here, my taste buds already anticipating that incredible pulled pork sandwich.

Unfortunately, it wasn't the same. It should have been - but it was not. The sandwich was still huge and the bun was still soft, but the star of the show, that incredible BBQ sauce, simply wasn't a star. It lacked the flavor that elevated their sandwich from "good" to "incredible". It was also thinner, even watery. Every time I ate there in Romeoville, I was so covered in thick BBQ sauce by the time I was done that it was a challenge even to open the bathroom door to wash my hands. Here, a napkin did the job.

The rest of the food was also just "good" but, again, nothing special. My father asked for sweet peppers  on his sub but said it was so hot he could barely eat it, suggesting someone ignored his request. The coleslaw was as good as I remembered, but coleslaw does not a meal make.

The other thing that made that Nick's fun was that it was a smaller place, the tables close together, encouraging friendliness and even occasional banter between tables. It felt homey and inviting. Here, there's a lot of space for a small number of tables. Unless you're sitting at the back to back booths (which have little sitting room), you'd almost have to yell to talk to people at another table. (And I'm sure they would think you were quite strange if you did.) This place lacks that inviting vibe that existed in Romeoville.

In short, I would probably return if I was in the area, if only to give them a second chance, but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat at this Nick's.

Most dissatisfying though were the rib tips. They fell off the bone easily enough, but were tough and chewy, not too dissimilar to jerky. Even the collard greens were disappointing as they tasted watered down with next to no lemon.

The service was great initially, but the waitress was less attentive the closer we got to finishing our meal. Having been a huge fan of the Nick's in Romeoville, and having been very sad when they closed without warning, I was thrilled to find this Nick's fairly close to home. So on our way to Big R, we stopped in here, my taste buds already anticipating that incredible pulled pork sandwich.

Unfortunately, it wasn't the same. It should have been - but it was not. The sandwich was still huge and the bun was still soft, but the star of the show, that incredible BBQ sauce, simply wasn't a star. It lacked the flavor that elevated their sandwich from "good" to "incredible". It was also thinner, even watery. Every time I ate there in Romeoville, I was so covered in thick BBQ sauce by the time I was done that it was a challenge even to open the bathroom door to wash my hands. Here, a napkin did the job.

The rest of the food was also just "good" but, again, nothing special. My father asked for sweet peppers  on his sub but said it was so hot he could barely eat it, suggesting someone ignored his request. The coleslaw was as good as I remembered, but coleslaw does not a meal make.

The other thing that made that Nick's fun was that it was a smaller place, the tables close together, encouraging friendliness and even occasional banter between tables. It felt homey and inviting. Here, there's a lot of space for a small number of tables. Unless you're sitting at the back to back booths (which have little sitting room), you'd almost have to yell to talk to people at another table. (And I'm sure they would think you were quite strange if you did.) This place lacks that inviting vibe that existed in Romeoville.

In short, I would probably return if I was in the area, if only to give them a second chance, but I wouldn't go out of my way to eat at this Nick's.

Johnny V's Smoke-Shack, nestled now in the small town of Perry, is not a marketing term in comparison to Johnny V's Smokehouse in Corruna. It is a smaller, more family oriented restaurant, however. It's size is that made for the small town of Perry, I personally felt that it's price might have not been. I walked in and had a sense of modernism. An architectural design I felt Perry was really lacking aside from a majority of the fast food restaurants that are present by the time of this review. I ordered the Smokehouse Sliders with Burnt Ends --which can have different choices of protein aside from the Burnt Ends--, but prior to ordering, the definition of this was vague. The menu did not specify the count of sliders per order, not the mention it does not specify to come with a drink nor a side as those must be ordered separately as based on the menu itself. I would advise them to make an edit to assist to get that message accross. The menu also did not mention the toppings of onions and pickles, so I'm glad I did ask the cashier about that. Personally, not a pickle fan, but onions are neat. I also wanted to try their seasoned fries, so I got that to go along with it. I didn't get a drink, but if I was they do have the modern style Fountain Dispensers where one can mix different style beverages. I ordered it to go as I am a busy man who had to go places, yet I was told the wait would take twenty minutes, which I was okay to make the sacrifice for. During the wait, I leaned on the railing that was on the border of the kitchen area, and a gentleman accross asked if he could help me. I had some questions about the restaurant, I did not expect it to be the owner. It's owner is the same owner of the Smokehouse, a gentleman I've met named Kevin who had a very down-to-earth vibe. They have been quite busy getting this going, and with their product being sold out in certain areas, show potential. I was given my food and went along my way.

The burnt ends had a good bitter taste from the char on the side and would fall apart in the mouth, but I found a few pieces of unrendered fat which made it difficult to enjoy. Three Small sliders that didn't have onion, "seasoned" fried (???), and a small cup of barbeque sauce. Price: $11.23, which my wallet felt like it got hit with a shovel for what it was worth, especially for the value one can get from competitors. I would like to see this place grow for this community as it's an addition to the local economy and an alternative flavor for many to try. I used to dine there or order carryout at least once a month. Then, the business was sold. The food has remained consistent, but the prices have doubled in the last 10 years or so. I understand inflation, but the price you pay for what you get has gotten unreasonable. Their largest steak (other than the 20 Oz sirloin which the server will recommend against) is only 14 Oz and it's $28. Until the late '90's, the 13 Oz t-bone cost around $12. Brilliance mixed with a few misses.

TL;DR
While the ribs and pinto beans need some more love, this place has some positive potential.  The mac and cheese, sausage, and cornbread are positively awesome and should be given a shoot.  I'm on the border between 3 and 4 stars and pushed to 3 because the ribs should be a focus.

Detailed Review
Let's start with the building.  The layout and ambiance of this place is right on the money for a BBQ place.  They have the standard chair/table layout with a bar off the to the side.  It feels like a BBQ place when you walk through the door.

By the time we arrived, they had deep 6'd most of the menu (which in BBQ is a GOOD THING).  This means that they are slow cooking their meats and not compromising to put more food out.

Full disclosure: I'm probably pickier about BBQ than most folks.  I grew up with a smoker, smoking, and now I'm older than dirt in dog years.

The Food:
1)  Mac and Cheese (10 out of 10)-  I don't normally start a bbq review with Mac and Cheese, but HOLY FREAKIN (EXPLETIVE) that is some incredible mac and cheese.  The only thing I might add would be a touch of truffle oil, but this is good stuff.
2)  Ribs (5 out of 10)-
a)  The taste on the ribs is pretty good where they had good smoke penetration and the dry rub on the meat was pretty good.  The rib did not take away from the flavor of the meat which is nice to see in the North.
b)  It looks like they might have an issue with the way in which they are cooking the ribs.  The ribs *DO* have a smoke ring; however, it is incredibly inconsistent around the meat.  I'm guessing that they didn't rotate the meat in the smoker and/or had the door open too much (see the picture).
c)  Back to the cook, the pull on the ribs was tough and the collagen had not broken down in the meat.  This generally means that the meat was pulled out with an internal temp below 190.  If you let the meat go up to 190 internal before pulling, the collagen and fat melt into the meat and the meat is juicier and gives you that good pull.  (These guys probably already know this, but for the rest of you.  It is a little counterintuitive but raising the internal temperature higher makes the meat juicy in ribs.)
3)  Sausage (9 out of 10)-  I don't have a long review for the sausage but it was pretty darn good.  You could tell that it was made fresh and by someone that knows what they are doing.
3)  Pork Belly (8 out of 10)-  For a restaurant, they did an outstanding job on pork belly.  Pork Belly is a labor of love and they did a pretty darn good job on it.  The cracked pepper style rub is a win in my book.
4)  Pinto Beans (2 out of 10)-  As much as I loved the mac, I hated the pinto beans.  It was a bit like hormel and lacked any real defining flavor.  They need to fix or remove.
5)  Cornbread (9 out of 10)-  They have a sweet cornbread which is pretty amazing.  I normally do not like sugar in my cornbread (it's a religious thing in the south), but this was very good.  They didn't kill it in sugar so you could just taste the sweetness at the end of the bite.  They might make me change my views on sugar in cornbread.
6)  Sawce (3 out of 10)-  We tried two sauces, mild and hot.  The worcestershire/vinegar flavors in the sauce are not something I enjoy.  I feel like they completely overpower the meat and do very little to enhance the flavor of the meat.  I'm guessing these guys are either Carolina and/or Texas influenced because this is standard fair in those regions.  To bring their sauces into balance, they might want to dial back on the vinegar and worcestershire sauce.

They are new and hopefully they can fix some of the issues with the ribs and pintos.

I'll be heading back over to the restaurant some time in the next two weeks to try more of the items and then I'll update the review.  I normally like to truly judge a bbq place by their brisket and burnt ends.  Hopefully, we can pull that together soon.

This is a hard review for me to write, and probably going to be controversial.

I'm going to preface this saying, I'm writing this as a BBQ aficionado. I made a trip to Kansas City JUST to try the original recipe for Kansas City BBQ, I've been to Q39, a place arguably the most acclaimed BBQ restaurant in the world. I know BBQ pretty well. And from that lens, a lot of what I'm saying is going to be relative to these things. I will try to keep it grounded, but keep that in mind.

The first thing you'll notice is the location is small, like, too small. It really feels like they should be in a stand alone place, because there's not nearly enough seating if you're looking for a dine in experience. But I won't dock points on that. The ordering system is a bit odd, but it's simple enough to figure out, and not something I will dock points over.

The food came pretty quick, we got pulled pork, brisket , I believe fried pickles, and ribs. The real issues are shown here first: for the price point, the portions are pretty small. Not upsettingly so, but generally BBQ places are known for their generosity in a plate, Saddleback simply doesn't deliver here.

The next major issue is that honestly...it's not that great. I've had truly, life changing-ly good BBQ in a number of places before. The two things that make BBQ amazing are the sauce, and the technique. Here, both are disappointingly-average. With all the hype, I expected something truly amazing, and what I got was something better than store-bought, but unfortunately not something I felt like a true, "pit master" could conjure. A true quality BBQ place brings you a product that once you've had it, you are almost in awe of how they created it. There is none of that magic here. It is an average sauce, cooked by going through the motions. In the lens of perspective, it is simply just mediocre, balancing on good.

The sides are really the next issue. If you're going to focus your efforts on making a quality BBQ product, and it is simply average, you need to have sides that elevate the dish. I believe we had Coleslaw and Mac & Cheese, and again, it simply didn't impress, nor did the Texas toast if I'm recalling correctly.

The final, and perhaps biggest issue is that legitimately, there's one of the best BBQ places in the country quite literally right here in Lansing, and not very far away, Meat BBQ. It is just madness to me, that when there is such a homerun establishment so close nearby, Saddleback doesn't emulate, or try to innovate over such a truly fantastic place. I would LOVE to see a true rival to them here in Saddleback, perhaps even the creation of our own, unique "Michigan Style" BBQ emerge over it.

If I had any advice, it would be seriously consider taking some time off work to hit up some of the big BBQ places, go to Joe's in KC, see what it's like, head over to Memphis and hit up Jim Neely's. See what it is that truly makes these places special. I'd wager a place like Q39, if you hit up their head chef would even be willing to show you what they do. You don't need to copy other places to be the best, but there are clearly techniques that separate a master from an enthusiast that are not at work here.

That's not to say Saddleback BBQ is bad; it isn't. It's just...average. And considering the proximity of a place that surpasses average to exceptional, I just can't see a reason to come here.

I'll give it a try again someday, but unless there's some serious 'upping their game' I don't see this becoming a regular visit, unless I'm already in the neighborhood and don't feel like cooking that night. Like I said, hard review.

The place is located in a strip mall not easily visible from the street. You gotta kinda know it’s there to go there. They have a take-out area that seemed to be doing a decent amount of business. We sat in the dining room which was open, airy and clean. I like the picnic like tables that line the dining room walls. The mellow R&B music sets the tone of the place. The air is ripe with the scent that I can best describe as sweet meaty smoke…absolutely appetizing. The waitress was friendly, likeable and the service was fine.

What excited me was that they serve rib tips. I love rib tips and these did not disappoint. Tender and juicy with just the perfect note of smoke (pun intended). The thing with rib tips is that they are an over looked portion of the pigs ribs. More often seen as a poor man’s ribs, they are more flavorful and juicier than traditional ribs because there are more bones and the little white nubs of cartilage preserve more of the porky goodness. I, being of the Caucasian persuasion but spending most of my life on the south side of Chicago, know that they are mostly offered at Black (African American) BBQ joints. If you have not had the opportunity to eat Rib Tips you need to. For my sides I had Mac & Cheese, which didn’t knock my socks off but I liked it. I also had the baked beans, which I didn’t care for, but if you have read my other BBQ joint reviews I am a baked bean snob.

I will get my negative comment out of the way here with a caveat that this may not be indicative of the kitchens performance on a regular basis. However, the wait for our food was beyond acceptable for the time of day we were there (lunch). If we were in a hurry, it would have been bad. Thankfully we were not.

We arrived around 8:30pm on a Friday night. Since most of any evening dinner rush was pretty much over (and the fact that I got front row parking right next to the door) we were seated right away. The hostess was less than friendly and appeared to be bothered to actually seat us. She originally started us at a regular table but when we asked for a booth she sighed and took us to the back corner. She didn't tell us anything, just sat the menus down and walked away.

Turns out that by asking for a booth we were placed in a section that had just been sat. So it took our server a while to get over to us. She did stop by and tell us it would be a minute...which was appreciated. The long wait allowed us to make all the necessary selections on what we wanted to eat. When she did come back she asked if we wanted to place our order or wait until the appetizer came out. We opted to place our order. Pretty much after we ordered the fried pickles came out. They were good, but seeing that just a few days ago we had some from Bubba 33's they just didn't stand out like theirs do. The onion rings were perfect, and the baked beans had a little kick to them. My other half said the brisket was good and said it wasn't tough like other places. Overall the food was good and I was impressed...ok...that is a lie. The food was ok, but I have had better. The "sweet" sauce wasn't very sweet at all. It had more kick to it than other places with a "mild" sauce. We did go with dessert as well...the donuts. They were good and came with raspberry and chocolate dipping sauce.

All in all I would probably go back again, but probably because they are open late and it gives another option if I don't feel like cooking after getting home from work at 10pm.

So my honest review of Studio Hotrods Roadhouse follows. First off the parking lot in front is tight. The look of the place as you walk up is nice, well lit, and clean. Bartender was very friendly and fast. Some items on the menu seem over priced but others seemed to be in line with what you would expect. For instance a burger was $16 for Black Angus that had only basic toppings. This seems a bit over priced by about $4 to $6 dollars. On the other hand a deep dish pizza was $24 and looked very good. This is close to what I would expect to pay for a great Chicago deep dish. Goldy and I ordered some desert. We were told everything is made from scratch so the price for the items seemed fine. We ordered Key Lime Pie and Creme Brulee. Both items were clearly made on sight and were fantastic. Seriously some of the best deserts I ever had. The bill for the two deserts, two premium beers, and one Captain and Coke came to $44.76. This to me was not too high so like I said some things are not too pricey. Both Goldy and I agreed to come back and try the deep dish pizza. The bartender closed us out quickly and we headed out. On the way out I did notice a bit of clutter under the stairs in a cage by the fire pump. I'm guessing this is because there still working on the place but it should be out of sight and not near the fire pump. I am giving a 3 stare review for now and will see how future visits go.

Black beans - better from the can

Bread that comes w meat - good toasted garlic bread

Detailed Review
Let's start with the building.  The layout and ambiance of this place is right on the money for a BBQ place.  They have the standard chair/table layout with a bar off the to the side.  It feels like a BBQ place when you walk through the door.

By the time we arrived, they had deep 6'd most of the menu (which in BBQ is a GOOD THING).  This means that they are slow cooking their meats and not compromising to put more food out.

Full disclosure: I'm probably pickier about BBQ than most folks.  I grew up with a smoker, smoking, and now I'm older than dirt in dog years.

The Food:
1)  Mac and Cheese (10 out of 10)-  I don't normally start a bbq review with Mac and Cheese, but HOLY FREAKIN (EXPLETIVE) that is some incredible mac and cheese.  The only thing I might add would be a touch of truffle oil, but this is good stuff.
2)  Ribs (5 out of 10)-
a)  The taste on the ribs is pretty good where they had good smoke penetration and the dry rub on the meat was pretty good.  The rib did not take away from the flavor of the meat which is nice to see in the North.
b)  It looks like they might have an issue with the way in which they are cooking the ribs.  The ribs *DO* have a smoke ring; however, it is incredibly inconsistent around the meat.  I'm guessing that they didn't rotate the meat in the smoker and/or had the door open too much (see the picture).
c)  Back to the cook, the pull on the ribs was tough and the collagen had not broken down in the meat.  This generally means that the meat was pulled out with an internal temp below 190.  If you let the meat go up to 190 internal before pulling, the collagen and fat melt into the meat and the meat is juicier and gives you that good pull.  (These guys probably already know this, but for the rest of you.  It is a little counterintuitive but raising the internal temperature higher makes the meat juicy in ribs.)
3)  Sausage (9 out of 10)-  I don't have a long review for the sausage but it was pretty darn good.  You could tell that it was made fresh and by someone that knows what they are doing.
3)  Pork Belly (8 out of 10)-  For a restaurant, they did an outstanding job on pork belly.  Pork Belly is a labor of love and they did a pretty darn good job on it.  The cracked pepper style rub is a win in my book.
4)  Pinto Beans (2 out of 10)-  As much as I loved the mac, I hated the pinto beans.  It was a bit like hormel and lacked any real defining flavor.  They need to fix or remove.
5)  Cornbread (9 out of 10)-  They have a sweet cornbread which is pretty amazing.  I normally do not like sugar in my cornbread (it's a religious thing in the south), but this was very good.  They didn't kill it in sugar so you could just taste the sweetness at the end of the bite.  They might make me change my views on sugar in cornbread.
6)  Sawce (3 out of 10)-  We tried two sauces, mild and hot.  The worcestershire/vinegar flavors in the sauce are not something I enjoy.  I feel like they completely overpower the meat and do very little to enhance the flavor of the meat.  I'm guessing these guys are either Carolina and/or Texas influenced because this is standard fair in those regions.  To bring their sauces into balance, they might want to dial back on the vinegar and worcestershire sauce.

They are new and hopefully they can fix some of the issues with the ribs and pintos.

I'll be heading back over to the restaurant some time in the next two weeks to try more of the items and then I'll update the review.  I normally like to truly judge a bbq place by their brisket and burnt ends.  Hopefully, we can pull that together soon.

The Place
Lillie's Q is located in Bucktown or in the Wicker Park area if you will at 1856 W North Ave, Chicago, IL. Nice up beat fun atmosphere area at 's this urban barbecue shack.  The decor is very rustic but with a warm southern charm.  There is a small outdoor eating area which is nice when the weather permits and space is available.

The Menu
Typical Southern BBQ menu on the surface.  We had a rack of ribs, 1/2 bbq chicken, brussel sprouts, and sweet potato fries.  They were out of green beans.  A couple of observations vs a true southern smokin pig style menu.  The size of the sides is without a doubt small.  A true southern place would have Jalapeño grits, loaded potato casserole, and fried okra.  Our ribs were tasty and the rub was good.  The chicken was nicely done as well. The sides were disappointing.

The Experience/Value/Service
Our service was good.  The price was slightly high on the entrees but somewhat reasonable when compared to the value delivered.  The sides were over priced and tiny.  Overall it was a good experience.  I know this restaurant has multiple locations but with a little more focus on the menu and the sides this place could be a true southern gem.

My suspicion is that they take 3 ribs and then cut them such that all of the meat is on the outermost 2 bones, making it seem like each has a ton of meat. But this takes 3 ribs that you might be able to charge $20 for and converts them into 2 that you can sell for $40. I don’t have proof of it, but it’s what I think is happening.

The brisket is overall above average. It’s cooked and served appropriately, with good texture and moistness. I think the flavor could have been a little more smoky. I can’t recall the sides that we had.

We were pretty excited to have a new BBQ place in town. After Kelly Joy's left we were pretty bummed. We also own our own smoker but sometimes you just want someone else to do the 8-12 hour cook.
So we were ready to get some good BBQ. We decided to try the Family Meal #2 (with pulled pork as the 1 lb meat option) so we could try several things.
Here's our verdict:
Get the beans. They are VERY good.
The coleslaw is generic but not bad.
The mac and cheese needs texture. A little bread crumbs will go a long way.
Good slider buns and cornbread but nothing to write home about.
The pulled pork was good I suppose but even when smoking meat, smoke shouldn't be the only flavor. It doesn't taste like an injection or even a rub was used.
The ribs were okay as well other than the couple on the end of the rack which were thin and therefore dry. Again it's hard to tell if a rub was used. (I would suggest to the owner to have the waitress ask the customer what sauce for the ribs and then use that sauce to get the ever-important glaze)
The chicken was TERRIBLE. Undoubtedly the worst chicken I've had at a restaurant. Not only was it super SUPER dry but the skin was leather. On top of that the skin had a flavor that tasted chemical in nature and makes me think that lighter fluid, charcoal briquettes (which often have lighter fluid in them) or direct propane flames were used. At the very least it could be that one of those things were used in the smoker at some point and the flavor is residual. We've come across this before.
The sauces available were...something. On a slider bun with pulled pork and coleslaw all three were passable. But just on the meat the korean one tasted like a spicy version of Burger King's Sweet and Sour sauce which wasn't my cup of tea but some people like that.
The house sauce tasted like sweet cinnamon and in my opinion was not good at all.
The bourbon was the best of the three but I wouldn't go in asking for a pint to use at home.
Oddly enough the korean and house together were not too bad.
All in all, if I'm hankering for pulled pork but don't want to cook that long I may go again but use my own homemade sauce.
Also the prices were good for what we got.
My final thoughts are don't ever go there for the chicken. Just don't. Get it takeout and use your own sauce. Don't forget the beans.

The look of the fatty bubbles alone was a turn-off, but the rests were just a leathery chewy mess. Not a go-to in my book; on the other hand, the ribs we're plentiful and pretty tasty. What lacked in smoke flavor made up for in a meaty, tender smothered in a mild flavor of barbecue sauce. If you like mild sauce then you will enjoy their sauce, but I was more of an enthusiast for a mixture of mild/hot combination barbecue sauce which was provided on the hotlink sausage. The only type of fires they have are the seasoned fries which I am not a fan of either but with a little barbecue sauce and bread, it makes for a delectable fries sandwich. There has been much to do about how they cook their ribs, well let me just say this because when LEONS first opened it was much the same as all neighborhood barbecue rib joints. Then the cooking staff changed hands right before the old man retired or past away. The style of how the meat was cooked changed from ALL SMOKED to BOILED AND SOMEWHAT SMOKE COOKED, kind of like the way CARSON RIBS cooked their meat. You guys remember CARSON RIBS right??! It was the same place that was popular for years and was a go-to for many events I went to back in the day. Folks just loved them some CARSON for it tender and meaty falling off the bone flavor. It was always a decent place but never understood why they were so popular when the meat was never OPEN PITTED cooked. Anyway, this place was decent and like most places, one day the meat is cooked to perfection, and the next time it is depending on the cook is just okay. I will probably go back just for the ribs and sauce. Thanks!

And from a price point it wasn't bad, especially compared to how many bbq joints have a price point which usually comes with either them trying to price according to other joints despite lackluster quality or they really have a product worthy of a $15-20 plate.

They also have a cozy location, friendly staff and good bar selection, I stayed for a drink while I waited and the crowd was friendly too.

Now, that said, there were some glaring flaws that kept me from giving a better rating and as I said, if it wasn't for actually having a decently cooked brisket it would have been a 2-Star.

Starting with the brisket, while it's one thing to properly cook a brisket, its another to make it shine and make it delicious. Anyone can throw a steak on a grill or a piece of chicken in a pan and pull it off at the proper time and thats what it seems like happened here. There was no flavor in the meat itself. The rub was non-existent in flavor but I could tell there was something on it, and from a smoke perspective, I could see the ring so it did penetrate but there was no flavor to it, no taste of mequite or hickory or applewood or anything, almost as if they just stopped by a side of the road firewood stand and used some chopped down pine tree for the wood. In my opinion, a good brisket should shine on its own and a BBQ sauce should be a compliment to it. With this, it would've been pretty much bland and not inedible but unenjoyable without using a highly flavored sauce.

The burger my wife ordered she said was good but definitely tasted like just a prepackaged patty. It was clearly fresh meat and toppings but with a host of other burger joints in the area touting quality burgers it takes a good show to stand out and with Smoke Creek advertising itself as a bbq and burger place it's not shining with their burger and definitely not a place we'd go "Hey, lets go get a burger from Smoke Creek" when we could do just about the same running up to Meijer and getting some patties from the meat dept. It wasn't a fast food burger by any means, but it was definitely just something you'd get if you got asked to go out and didn't like BBQ and it was all there was else.

Lastly, the cornbread. I ordered an extra order of it cause I LOVE cornbread, I'll whip up a batch just on a whim and eat an entire tray of it. But this was bland, dry, and burnt on the bottom. They were cupcake muffins of cornbread, tasted prepackaged and a burnt bottom where the cupcake wrapped ripped off half the bottom.

Overall, if I get a super big craving for BBQ I might come by again just to appease that itch but I could eat BBQ 4-7 times a week, I was really hoping this would be the place I could go once a week but I'm thinking it's just gonna be one of those once every few months kinda places if that.

The onion rings were perfect, and the baked beans had a little kick to them. My other half said the brisket was good and said it wasn't tough like other places. Overall the food was good and I was impressed...ok...that is a lie. The food was ok, but I have had better. The "sweet" sauce wasn't very sweet at all. All in all I would probably go back again, but probably because they are open late and it gives another option if I don't feel like cooking after getting home from work at 10pm.

Johnny V's Smoke-Shack, nestled now in the small town of Perry, is not a marketing term in comparison to Johnny V's Smokehouse in Corruna. It is a smaller, more family oriented restaurant, however. It's size is that made for the small town of Perry, I personally felt that it's price might have not been. I walked in and had a sense of modernism. An architectural design I felt Perry was really lacking aside from a majority of the fast food restaurants that are present by the time of this review. I ordered the Smokehouse Sliders with Burnt Ends --which can have different choices of protein aside from the Burnt Ends--, but prior to ordering, the definition of this was vague. The menu did not specify the count of sliders per order, not the mention it does not specify to come with a drink nor a side as those must be ordered separately as based on the menu itself. I would advise them to make an edit to assist to get that message accross. The menu also did not mention the toppings of onions and pickles, so I'm glad I did ask the cashier about that. Personally, not a pickle fan, but onions are neat. I also wanted to try their seasoned fries, so I got that to go along with it. I didn't get a drink, but if I was they do have the modern style Fountain Dispensers where one can mix different style beverages. I ordered it to go as I am a busy man who had to go places, yet I was told the wait would take twenty minutes, which I was okay to make the sacrifice for. During the wait, I leaned on the railing that was on the border of the kitchen area, and a gentleman accross asked if he could help me. I had some questions about the restaurant, I did not expect it to be the owner. It's owner is the same owner of the Smokehouse, a gentleman I've met named Kevin who had a very down-to-earth vibe. They have been quite busy getting this going, and with their product being sold out in certain areas, show potential. I was given my food and went along my way.

The Food. It was... Well, I can imagine the chefs might have had some fatigue. Even though I ordered my meal to have onions, there was no onions. I ordered the seasoned fries, but these were bland. I'm not sure if they gave me seasoned fries or normal fries. I had a side of Kansas Barbeque sauce, it was sweet, but too sweet where it can blind the pallet. The burnt ends had a good bitter taste from the char on the side and would fall apart in the mouth, but I found a few pieces of unrendered fat which made it difficult to enjoy. Three Small sliders that didn't have onion, "seasoned" fried (???), and a small cup of barbeque sauce. Price: $11.23, which my wallet felt like it got hit with a shovel for what it was worth, especially for the value one can get from competitors. I would like to see this place grow for this community as it's an addition to the local economy and an alternative flavor for many to try. I would like to see improvments that take it from "Okay I guess" to "Wow, this is great". For now, it's okay, I guess. 👌🏻

My wife and myself decided to finally try Dr.Rolf's Barbecue on Sunday 8/4 around 3 pm since it had good reviews and we heard good recommendations form others. We like to eat at and see local restaurants succeed.

I always check restaurants out when I walk in and sit down.  The place was clean and the patrons seemed to be enjoying the food.  It had an open kitchen so I checked out the line and it was clean and organized.  Unfortunately I saw food code violations that are far to common nowadays at many restaurants. 1.  The cooks with beards had no beard guards on.  Beards are 6 times more likely to have hair fall out than hair on the head.  2. At least one cook was wearing a watch and bracelet.  Health code allows one smooth wedding ring.  3.  The cooks were wearing and changing gloves while handling ready to eat food, but were not washing their hands before putting on new gloves.  Health code states that hands must be washed before putting on new gloves.  When a food-service worker grabs new gloves with dirty hands all the gloves are now contaminated.  Like I said this is not just an issue at Dr. Rolf's, but at many other food service establishments.

We had 2 waitresses do to a change in the shift and both did a good job.  We ordered dirty tots with smoked pork to share between us.  These were very good.  The only thing that should be addressed is the tots having paper underneath. some of the cheese sank to the bottom and stuck to the paper.  It made it hard to scoop the tots out and not tear the paper when serving.

I ordered the southwest salad with smoked chicken.  The price of the added chicken was $2 and that was quite reasonable.  The food came out and presentation was appealing.  I instantly noticed that the avocado looked unripe, and it was hard and unripe when I picked it up.  The chicken looked poached and not smoked.  No smoke color and no smoke smell.  I went back online and looked at the menu to make sure that it was supposed to be a smoked chicken breast.  Yes it was.  The chicken had no smoke flavor.  Otherwise the salad was good.

My wife ordered the salmon salad.  When it came out she said to me it had a very fishy smell.  The salmon also looked poached.  It was supposed to be a roasted smoked  teriyaki salmon.  No color and the smell wash extremely fishy and not smokey.  She tried a small bite of the salmon and it was fishy tasting and bad.  Fresh salmon, regardless of how it is prepared, should never taste fishy.  The waitress was not sure how to handle it at first, but she was OK with my wife ordering a new meal.  She eventually ordered the beet salad and that came out quickly and was very good.

We also tried the cornbread waffle.  This was a great idea and a change from the cornbread muffin that most BBQ joints serve.  It was done well.  The ideas of using it in different desserts seams quite appealing.

We almost always give a restaurant that has not met expectations a second chance, so eventually we will visit Dr. Rolf's Barbecue again.  I hope they take this as constructive criticism, so that when we do visit again we can give a better review.  We want them to succeed as a local establishment.

This is a hard review for me to write, and probably going to be controversial.

I'm going to preface this saying, I'm writing this as a BBQ aficionado. I made a trip to Kansas City JUST to try the original recipe for Kansas City BBQ, I've been to Q39, a place arguably the most acclaimed BBQ restaurant in the world. I know BBQ pretty well. And from that lens, a lot of what I'm saying is going to be relative to these things. I will try to keep it grounded, but keep that in mind.

The first thing you'll notice is the location is small, like, too small. It really feels like they should be in a stand alone place, because there's not nearly enough seating if you're looking for a dine in experience. But I won't dock points on that. The ordering system is a bit odd, but it's simple enough to figure out, and not something I will dock points over.

The food came pretty quick, we got pulled pork, brisket , I believe fried pickles, and ribs. The real issues are shown here first: for the price point, the portions are pretty small. Not upsettingly so, but generally BBQ places are known for their generosity in a plate, Saddleback simply doesn't deliver here.

The next major issue is that honestly...it's not that great. I've had truly, life changing-ly good BBQ in a number of places before. The two things that make BBQ amazing are the sauce, and the technique. Here, both are disappointingly-average. With all the hype, I expected something truly amazing, and what I got was something better than store-bought, but unfortunately not something I felt like a true, "pit master" could conjure. A true quality BBQ place brings you a product that once you've had it, you are almost in awe of how they created it. There is none of that magic here. It is an average sauce, cooked by going through the motions. In the lens of perspective, it is simply just mediocre, balancing on good.

The sides are really the next issue. If you're going to focus your efforts on making a quality BBQ product, and it is simply average, you need to have sides that elevate the dish. I believe we had Coleslaw and Mac & Cheese, and again, it simply didn't impress, nor did the Texas toast if I'm recalling correctly.

The final, and perhaps biggest issue is that legitimately, there's one of the best BBQ places in the country quite literally right here in Lansing, and not very far away, Meat BBQ. It is just madness to me, that when there is such a homerun establishment so close nearby, Saddleback doesn't emulate, or try to innovate over such a truly fantastic place. I would LOVE to see a true rival to them here in Saddleback, perhaps even the creation of our own, unique "Michigan Style" BBQ emerge over it.

If I had any advice, it would be seriously consider taking some time off work to hit up some of the big BBQ places, go to Joe's in KC, see what it's like, head over to Memphis and hit up Jim Neely's. See what it is that truly makes these places special. I'd wager a place like Q39, if you hit up their head chef would even be willing to show you what they do. You don't need to copy other places to be the best, but there are clearly techniques that separate a master from an enthusiast that are not at work here.

That's not to say Saddleback BBQ is bad; it isn't. It's just...average. And considering the proximity of a place that surpasses average to exceptional, I just can't see a reason to come here.

I'll give it a try again someday, but unless there's some serious 'upping their game' I don't see this becoming a regular visit, unless I'm already in the neighborhood and don't feel like cooking that night. Like I said, hard review.

After years of hearing the praise and adulation of Slow's I was obliged to visit their new Pontiac location. I was blown away by the mediocrity of the food. It was not bad food, it was not good food. It tasted precisely like nothing. I'm not sure a single rock of salt made its way into any of the dishes in the kitchen.

My date and I ordered 4 of the sides, and while the smoked baked beans with pulled pork is a great concept, they tasted like nothing. Ditto the Mac and cheese. Mom's Green beans were pleasantly spicy with a mustard kick, though they were not terribly flavorful beyond that spice. The coleslaw, again, very bland and inoffensive.

I ordered the jambalaya entree, and was rather disappointed that it lacked spice and flavor entirely. My dining companion ordered the pulled pork, which had a wonderful texture and a great bark from the smoker (I could tell that their rub was pretty decent, in fact). Alas the interior portion of the meat was, again, devoid of flavor. The sauce selection was underwhelming as well, though the North Carolina sauce was authentic and probably the highlight of the meal.

The waitress was excellent and attentive, I made a reservation and got right in on a fairly busy night. The restaurant interior was pleasant, and I have nothing but compliments to offer on those fronts. I also appreciate that Slow's made an investment in downtown Pontiac.

However, there are countless other places in the Metro Detroit area that do what Slow's does, only with a whole lot more flavor in the food. I'm going to return in a few months and give them another try, because I cannot in good conscience write an establishment off based on one meal. It is my sincere hope that the kitchen opens a box of salt in the meantime and dares to use it for seasoning the food.

My wife and myself decided to finally try Dr.Rolf's Barbecue on Sunday 8/4 around 3 pm since it had good reviews and we heard good recommendations form others. We like to eat at and see local restaurants succeed.

I always check restaurants out when I walk in and sit down.  The place was clean and the patrons seemed to be enjoying the food.  It had an open kitchen so I checked out the line and it was clean and organized.  Unfortunately I saw food code violations that are far to common nowadays at many restaurants. 1.  The cooks with beards had no beard guards on.  Beards are 6 times more likely to have hair fall out than hair on the head.  2. At least one cook was wearing a watch and bracelet.  Health code allows one smooth wedding ring.  3.  The cooks were wearing and changing gloves while handling ready to eat food, but were not washing their hands before putting on new gloves.  Health code states that hands must be washed before putting on new gloves.  When a food-service worker grabs new gloves with dirty hands all the gloves are now contaminated.  Like I said this is not just an issue at Dr. Rolf's, but at many other food service establishments.

We had 2 waitresses do to a change in the shift and both did a good job.  We ordered dirty tots with smoked pork to share between us.  These were very good.  The only thing that should be addressed is the tots having paper underneath. some of the cheese sank to the bottom and stuck to the paper.  It made it hard to scoop the tots out and not tear the paper when serving.

I ordered the southwest salad with smoked chicken.  The price of the added chicken was $2 and that was quite reasonable.  The food came out and presentation was appealing.  I instantly noticed that the avocado looked unripe, and it was hard and unripe when I picked it up.  The chicken looked poached and not smoked.  No smoke color and no smoke smell.  I went back online and looked at the menu to make sure that it was supposed to be a smoked chicken breast.  Yes it was.  The chicken had no smoke flavor.  Otherwise the salad was good.

My wife ordered the salmon salad.  When it came out she said to me it had a very fishy smell.  The salmon also looked poached.  It was supposed to be a roasted smoked  teriyaki salmon.  No color and the smell wash extremely fishy and not smokey.  She tried a small bite of the salmon and it was fishy tasting and bad.  Fresh salmon, regardless of how it is prepared, should never taste fishy.  The waitress was not sure how to handle it at first, but she was OK with my wife ordering a new meal.  She eventually ordered the beet salad and that came out quickly and was very good.

We also tried the cornbread waffle.  This was a great idea and a change from the cornbread muffin that most BBQ joints serve.  It was done well.  The ideas of using it in different desserts seams quite appealing.

We almost always give a restaurant that has not met expectations a second chance, so eventually we will visit Dr. Rolf's Barbecue again.  I hope they take this as constructive criticism, so that when we do visit again we can give a better review.  We want them to succeed as a local establishment.

At first glance, this indicates an inconsistent fry time - possibly two separate batches combined. All told, they look fairly inoffensive.

Beyond a thin veneer of grease, these onion rings had literally no flavor whatsoever. There was no seasoning, a completely bland batter, and even the onions tasted like a mushy, flavorless paste - the type of bland sludge I imagine they would serve on an interstellar voyage in a dystopian future. The best comparison I can make for the taste of these onion rings is a particularly bland variety of cardboard, surrounding a ring of moistened paper.

Even after biking for a few miles, and having worked up something of an appetite in the process, these onion rings did absolutely nothing for me. They provided no flavor, no sustenance, and no joy. I could feel anger building as I tried to shovel them down before wisely abandoning the prospect - though remained intrigued by a food that offered less flavor than a particularly white piece of iceberg lettuce. For the first time in my entire time writing review of onion rings, I was literally unable to finish eating them.

In another feat of onion ring engineering, these onion rings had a texture that was simultaneously overcooked and cold. The batter was much too crunchy, and it felt more like gnawing through a hunk of wood than biting into an onion ring. Though the coloration would suggest not every onion ring would be overcooked, they were. They were also dry, sans the previously mentioned veneer of grease.

I suspect that the overcooking was what led to the complete removal of any sense of flavor from the onion, though there was a hint of texture remaining. Though heated to within an inch of its existence, the onion interior was bizarrely cold. Given the wait time, I had assumed these were made to order, but the only possible explanation I can have for them being freezing and overcooked simultaneously is that they had waited in a bin somewhere for an hour or two before I arrived.

Despite the complete absence of flavor and the almost inedible texture, both which I suspect were brought about by an excessive cook time, I still think these onion rings are a pretty good value. The whole basket was $4.50, an astronomically low price for Mackinac Island - probably equivalent to a $2 thing of frozen, poorly prepared onion rings on the mainland. My high evaluation of the value no doubt partially stems from the absurd prices for other frozen rings back in town.

That said, they were close to inedible, I couldn't bring myself to finish them, and they are a memory best buried.

"Thanks for tipping."

"Thanks for tipping."

I tried to order the 1/4lb Turkey and Brisket Plate, and was curtly told I couldn't order that, despite it being clearly listed on their menu (on the wall right next to the register). Ended up with the 1/2lb version, with southern greens and Cole slaw as sides, and my wife ordered the Carolina pulled pork sandwich. I tried to pay with a Discover card, and the man taking our order nearly rolled his eyes as he handed the card back and said they didn't take Discover, like I was supposed to somehow know that already.
The food was underwhelming as well. My brisket was dried out and tough, and I tasted no smoke, and there was no flavor from any kind of dry rub (bark and smoke ring were absent), so it just tasted like steamed beef. The turkey was more tender and juicier, but also didn't appear seasoned and didn't taste smoked. The coleslaw and greens were unremarkable, and served in very small portions in tiny plastic cups I've only ever gotten at fast food places. My wife's sandwich was also bland, as was her small-portioned side of mac and cheese. Both of us slathered our food in their house BBQ sauces for some flavor, but the sauces themselves were underwhelming; my wife got the Carolina vinegar sauce, and it just tasted like straight vinegar (she lived in Raleigh for two years, and serving that sauce down there would've started a fight).
All told, we spent $30 for food and drinks, which was too much for the quality of food and the total experience. We frequent a brewery (Teay's River) that also does barbecue, and would pay comparable prices for much better food, be able to have a beer, and be at a full-service restaurant.
If you're looking for truly good barbecue, I'd highly recommend going somewhere else.

FOOD POISONING + BAD MANAGERIAL RESPONSE = MILTS

On 12/25/2013 I went to MILTS and wish I never stepped foot in the place. Not only did I have probably the worst food poisoning of my life, but also experienced the worst managerial response.

MILTS was a restaurant that I have always wanted to patron and heard great reviews from. My friend and I stayed in Chi-town during the holidays and decided to eat there for lunch on Christmas day.

I ordered the smoked chicken soup and beef brisket sandwich. The soup tasted like they just added liquid smoke, and not like an hearth smokey flavor. The brisket (where I think I got food poisoning) tasted off and I only ate 1/4 of the sandwich.

I noticed when I got back to the car that I started feeling a bit weird, but wasn't really sure what it was. It wasn't until hours later at the Evanston movie theater when I started feeling hot and nauseous, did I realize it was food poisoning. I actually had to run out of the theater to the bathroom to throw up. Keep in mind that MILTS was the only place I ate all day.

My friend took me home and over the course of the night and wee hours of the morning, I was on my hands and knees vomiting. I ended up getting a mild fever and had horrible diarrhea too.

Finally after I threw up everything in my stomach, did my fever start to subside and feel better. That morning I went to the doctors and got two bags of IV fluid for dehydration.

I thought it was imperative to alert the restaurant so no one else got sick, so I called on 26th. The host stated the general manager will contact me right away regarding the issue. I must say that the host probably was the most customer service focused during this whole ordeal.

The general manager called me the next day (27th) already in a defensive tone asking about what I ate and if I had documentation from my doctor proving it was food poisoning. I am thinking, "Is this place really asking me to submit a doctor's note proving I got food poisoning?" He even contested that you can't get a fever from food poisoning, which you can and symptoms range from diarrhea , nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain and/or cramping, malaise (general uneasiness) and fever. The food at MILTS made me experience all of these symptoms. Does it make sense to anyone to have the customer submit documentation to a restaurant to prove that they got food poisoning? He stated that he could send me a gift card, but wouldn't refund my meal, which is just a complete insult and poor response. Why the hell would I ever want to eat there again. I just want a refund and didn't even ask them to pay for my $119 doctors visit.

The manager said  the owner is out-of-town, but he will escalate the issue to him and follow up with me next week.

I have worked in a variety of food establishments from fine dining to country clubs, and never have I ever experienced as poor a customer service response as I did here. I reported my food poisoning to the Chicago Health Department and hope they follow up on this. I would hate for anyone to get sick and experience what I went through at MILTS.

Our whole experience was, in a word, disappointing. Given the many glowing reviews, we decided to check the place out, but we must've caught them on a bad night or something. Or, as another reviewer noted, Lafayette natives might not really know what good barbecue is if they haven't traveled elsewhere.
The service was at its best cold, and more accurately rude. I tried to order the 1/4lb Turkey and Brisket Plate, and was curtly told I couldn't order that, despite it being clearly listed on their menu (on the wall right next to the register). Ended up with the 1/2lb version, with southern greens and Cole slaw as sides, and my wife ordered the Carolina pulled pork sandwich. I tried to pay with a Discover card, and the man taking our order nearly rolled his eyes as he handed the card back and said they didn't take Discover, like I was supposed to somehow know that already.
The food was underwhelming as well. My brisket was dried out and tough, and I tasted no smoke, and there was no flavor from any kind of dry rub (bark and smoke ring were absent), so it just tasted like steamed beef. The turkey was more tender and juicier, but also didn't appear seasoned and didn't taste smoked. The coleslaw and greens were unremarkable, and served in very small portions in tiny plastic cups I've only ever gotten at fast food places. My wife's sandwich was also bland, as was her small-portioned side of mac and cheese. Both of us slathered our food in their house BBQ sauces for some flavor, but the sauces themselves were underwhelming; my wife got the Carolina vinegar sauce, and it just tasted like straight vinegar (she lived in Raleigh for two years, and serving that sauce down there would've started a fight).
All told, we spent $30 for food and drinks, which was too much for the quality of food and the total experience. We frequent a brewery (Teay's River) that also does barbecue, and would pay comparable prices for much better food, be able to have a beer, and be at a full-service restaurant.
If you're looking for truly good barbecue, I'd highly recommend going somewhere else.

On 12/25/2013 I went to MILTS and wish I never stepped foot in the place. Not only did I have probably the worst food poisoning of my life, but also experienced the worst managerial response.

MILTS was a restaurant that I have always wanted to patron and heard great reviews from. My friend and I stayed in Chi-town during the holidays and decided to eat there for lunch on Christmas day.

I ordered the smoked chicken soup and beef brisket sandwich. The soup tasted like they just added liquid smoke, and not like an hearth smokey flavor. The brisket (where I think I got food poisoning) tasted off and I only ate 1/4 of the sandwich.

I noticed when I got back to the car that I started feeling a bit weird, but wasn't really sure what it was. It wasn't until hours later at the Evanston movie theater when I started feeling hot and nauseous, did I realize it was food poisoning. I actually had to run out of the theater to the bathroom to throw up. Keep in mind that MILTS was the only place I ate all day.

My friend took me home and over the course of the night and wee hours of the morning, I was on my hands and knees vomiting. I ended up getting a mild fever and had horrible diarrhea too.

Finally after I threw up everything in my stomach, did my fever start to subside and feel better. That morning I went to the doctors and got two bags of IV fluid for dehydration.

I thought it was imperative to alert the restaurant so no one else got sick, so I called on 26th. The host stated the general manager will contact me right away regarding the issue. I must say that the host probably was the most customer service focused during this whole ordeal.

The general manager called me the next day (27th) already in a defensive tone asking about what I ate and if I had documentation from my doctor proving it was food poisoning. I am thinking, "Is this place really asking me to submit a doctor's note proving I got food poisoning?" He even contested that you can't get a fever from food poisoning, which you can and symptoms range from diarrhea , nausea and vomiting, abdominal pain and/or cramping, malaise (general uneasiness) and fever. The food at MILTS made me experience all of these symptoms. Does it make sense to anyone to have the customer submit documentation to a restaurant to prove that they got food poisoning? He stated that he could send me a gift card, but wouldn't refund my meal, which is just a complete insult and poor response. Why the hell would I ever want to eat there again. I just want a refund and didn't even ask them to pay for my $119 doctors visit.

The manager said  the owner is out-of-town, but he will escalate the issue to him and follow up with me next week.

I have worked in a variety of food establishments from fine dining to country clubs, and never have I ever experienced as poor a customer service response as I did here. I reported my food poisoning to the Chicago Health Department and hope they follow up on this. I would hate for anyone to get sick and experience what I went through at MILTS.

In a first (so far) for the island, these onion rings are *not* the exact same frozen mishmash from Brew City. They are served in a brown patterned cardboard container - a slight cut above from plain coloration - though without the near-ubiquitous wax paper beneath. They are served in a large pile bulging out from the container.

Though I suspect the onion rings may still be frozen, they're enough variation in the batter to make me doubt it - as cracks and crevices are mottled throughout the rings. The rings are also inconsistently sized - and varying in color from a pale golden brown to a darkened copper. At first glance, this indicates an inconsistent fry time - possibly two separate batches combined. All told, they look fairly inoffensive.

Beyond a thin veneer of grease, these onion rings had literally no flavor whatsoever. There was no seasoning, a completely bland batter, and even the onions tasted like a mushy, flavorless paste - the type of bland sludge I imagine they would serve on an interstellar voyage in a dystopian future. The best comparison I can make for the taste of these onion rings is a particularly bland variety of cardboard, surrounding a ring of moistened paper.

Even after biking for a few miles, and having worked up something of an appetite in the process, these onion rings did absolutely nothing for me. They provided no flavor, no sustenance, and no joy. I could feel anger building as I tried to shovel them down before wisely abandoning the prospect - though remained intrigued by a food that offered less flavor than a particularly white piece of iceberg lettuce. For the first time in my entire time writing review of onion rings, I was literally unable to finish eating them.

In another feat of onion ring engineering, these onion rings had a texture that was simultaneously overcooked and cold. The batter was much too crunchy, and it felt more like gnawing through a hunk of wood than biting into an onion ring. Though the coloration would suggest not every onion ring would be overcooked, they were. They were also dry, sans the previously mentioned veneer of grease.

I suspect that the overcooking was what led to the complete removal of any sense of flavor from the onion, though there was a hint of texture remaining. Though heated to within an inch of its existence, the onion interior was bizarrely cold. Given the wait time, I had assumed these were made to order, but the only possible explanation I can have for them being freezing and overcooked simultaneously is that they had waited in a bin somewhere for an hour or two before I arrived.

Despite the complete absence of flavor and the almost inedible texture, both which I suspect were brought about by an excessive cook time, I still think these onion rings are a pretty good value. The whole basket was $4.50, an astronomically low price for Mackinac Island - probably equivalent to a $2 thing of frozen, poorly prepared onion rings on the mainland. My high evaluation of the value no doubt partially stems from the absurd prices for other frozen rings back in town.

That said, they were close to inedible, I couldn't bring myself to finish them, and they are a memory best buried.

I immediately called Jeremy, our server, back and explained our dilemma, and his response was that the restaurant keeps the desserts frozen so they don't go bad or get stale. So be it. But they do need to be thawed before served--Cooking 101. I insisted he take it back to the cook and have him solve the problem....Guess what, the kitchen staff sent it back whole with a steak knife! Again, not to spoil our lunch, I laughed it off and my two guests "thawed" the pie with their hot tea cups! Jeremy shortly thereafter delivered our checks, and I wanted the one with the dessert since it was my idea. Without asking, he divided the cost of the pie by 3 and charged each of us our share. I was mortified! He did not ask nor have I ever seen this done. A good restaurant needs to have good food and a staff that does what it can to make the meal a pleasant, satisfying experience. My last two were not and it was the staff's fault. Thaw your desserts before serving them. Check with your customer before making billing decisions.

I just want to start off by saying that the food was okay, the service was excellent, and the restaurant itself is comfortable and extremely nice. But I do not recommend spending between $60 and $80 for a meal (for 2) here when you could spend less and get something more tasty somewhere else.

There are two sides to the restaurant. There's a family style seating where you order at the register, and the other side of the restaurant is traditional table service. We sat at the table service side of the restaurant and let me tell you the service was excellent. Our waitresses were extremely friendly and prompt. The restaurant is very clean and our table was comfortable as far as seating, with pleasing views from the large windows. Once seated, we were given a pitcher of room temperature water and two highball glasses to drink with. That was a little odd, and also not very enjoyable. I don't know many people who don't like their water to be cold. Their tap selection was good and the mixed drinks sounded delicious.

For the starters we tried the chicken wings and the cornbread balls. You get five of the cornbread balls, they are smaller and they are sticky cuz they're covered with honey but they are delicious. You get four of the Wings, which are also delicious. I have to honestly say that the appetizers were actually better than our meal. Especially with their signature sauces which we sampled with our appetizers and let me tell you they are delicious. I tried every single one and loved every single one.

As for our meal, that was disappointing. I got the brisket which was extremely fatty but you can't really complain too much about that as brisket can tend to be fatty. I wish I would have gotten the pork butt, as I sampled that off of my boyfriend's plate and it was delicious. As for the sides that you get with your meal...wow that was so disappointing. The mac and cheese is right on the edge of overcooked and covered in a packaged cheese sauce with crushed-up Cheez-Its sprinkled on top. First let me say that it is very disappointing that this opportunity for a signature roux for the macaroni that would compliment the meat at this restaurant has been missed. And I would recommend that if they're going to crush Cheez-Its and put it on top of the macaroni and cheese, they should not be stale. But just in general please ditch the Cheez-Its and make a roux. The coleslaw was also disappointing. The sauce covering the slaw was kind of watery and low in flavor; though I do have to say the Cabbage was very fresh and crisp. The white beans, well that was just Bland. On your platter they put a piece of white bread, a couple of onion slices, and a couple of pickle slices. Not impressive, and not very tasty. The pickles aren't even what I would consider Deli pickles or quality. They look like something off of a Big Mac. Coleslaw was atrocious. It had hardly any flavor at all besides straight cabbage and vinegar.
