I will preface this review by saying, I am not fussy when it comes to BBQ or restaurants with good food. That being said, there were too many things wrong with my experience here to not write this review. First the good, my pulled pork sandwich with the table BBQ sauce was delicious (that is why I gave it two stars.) It was very tender and well done. Now the bad. We entered the place through the North entrance (where the parking lot is,) This was after we had to walk past the tattered clothed and filthy kitchen staff, smoking and complaining about how busy it was. Once inside, we stumbled upon the ordering station, and when we were ready to order, the curly haired young lady was too busy paying attention to her friends/co-workers who were behind the bar (clearly not on shift) to enter our order correctly without me repeating my selections, several times. We took a seat at a table, that was thankfully clean and waited. While waiting, we witnessed a large party of diners that had entered through the south entrance (the entrance that would have the most foot traffic from tourists walking the strip and the entrance that has only handicap parking spaces) stand around confused and waiting for a hostess or waitress to direct them on how to be seated or where to order. Once they figured it out for themselves, they proceeded to place several orders for one table. We even witnessed them getting all their drinks, group by group themselves, from the bar. Our food then came out in a timely manner from a clearly overworked young man who was very concerned about our meal and overall dining experience. As mentioned above, the pulled pork sandwich was delicious, however, not much else was. I ordered the spicy creamed corn and an additional side of baked beans, while my wife ordered the mac and cheese and a side of fries. I'm going to blunt here for the sake of brevity. The mac and cheese was flavorless, the beans had a mystery ingredient (I suspect the Tabasco Sriracha that was on every table and bar space and shelf) that made them very salty/spicy, but not in a good way and the "spicy" creamed corn was not spicy, but was in fact burned and soupy. I did not finish either. The fries had clearly been cooked in old oil and were little more than food service, frozen bagged fries. One last thing, the "mustard" BBQ sauce that is table side is little more than yellow table mustard with some other "flavors." Very poor showing for the Carolina sauce. I realize  this review might be in stark contrast to the others here, but I say again, I am very tolerant of a restaurant, as long as they get a couple things right. Unfortunately, the pulled pork was the only thing right, everything else was confusingly wrong. This may be a classic example of someone who knows how to cook in a restaurant, but knows nothing about running one. I've had BBQ all the country, this isn't one of the places I'll be returning to. BTW the kitchen staff was still outside complaining, smoking and laying in the parking, by the dumpster, when we left.

Another place lowering my confidence in Michigan's ability to produce actual BBQ and smoked meats. This type of establishment seems to be the latest fad pushing itself up, over the last few years: promises authenticity, puts unseasoned meat in a smoker, serves comfort foods on paper-covered trays, dumps sweet sauces on the table. The website says "Real Southern-Style BBQ In Lansing, Michigan", so we ordered just about one of everything. 6PM, restaurant's empty; food takes 30 minutes to arrive. Pulled pork: bland, mostly fat, but at least not dry. Brining and dry-rubbing is mandatory; your sauces shouldn't carry you. Brisket: it's pot roast. Zero flavor. I could've sworn it wasn't smoked, and I had to cover it in sauce to taste anything. It was tender. Pulled chicken: at least it was different. It had a different flavor, but it was vague and minimal - sauce required. Sausage: you probably didn't make these in your kitchen, but they had a typical sausage flavor; Nothing amazing, but nothing to complain about, but nothing to comment about. Your chicken wings had an interesting rub, with spice and sweetness, and they were cooked well. Were they smoked? I'm not sure, but the meat inside the fried exterior was bland. Ribs: chewy, which isn't my thing; sauce to the rescue. I'm not sure if it's a regional thing, shooting for chewy over fall-off-the-bone, but it's not working for me. Crack Mac: noodles in Velveeta with bacon crumbles. Very very lazy, but I'm sure people like it. Real mac and cheese is made with a roux, not melting semisolid blocks of food-scienced American cheese, but no one's going to complain about bacon... Fries: battered, seasoned, and cooked well. I liked these quite a bit. Everything else was unremarkable; forgettable. Oh, except for the surprising lack of beer, which probably contributes to the place being empty. I don't know why you've chosen to do what you're doing; you have almost 200 people contributing to a 4.5 star rating on what I consider to be a pretty mediocre production of what you consider to be BBQ. I don't think it's too much to ask that you brine your meats for at least 24 hours in a basic brine: equal parts sugar, salt, and vinegar. You rely too heavily on sauces to provide flavor instead of using a rub and smoke profile to get the flavor you want. Sure, it's more work and expense, and you could probably continue to take advantage of a population that doesn't know BBQ beyond an over-sweetened sauce they baste their food in, but it's so easy to do right and only a matter of time until everyone moves on. It's so easy to do that I placed my own smoking meat on hold, went to your place, experienced the above, went back to my place, pulled the meat out of the smoker, and fed everyone. I'm probably not coming back because you're like every other place in Lansing (even though you're actually in Grand Ledge).

Just because you have a pit master building your smoker or winning an award for bbq does not mean your bbq competes with the best of the best outside of what particular fest they may be showcasing their bbq. But the most important thing, the BBQ, in my humble opinion was a total bust.  I ordered the brisket.  This is not an easy thing to make and harder to perfect, but beef is a strong flavor and it doesnt need much help.  I'm not sure how they prepared it but it involved flavor removing.  It tasted more like a pot roast than a brisket, no smoke flavor to speak of.  A good brisket is cut against the grain, the fat is rendered and juicy and you have a good tug that just pulls apart.  This brisket was mushy and tasteless, and without guessing that it sat in a vat of juice in an attempt to keep it from drying out, I couldnt tell you why it tasted the way it did. Let's start with the watermelon salad. First, google watermelon salad if you haven't had one before. I included a picture in my review from my search. Notice how none of these images include four unwieldly giant wedges of watermelon sprinkled with nuts, pickled jalapenos,  and parsley. I will admit the flavor was delicious, but the presentation was terrible and the small bbq platter style tray it came out on made it impractical to cut and eat properly. I'm not sure if the chef meant for it to be picked up and have the nuts all fall in your lap, but I digress. I felt awful getting watermelon and nuts all over their floor and table as I attempted to eat this deconstructed salad.

We ordered the spoon bread with hot honey, which were admittedly delicious and was the shining, but corny star of our night at Station. The other sides were nothing but disappointments. The mac and cheese was cold, dry, and the sauce was quite tasteless. There were some kind of corn chips sprinkled over the mac, but they had obviously been there a while because they lacked any crunch. Next up, the coleslaw which is described as creamy on the menu. Creamy, it is, and the sauce was tasty. However, the shredded cabbage was swimming in sauce and since it wasn't diced it was almost as unwieldy to eat as the watermelon slices.

To sum up the meats that we ordered:

Brisket: B+ not the best, not the worst. I wish we would've asked for a fattier piece, but that's our fault.

Sausage: I would give it a D personally, but we are not Cincinnati natives. It was heavily spiced with cinnamon, so something like this would probably appeal to a Cincinnatian that also enjoys Skyline/goetta.

Pulled Pork: B, The meat was moist but lacked in flavor. Obviously the meat was not well seasoned before it was smoked.

As for the sauces, they were unmemorable and generic for their styles. This would be fine if the meat was better seasoned.

We ordered one drink, it was delicious.

I think that there are a lot of easy fixes to make Station a restaurant that I would return to. However, at this point I could not recommend it to someone.

Let's start with the watermelon salad. First, google watermelon salad if you haven't had one before. I included a picture in my review from my search. Notice how none of these images include four unwieldly giant wedges of watermelon sprinkled with nuts, pickled jalapenos,  and parsley. I will admit the flavor was delicious, but the presentation was terrible and the small bbq platter style tray it came out on made it impractical to cut and eat properly. I'm not sure if the chef meant for it to be picked up and have the nuts all fall in your lap, but I digress. I felt awful getting watermelon and nuts all over their floor and table as I attempted to eat this deconstructed salad.

We ordered the spoon bread with hot honey, which were admittedly delicious and was the shining, but corny star of our night at Station. The other sides were nothing but disappointments. The mac and cheese was cold, dry, and the sauce was quite tasteless. There were some kind of corn chips sprinkled over the mac, but they had obviously been there a while because they lacked any crunch. Next up, the coleslaw which is described as creamy on the menu. Creamy, it is, and the sauce was tasty. However, the shredded cabbage was swimming in sauce and since it wasn't diced it was almost as unwieldy to eat as the watermelon slices.

To sum up the meats that we ordered:

Brisket: B+ not the best, not the worst. I wish we would've asked for a fattier piece, but that's our fault.

Sausage: I would give it a D personally, but we are not Cincinnati natives. It was heavily spiced with cinnamon, so something like this would probably appeal to a Cincinnatian that also enjoys Skyline/goetta.

Pulled Pork: B, The meat was moist but lacked in flavor. Obviously the meat was not well seasoned before it was smoked.

As for the sauces, they were unmemorable and generic for their styles. This would be fine if the meat was better seasoned.

We ordered one drink, it was delicious.

I think that there are a lot of easy fixes to make Station a restaurant that I would return to. However, at this point I could not recommend it to someone.

Ok, so we placed a large order with them, and got several items:
(12) Chicken Wings x 1
Kids - Chicken Nuggets
1, Large - Mac & Cheese
1, Small Rib Tips - 1/2 Lb
1, Slab x 1
Appetizer: Onion Rings x 1
Appetizer: Fresh-Cut Fries x 1
Burger - Single x 1
Specialty Single Burger: Mushroom & Swiss x 1

In order as above:
The Chicken Wings (Teriyaki) were, in fact, the best thing we ordered. They were quite good, really enjoyed them.

They were out of nuggets for the kids meal, so we had to replace it with a cheeseburger. So both kids ended up with a burger, which is fine, except that neither finished them, saying that they were too dry.

The mac & cheese was quite cheesy, and indeed "creamy", but it was EXTREMELY over-peppered (black pepper). So much so, that it was almost the only thing you could taste, like they're trying to disguise the flavor of mac & cheese with the pepper.

We ORDERED a full slab of ribs, of which they were out of. So we ended up with the rib tips. The rib tips were "good", but were a little dry, as though from being over-cooked or having been sitting on the warmer for too long.

The onion rings were quite good, very much enjoyed them. However, it wasn't like they had a "signature" taste. They were just beer-battered onion rings, no different than if you got them from anywhere else. Enjoyable, but standard.

The fries were very much like the fries you would get from Rally's. If you like those fries, you'll like these. Otherwise, they're just "meh".

I was really looking forward to the mushroom and swiss burger, and ordered extra swiss with it. Well, the extra swiss wasn't on it, which isn't a "huge" issue, but the burger was very disappointing. Like the burgers we ended up with for the kids, the patty was a good size (awesome) but it was dry, and not really "full" of flavor. The sandwich itself was also dry because the mushrooms & sauce was completely devoid of the sauce, and the mushrooms themselves were dry.

Ok, so we placed a large order with them, and got several items:
(12) Chicken Wings x 1
Kids - Chicken Nuggets
1, Large - Mac & Cheese
1, Small Rib Tips - 1/2 Lb
1, Slab x 1
Appetizer: Onion Rings x 1
Appetizer: Fresh-Cut Fries x 1
Burger - Single x 1
Specialty Single Burger: Mushroom & Swiss x 1

In order as above:
The Chicken Wings (Teriyaki) were, in fact, the best thing we ordered. They were quite good, really enjoyed them.

They were out of nuggets for the kids meal, so we had to replace it with a cheeseburger. So both kids ended up with a burger, which is fine, except that neither finished them, saying that they were too dry.

The mac & cheese was quite cheesy, and indeed "creamy", but it was EXTREMELY over-peppered (black pepper). So much so, that it was almost the only thing you could taste, like they're trying to disguise the flavor of mac & cheese with the pepper.

We ORDERED a full slab of ribs, of which they were out of. So we ended up with the rib tips. The rib tips were "good", but were a little dry, as though from being over-cooked or having been sitting on the warmer for too long.

The onion rings were quite good, very much enjoyed them. However, it wasn't like they had a "signature" taste. They were just beer-battered onion rings, no different than if you got them from anywhere else. Enjoyable, but standard.

The fries were very much like the fries you would get from Rally's. If you like those fries, you'll like these. Otherwise, they're just "meh".

I was really looking forward to the mushroom and swiss burger, and ordered extra swiss with it. Well, the extra swiss wasn't on it, which isn't a "huge" issue, but the burger was very disappointing. Like the burgers we ended up with for the kids, the patty was a good size (awesome) but it was dry, and not really "full" of flavor. The sandwich itself was also dry because the mushrooms & sauce was completely devoid of the sauce, and the mushrooms themselves were dry.

We got their "mixed" BBQ sauce for the rib tips, which is apparently only mixed with "Hot" and "Hotter". I'm Ok with "hot", I love a really good-flavored, hot, BBQ sauce. But that's all this BBQ sauce WAS: Hot. Entirely missing the other component: Flavor. Their was no real "flavor" to it, making it similar to something like pepper-spray that's been reduced to half-strength, with no enjoyable flavor to go with it.

*IF* we order again, the only thing we WOULD be ordering are the wings, and maybe the onion rings to go with them. The teriyaki wings really were delicious.

Maybe it was an "off-night" for them, or maybe this is how they always are, but we've marked them off our list for BBQ places.

Another place lowering my confidence in Michigan's ability to produce actual BBQ and smoked meats. This type of establishment seems to be the latest fad pushing itself up, over the last few years: promises authenticity, puts unseasoned meat in a smoker, serves comfort foods on paper-covered trays, dumps sweet sauces on the table. The website says "Real Southern-Style BBQ In Lansing, Michigan", so we ordered just about one of everything. 6PM, restaurant's empty; food takes 30 minutes to arrive. Pulled pork: bland, mostly fat, but at least not dry. Brining and dry-rubbing is mandatory; your sauces shouldn't carry you. Brisket: it's pot roast. Zero flavor. I could've sworn it wasn't smoked, and I had to cover it in sauce to taste anything. It was tender. Pulled chicken: at least it was different. It had a different flavor, but it was vague and minimal - sauce required. Sausage: you probably didn't make these in your kitchen, but they had a typical sausage flavor; Nothing amazing, but nothing to complain about, but nothing to comment about. Your chicken wings had an interesting rub, with spice and sweetness, and they were cooked well. Were they smoked? I'm not sure, but the meat inside the fried exterior was bland. Ribs: chewy, which isn't my thing; sauce to the rescue. I'm not sure if it's a regional thing, shooting for chewy over fall-off-the-bone, but it's not working for me. Crack Mac: noodles in Velveeta with bacon crumbles. Very very lazy, but I'm sure people like it. Real mac and cheese is made with a roux, not melting semisolid blocks of food-scienced American cheese, but no one's going to complain about bacon... Fries: battered, seasoned, and cooked well. I liked these quite a bit. Everything else was unremarkable; forgettable. Oh, except for the surprising lack of beer, which probably contributes to the place being empty. I don't know why you've chosen to do what you're doing; you have almost 200 people contributing to a 4.5 star rating on what I consider to be a pretty mediocre production of what you consider to be BBQ. I don't think it's too much to ask that you brine your meats for at least 24 hours in a basic brine: equal parts sugar, salt, and vinegar. You rely too heavily on sauces to provide flavor instead of using a rub and smoke profile to get the flavor you want. Sure, it's more work and expense, and you could probably continue to take advantage of a population that doesn't know BBQ beyond an over-sweetened sauce they baste their food in, but it's so easy to do right and only a matter of time until everyone moves on. It's so easy to do that I placed my own smoking meat on hold, went to your place, experienced the above, went back to my place, pulled the meat out of the smoker, and fed everyone. I'm probably not coming back because you're like every other place in Lansing (even though you're actually in Grand Ledge).

I truly hate leaving negative reviews but sometimes experiences are simply so bad it just feels necessary. My husband and I are BBQ connoisseurs. We generally have to drive 2 hours to get amazing BBQ or spend multiple days making it ourselves. Unfortunately, that still holds true with Texas Beef and Cattle Company. We had heard mostly good things and decided to give it a try one night. I truly hope it was just an off day but we had a very bad experience. We did arrive late in the evening and as we expected several items we were interested in were sold out. But what we did end up getting was terribly disappointing. We placed a large carryout order (about $130 worth of food for a party) with meat by the pound and some sides. The Tater Salad and Cole Slaw was sadly just bland and had too much vinegar. A let down but not a deal breaker as we really just came for the meat! And boy was that meat a true disappointment. The pulled pork and brisket was very very dry, had barely any flavor or smokiness. The Beef Rib was very very tough with barely any meat on the bone. I've had Beef Rib many times and this was just an improper cook. We also decided to try a whole pasture chicken since they were out of St Louis and Baby Back Ribs that night. We brought it home and even heated it up once we arrived with our take out order and the chicken was raw around the thigh and drum bones, and slightly undercooked in the thickest portion of the breast. I've worked in the food safety industry, this is absolutely unacceptable. $22 for an undercooked whole chicken! I generally try places 2 or 3 times before making a final decision and writing it off permanently... but serving raw chicken is unforgivable. Hopefully others will never experience this but please beware of the possibility. I do hope this place can succeed, it has a great premise and the owner was incredibly nice when we met him but my family and I will not be returning.

I truly hate leaving negative reviews but sometimes experiences are simply so bad it just feels necessary. My husband and I are BBQ connoisseurs. There's truly no good authentic BBQ anywhere around Dayton, we've tried every single place. Its generally poor quality meat that is overcooked, improper cooking or smoking, or smothered in sauce to cover up bad technique. We generally have to drive 2 hours to get amazing BBQ or spend multiple days making it ourselves. Unfortunately, that still holds true with Texas Beef and Cattle Company. We had heard mostly good things and decided to give it a try one night. I truly hope it was just an off day but we had a very bad experience. We did arrive late in the evening and as we expected several items we were interested in were sold out. But what we did end up getting was terribly disappointing. We placed a large carryout order (about $130 worth of food for a party) with meat by the pound and some sides. The Tater Salad and Cole Slaw was sadly just bland and had too much vinegar. A let down but not a deal breaker as we really just came for the meat! And boy was that meat a true disappointment. The pulled pork and brisket was very very dry, had barely any flavor or smokiness. The Beef Rib was very very tough with barely any meat on the bone. I've had Beef Rib many times and this was just an improper cook. We also decided to try a whole pasture chicken since they were out of St Louis and Baby Back Ribs that night. We brought it home and even heated it up once we arrived with our take out order and the chicken was raw around the thigh and drum bones, and slightly undercooked in the thickest portion of the breast. I've worked in the food safety industry, this is absolutely unacceptable. $22 for an undercooked whole chicken! I generally try places 2 or 3 times before making a final decision and writing it off permanently... but serving raw chicken is unforgivable. Hopefully others will never experience this but please beware of the possibility. I do hope this place can succeed, it has a great premise and the owner was incredibly nice when we met him but my family and I will not be returning.
